papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Reinforcement Learning for Edge Offloading in AGI-MEC Systems
papers.abstract: Air–ground integrated mobile edge computing (AGI-MEC) integrates aerial and terrestrial resources to provide efficient computing services for massive mobile terminals (MTs), enabling 6 G network intelligence. However, jointly optimizing offloading and power control remains challenging due to dynamic channels, resource constraints, communication overhead, and privacy concerns. To address these issues, this paper proposes a clustering-based two-layer federated deep reinforcement learning (CTL-FDRL) algorithm. A clustered federated training framework with parameter sharing is first developed, in which raw data exchange is replaced by periodic model aggregation, enabling MTs to learn offloading policies locally while preserving privacy. Furthermore, an efficient representative MT selection method is introduced. A self-organizing map (SOM)-based MT clustering method is designed to adaptively group MTs without a predefined number of clusters. Guided by the derived convergence bound, representative selection within each cluster is posed as a linear programming problem. The resulting representatives are used for federated aggregation, which reduces communication overhead without degrading model performance. Simulation results verify the superiority of CTL-FDRL, achieving about 28.7% higher cumulative reward, 31.5% lower delay, and 18.3% lower energy consumption compared with baseline algorithms.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: FedMIF: Fast-Generalization Image Fusion Via Task-Customized Nodes Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Image fusion is a common approach to enhancing image quality by combining the strengths of multi-modal visual signals, thereby improving the performance of computer vision tasks. However, privacy concerns regarding raw images leave data from multiple domains and clients isolated, preventing centralized training of a universal image fusion model. Federated learning (FL) is a distributed framework that enables collaborative model training by aggregating parameters from multiple nodes without sharing raw data, offering a privacy-preserving solution for lightweight and generalizable models. In this paper, we propose thefederatedmulti-modalimagefusion (FedMIF), a general multi-modal image fusion solution across multiple domains that operates without raw data sharing. We notice existing FL methods lack task-specific strategies tailored for general fusion tasks, leading to suboptimal fusion performance. To address this, we propose a four-stage framework that enhances detail features while maintaining overall visual quality, which are 1) Server initialization stage, dual decoders are trained on natural data to regulate feature distribution. 2) Task-agnostic stage, all clients collaboratively train the encoder to improve feature extraction performance. 3) Task-specific stage, training is conducted within relevant tasks to address the negative impact of inconsistent optimization objectives across different tasks. 4) Local-specific stage, local adapters are trained on each client to help mitigate detail loss resulting from model aggregation. Complete subjective and objective comparisons prove that FedMIF could generate information-rich fusion results on four fusion tasks while requiring less communication overhead. Our code is available at:https://github.com/suweijian1996/FedMIF.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Federated Continual Learning Framework for Dynamic and Heterogeneous IoV
papers.abstract: Traditional federated learning (FL) architectures face challenges in handling heterogeneous data and dynamic tasks, often resulting in catastrophic forgetting when new training tasks are continuously introduced. Federated continual learning (FCL) integrates the privacy-preserving capabilities of FL with the knowledge retention and incremental update mechanisms of continual learning, effectively mitigating catastrophic forgetting and protecting user privacy. However, existing FCL solutions largely overlook the unique requirements of Internet of Vehicles (IoV) scenarios, such as data heterogeneity and dynamic task management. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework, hierarchical federated continual learning (Hier-FCL), which incorporates local continual learning via optimized experience replay and meta-knowledge distillation, along with dynamic client clustering to tackle data heterogeneity. Additionally, a hierarchical aggregation mechanism is employed to enhance scalability and adaptability in diverse IoV scenarios. Experiments conducted in mixed-task environments using multiple datasets demonstrate that Hier-FCL outperforms baseline algorithms in terms of retained accuracy and backward transfer impact, validating its effectiveness in mitigating catastrophic forgetting and managing heterogeneous client data.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems

papers.title: Diameter-Constrained Topology Orchestration for Communication-Convergence Tradeoffs in Decentralized Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Decentralized federated learning (DFL) is pivotal for the integration of AI and communication in 6G, facilitating distributed edge-network learning without centralized coordination. However, existing DFL frameworks suffer from prohibitive communication overhead and slow convergence, with a critical issue being the difficulty of balancing the tradeoffs between communication efficiency and convergence rates. This paper proposes a novel distributed synchronization topology orchestration method for DFL that leverages the diameter of the communication graph as a tunable parameter to optimize this communication-convergence tradeoff. Our key insight stems from the relationship between the topology diameter and the spectral radius of the consensus matrix, i.e., constraining the diameter reduces the spectral radius, thereby accelerating convergence while minimizing communication costs. Specifically, we formulate the synchronization topology design as a diameter-constrained minimum spanning tree (MST) problem, where the diameter serves as an adjustable parameter to balance the tradeoff. To ensure robustness in dynamic networks, we further devise a distributed adaptation mechanism that maintains the diameterconstrained MST despite node/link failures. Experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset demonstrate that our method achieves accuracy comparable to fully connected topologies while reducing communication costs by 25% and accelerating convergence by 28% against state-of-the-art benchmarks.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Integrated Cloud-Edge-SAGIN Framework for Multi-UAV Assisted Traffic Offloading Based on Hierarchical Federated Learning
papers.abstract: The growing number of mobile devices used by terrestrial users has significantly amplified the traffic load on cellular networks. Especially in urban environments, the high traffic demand brought about by dense user populations has bottlenecked network resources. The Space-Air-Ground-Integrated Network (SAGIN) provides a new solution to cope with this demand, enhancing data transmission efficiency through a multi-layered network structure. However, the heterogeneous and dynamic nature of SAGIN also poses significant management and resource allocation challenges. In this paper, we propose a cloud-edge-SAGIN framework for multi-UAV assisted traffic offloading based on Hierarchical Federated Learning (HFL), aiming to improve the traffic offloading ratio while optimizing the offloading resource allocation. HFL is used instead of traditional Federated Learning (FL) to solve problems such as irrational resource allocation due to heterogeneity in SAGIN. Specifically, the framework applies a hierarchical federated average algorithm and sets a reward function at the ground level, aiming to obtain better model parameters, improve model accuracy at aggregation, enhance UAV traffic offloading ratio, and optimize its scheduling and resource allocation. In addition, an improved Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithm TD3-A4C is designed in this paper to assist UAVs in realizing intelligent decision-making, reducing communication latency, and further improving resource utilization efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework and algorithms display superior performance across all dimensions and offer robust support for the comprehensive investigation of intelligent traffic offloading networks.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: Agentic AI-Driven Federated Feature Distillation for Adaptive Resource–Performance Tradeoffs in Wireless Edge Networks
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: E-DIM: Federated Learning-Based Secure Autonomous Communication Through Enhanced Data Integrity Monitoring
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems

papers.title: Beyond LDP-FL: Independent Uplink–Downlink Privacy Protection in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) has emerged as a key distributed intelligence paradigm in modern computer networks, enabling model training across massive edge devices without exposing raw data. Nevertheless, the nature of FL — continuous sharing of local model updates — may result in privacy exposures over network interactions. To address this limitation, Local Differential Privacy Federated Learning (LDP-FL), a variant that strengthens privacy by injecting noise on each client, was proposed. However, the noise accumulates in the model through the two-phase indivisible sequential process of LDP, thereby bringing the well-recognized privacy-utility trade-off challenge. In this paper, to investigate whether the LDP framework has achieved a favorable trade-off, we propose an ideal interaction mode, Ideal Differential Privacy Federated Learning (IDP-FL), which allows for independent protection in the uplink and downlink phases. Through a comparative analysis of noise accumulation in IDP-FL and LDP-FL, we discover and theoretically prove that LDP-FL suffers from inherent noise redundancy, i.e. noise accumulation in uplink exceeds privacy requirements in downlink. To avoid this defect, we propose a novel framework, Noise Annihilation Differential Privacy Federated Learning (NADP-FL), which can be regarded as an instantiation of IDP-FL. In this framework, a portion of noises are distributedly generated in pairs, thereby mutually canceling each other out during aggregation and not appearing in the downlink phase. As a result, NADP realizes independent protection for both phases, eliminating unnecessary noise accumulation, achieving a more favorable privacy-utility trade-off and enhance protection in a way that incurs theoretically no further utility loss. We validate the superior utility, scalability and robustness of our framework through extensive experiments.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Dynamic Regret for Byzantine-Robust Online Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning enables decentralized model training across multiple clients without exchanging raw data, making it a crucial paradigm for privacy-preserving machine learning. However, its deployment in adversarial and dynamic environments remains fundamentally challenging, particularly under Byzantine attacks. Existing online Byzantine-robust methods face two critical limitations: (i) a strong reliance on the Independent and Identically Distributed (IID) assumption to achieve sublinear regret, and (ii) an inability to adapt to non-stationary environments due to their reliance on static regret metrics. These challenges substantially limit their applicability in practical federated learning scenarios characterized by heterogeneity and non-stationarity. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Byzantine-robust online algorithm, BR-OMGD, which performs multiple local gradient descent updates and incorporates a robust aggregation mechanism to mitigate adversarial effects under the weak growth condition. The algorithm achieves a nearoptimal dynamic regret bound of$O(S* T )$without requiring IID assumptions, where$S* T$denotes the squared path-length. When the online problem reduces to the offline case, BR-OMGD further guarantees exact linear convergence under strong convexity, smoothness, and the weak growth condition, even in the presence of data heterogeneity and Byzantine adversaries. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result establishing such convergence guarantees under these conditions. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets (MNIST, CIFAR-100) demonstrate the proposed algorithms practical effectiveness, showing improved robustness and lower dynamic regret under Byzantine attacks.

papers.title: FedSSV: Client Contribution for Secure Federated Learning Aggregation Using Scaled Shapley Values
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training on data distributed across multiple clients without sharing raw data, thus preserving privacy in sensitive applications such as healthcare. Due to its multi-agent setting, FL can be vulnerable to adversarial attacks in which malicious clients send corrupted models to manipulate the global model, leading to degraded performance and compromised outcomes in safety-critical domains such as healthcare. A robust aggregation framework that evaluates and weights client updates is necessary to mitigate such attacks. In this work, we propose FedSSV, a robust aggregation framework that enhances the security and performance of FL settings by leveraging Shapley values, a game-theoretical approach, to assess each client's impact on the global model. FedSSV dynamically scales client updates based on their evaluated contributions, reducing the influence of malicious or adversarial clients. Extensive experimental results validate FedSSV's effectiveness in mitigating diverse poisoning attack types (e.g., scaling, Gaussian, and sign flipping attacks) across various applications. Experimental results show that FedSSV maintains stable prediction accuracy under both IID and non-IID data settings. For example, it achieves 90% accuracy on Fashion MNIST (FMNIST) and 65% on CIFAR-10 under scaling attacks with 20% malicious clients, while baseline methods experience significant drops.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Programmable In-Network Aggregation for Communication-Aware Federated Learning in 5G RANs
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without sharing raw data, making it attractive for privacy-preserving applications at the wireless edge. However, when executed over real 5G networks, FL performance degrades due to uplink congestion, heterogeneous client capabilities, and intermittent connectivity. Most existing approaches attempt to mitigate these issues indirectly by optimizing clients (through adaptive participation, local training, or selection strategies) or by optimizing models (via pruning, quantization, or compression), but they ignore potential network bottlenecks. This paper introduces FLAG, an FL architecture that embeds innetwork aggregation directly into 5G gNodeBs, transforming the network into an active participant in the learning process. In particular, FLAG performs parameter aggregation at line rate within the 5G Service Data Adaptation Protocol layer and incorporates three mechanisms: Partial-Contribution Correction for loss-tolerant averaging, a timer-driven pipeline for real-time scheduling, and a deadline-based grouping strategy to mitigate stragglers. Experiments with realistic wireless emulation show that FLAG achieves up to 5.1× faster time-to-accuracy and maintains accuracy within 0.8% of a loss-free baseline, while reducing gNB-to-server bandwidth by aggregating pergNB rather than per-client. FLAG requires no modifications to clients or the parameter server, demonstrating how 5G-aware system design can make federated learning scalable, efficient, and resilient under real-world wireless conditions.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: FedAdapt: Unsupervised Federated Domain Adaptation for Cross-Satellite Hyperspectral Image Classification
papers.abstract: Multi-satellite hyperspectral image classification is increasingly expected to be performed on-orbit to reduce downlink and annotation costs. However, existing unsupervised domain adaptation methods typically rely on the closed-set assumption that source and target domains share the same label space, which is often violated in real multi-satellite deployments due to temporal land-cover changes and sensor upgrades. When the target domain contains previously unseen classes, directly aligning the two domains may induce negative transfer, making it difficult to learn a reliable decision boundary between known and unknown categories, especially under privacy constraints that prohibit raw data sharing. To address these challenges, we propose FedAdapt, an open-set unsupervised federated domain adaptation framework for cross-satellite hyperspectral image classification. FedAdapt first constructs class prototype vectors to induce a discriminative metric space for known classes and estimates an instance-level reliability weight for each target sample by its similarity to the prototypes. Based on this reliability, a relevance-driven weighting strategy is introduced to perform cautious adversarial domain alignment, emphasizing likely-known target samples while suppressing potential unknowns to mitigate negative transfer. In addition, an energy-based dynamic thresholding scheme is learned to adaptively separate known and unknown target samples without manual threshold tuning. Experimental results on multiple cross-scene HSI classification tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing

papers.title: S-PFEL: Secured Prototypical Personalized Federated Edge Learning for Consumer Electronics
FSSL-TANet: A Federated Semi-Supervised Temporal Attention Network for Personalized Early Detection of Age-Related Macular Degeneration in Consumer Electronics
papers.abstract: The growing integration of consumer electronics in digital healthcare has opened promising pathways for personalized diagnosis of vision disorders, particularly Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD). Devices such as mobile retinal scanners and home-based OCT units now produce extensive time-stamped patient data. However, leveraging this data effectively is hindered by challenges, including privacy concerns, limited computational resources on edge devices, and the non-identical distribution of data across users, which make traditional centralized learning approaches less viable. To navigate these constraints, this study presents FSSL-TANet—a Federated Semi-Supervised Learning Temporal Attention Network tailored for multi-task AMD prediction using decentralized, longitudinal health data. The architecture integrates residual recurrent encoding, hierarchical temporal fusion, and a dual-channel attention mechanism to extract disease progression patterns from both labeled and unlabeled sequences. Personalization is achieved through an Adaptive Federated Temporal Aggregation (AFTA) mechanism that tailors updates based on client-specific behavior. Furthermore, a hybrid optimization strategy (AH-GTO) enhances training efficiency by reducing convergence time during hyperparameter tuning. An experimental evaluation on two public datasets—AMDP and ODIR—demonstrates the model’s strong performance, achieving 98.7% accuracy in AMD stage classification, a risk score RMSE of 0.038, and a time-to-AMD (TTAMD) estimation MAE of 1.32 months. The model also achieves a Temporal Progression Sensitivity (TPS) of 0.944, reduces overfitting by 19%, improves client fairness by 11%, and converges 24% faster compared to baseline optimizers. Designed for real-world deployment, FSSL-TANet is both lightweight and privacy-aware, making it well-suited for consumer-grade health tools such as mobile eye screening devices and home-based vision monitors. Its ability to deliver personalized AMD monitoring in everyday settings marks a meaningful advancement in the field of digital ophthalmic care.

papers.title: Data Heterogeneity and Byzantine Resiliency in Decentralized Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) enables direct peer-to-peer model updates among clients, thereby overcoming the single point of failure and network congestion inherent in centralized federated learning (CFL). However, DFL performance faces significant challenges arising from data heterogeneity across clients and possible Byzantine attacks, which may severely degrade model performance. Although some recent work has attempted to address these dual challenges, they still suffer from at least one of the following limitations: 1) limited robustness under high data heterogeneity or sophisticated attacks; 2) weak convergence rates; or 3) high computational complexity. This paper proposes Federated Scissors (FedScissors), a novel Byzantine-robust DFL algorithm robust to non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data distributions and Byzantine attacks. FedScissors integrates proximal term regularization to mitigate client drift caused by data heterogeneity and a scissors-like neighborhood-based aggregation technique to screen out Byzantine inputs with low computational complexity. We establish rigorous theoretical convergence guarantees for FedScissors under heterogeneous data distributions and Byzantine attacks. Extensive experiments on FashionMNIST and MNIST datasets show that FedScissors achieves better performance compared to state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods across varying degrees of data heterogeneity and Byzantine attack models.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Mobility-Aware Vehicle Selection and Bandwidth Allocation for Federated Learning in Vehicular Networks: An HPPO Approach
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for enabling distributed model training in vehicular networks while keeping raw data local. However, the dynamic mobility of vehicles and the limited spectrum resources create critical challenges for efficient FL execution. In particular, due to the high mobility of vehicles, the candidate set of participating vehicles keeps changing, which makes fixed-threshold selection strategies difficult to be applied effectively. Moreover, vehicle mobility also causes time-varying channel status, and if resource allocation is performed only once at the beginning of each training round, it might not match the varying channels, resulting in imprecise resource allocation and accordingly low resource utilization. To address these issues, we propose a dynamic vehicular FL framework where the long time duration is discretized into fine-grained time slots. A long time sequence two-timescale optimization problem is then formulated to jointly conduct vehicle selection and slot-level communication bandwidth allocation. To solve it, we design a hierarchical Markov Decision Process (H-MDP) framework, and then develop a hierarchical Proximal Policy Optimization-based vehicle selection and bandwidth allocation (HPPO-VSBAFL) strategy, consisting of two cooperative agents: a vehicle selection agent (VSA) for round-level participant selection, and a bandwidth allocation agent (BAA) for slot-level spectrum allocation. Extensive experimental results based on CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18 demonstrate that the proposed HPPO-VSBAFL framework significantly improves FL accuracy compared to baseline schemes, and can effectively adapt to the highly dynamic vehicular environments.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: FedShield: Robust Federated Intrusion Detection for Consumer IoT under Malicious Updates using Blockchain Validation
papers.abstract: The rapid adoption of IoT in healthcare enables real-time patient monitoring but introduces severe security and privacy vulnerabilities, including malicious node attacks, privacy leakage from centralized model training, and high blockchain storage costs. To address these challenges, we propose FedShield, a federated learning and blockchain-based intrusion detection framework for consumer IoT healthcare networks. FedShield keeps patient data locally at healthcare units, trains a hybrid CNN–KNN ensemble on virtual machines, and securely aggregates only model updates via a cloud server. A Proof-of-Stake blockchain ensures only authorized nodes can update the global model, while IPFS reduces on-chain storage by 93%. Extensive evaluations on the mHealth dataset and four additional public datasets (WISDM, PAMAP2, CIC-IDS2017, Edge-IIoTset) demonstrate that FedShield achieves 98.02% accuracy, 96.01% precision, 94.87% recall, and 95.44% F1-score, outperforming centralized KNN, CNN, and recent state-of-the-art FL-blockchain frameworks. It also maintains robust performance under sophisticated attacks (label-flipping, backdoor, model replacement, gradient inversion) and scales to 100 healthcare units with minimal accuracy degradation. Unlike prior FL-blockchain IDS that only combine existing components, FedShield introduces three novel mechanisms: (i) a non-parametric KNN immune to gradient poisoning, (ii) stake-weighted gradient deviation with coupled PoS, and (iii) attack-dependent blockchain integrity. These results confirm that FedShield provides an effective, privacy-preserving, and scalable solution for malicious node detection in IoT healthcare environments.

papers.title: FedTrust-UNLEARN: Trust-Aware Federated Learning with Auditable Unlearning for Privacy-Preserving Consumer IoMT EEG Intelligence
papers.abstract: The growing adoption of EEG-enabled consumer Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices and wearable neuro-monitoring systems in healthcare and home-centric environments has raised critical concerns regarding data privacy, trust, and regulatory compliance. Although centralised deep learning approaches achieve strong performance in EEG-based emotion and cognitive state recognition, their reliance on centralised data aggregation limits scalability and applicability in privacy-sensitive consumer healthcare settings. Furthermore, existing federated learning approaches often inadequately address trust heterogeneity, non-IID neurophysiological variability, unreliable client participation, and the emerging requirement of federated unlearning in distributed IoMT environments. This paper proposes FedTrust-UNLEARN, a trust-aware federated learning framework with auditable unlearning for privacy-preserving EEG intelligence across heterogeneous consumer IoMT networks. The proposed framework integrates adaptive spectral representation learning, dynamic trust-aware aggregation, and an auditable federated unlearning mechanism that enables selective attenuation of client influence without requiring complete retraining. Extensive experiments on the SEED, SEED-IV, and DREAMER datasets under subject-dependent and subject-independent settings demonstrate competitive performance relative to centralised learning while improving robustness against unreliable clients, privacy preservation, and practical unlearning behaviour. The results demonstrate stable collaborative optimisation, bounded post-unlearning degradation, and communication-efficient deployment, highlighting the practicality of trustworthy, regulation-aware federated EEG intelligence for real-world consumer IoMT healthcare applications.

papers.title: RDTSM: Robust Defense Based on Trusted Shadow Model Against Poisoning Attacks for Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative model training without sharing raw data, but remains vulnerable to poisoning attacks from malicious clients. These adversarial participants craft harmful updates to degrade global model performance or induce targeted misclassification. Without trusted reference gradients, the central model cannot be properly aggregated only based on updates provided by untrustworthy clients. In this paper, we propose RDTSM, a robust defense method based on a trusted shadow model. By leveraging a clean shadow dataset, the central server generates reference updates and evaluates each client’s update via a reputation scoring mechanism. A clustering algorithm is then applied to identify and exclude suspicious updates before model aggregation. Extensive experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 demonstrate that RDTSM consistently outperforms state-of-the-art defenses across a wide range of poisoning attacks. Notably, RDTSM maintains high accuracy even when the proportion of malicious clients is large, and remains robust under varying degrees of data heterogeneity and shadow dataset sizes. This robustness stems from the fact that shadow-guided reputation scores of benign and malicious clients remain well separated under homogeneous attack patterns, even when malicious clients constitute the majority. These results show RDTSM’s effectiveness and practicality for secure federated learning in adversarial environments.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: A Dual-Level Selective Unlearning Framework for Multi-Agent Decentralized Federated Learning
papers.abstract: In agentic AI-enabled edge computing, decentralized federated learning (DFL) leverages peer-to-peer model aggregation to improve the performance of on-device large language models (LLMs) without introducing a single point of failure, thereby enhancing local agents’ capabilities for decision-making. To protect the right to be forgotten for each agent, as required by data regulations such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), federated unlearning aims to remove the influence of a target agent’s data from the trained LLM while preserving model utility. However, existing federated unlearning methods predominantly assume centralized architectures and face two critical challenges when extended to decentralized federated learning systems: 1) requiring all remaining agents to participate in the unlearning process incurs prohibitive overhead; and 2) updating all Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) modules indiscriminately leads to excessive resource consumption while potentially degrading model performance. To tackle these challenges, we propose a dual-level selective unlearning framework (DSU) for decentralized federated learning. At the agent level, DSU selects retained agents by matching historical LoRA update sketches, label sketches, and exposure to the withdrawn agent. Meanwhile, we derive a sensitivity score from the DFL training trajectory that measures each LoRA module’s accumulated influence from the target agent via the energy of its effective weight changes, and then update only the most sensitive modules while freezing the rest. Theoretical analysis relates selective unlearning to full-participation unlearning, and experiments show that DSU reduces the audited target-agent influence while preserving retained utility and reducing both participating agents and updated LoRA modules in the evaluated settings. The public reproducibility package is available athttps://github.com/DGL-codes/LLM-DFL
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Age-of-Information Aware Federated Learning With Finite Speed Pinching Antenna
papers.abstract: This paper investigates age-of-information (AoI) aware federated learning over wireless networks with finite speed pinching antennas. In contrast to existing studies that assume an infinitely high antenna moving speed, a practical round based training procedure is considered, where the pinching antenna is repositioned during the local training phase and its feasible movement range depends on the selected devices. This creates a new coupling among device selection, antenna placement, local training time, model uploading time, and AoI evolution. To characterize the impact of antenna moving speed, the rate gain over the fixed antenna and the gap to the infinite speed benchmark are analyzed. Subsequently, an overall AoI minimization problem is formulated under a round latency deadline by jointly optimizing the selected device set and the pinching antenna position. A coalitional game based device selection algorithm is proposed, where finite speed antenna placement is incorporated into the coalition utility evaluation. For antenna placement, the optimal search region is derived by exploiting the mobility constraint and device location span, based on which a branch-and-bound (BnB) algorithm is developed to obtain the global optimum. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme can accelerate learning convergence, reduce the sum AoI, and improve device participation compared with baseline schemes, demonstrating the potential of pinching antennas for enhancing federated learning through flexible spatial reconfiguration.

papers.title: Closing the Generalization Gap in Parameter-Efficient Federated Edge Learning
papers.abstract: Federated edge learning (FEEL) provides a promising foundation for edge artificial intelligence (AI) by enabling collaborative model training while preserving data privacy. However, limited and heterogeneous local datasets, as well as resource-constrained deployment, severely degrade both model generalization and resource utilization, leading to compromised learning performance. To tackle this issue, in this paper, we propose a parameter-efficient FEEL framework that jointly leverages model pruning and client selection. First, we derive an information-theoretic generalization discrepancy coefficient that characterizes the discrepancy between training and reference test function losses and embed it into the convergence analysis. It reveals that a larger local generalization discrepancy coefficient can undermine the global convergence. Then, we formulate a generalization-aware average squared gradient norm bound minimization problem, by jointly optimizing the pruning ratios, client selection, and communication-computation resources under energy and delay constraints. Despite its non-convexity, the resulting mixed-integer problem is efficiently solved via an alternating optimization algorithm. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed design achieves superior learning performance to state-of-the-art baselines, validating the effectiveness of coupling generalization-aware analysis with system-level optimization for efficient FEEL.

papers.title: Dynamic Role Based Asynchronous Federated Learning for Scalability and Adaptive Consumer Electronics Networks
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) naturally fits intelligent consumer electronics through its privacy-preserving distributed training. However, practical deployment faces constraints from rigid architectures and static paradigms lacking the scalability and adaptability required for real-world settings. These limitations lead to significant inefficiencies and security risks when managing dynamic data quality and node reliability. To overcome these challenges, We propose Dynamic Role-Driven Asynchronous Federated Learning (DRFL), a system with a semi-decentralized architecture that features a Training-Validation-Idle (TVI) role model and dynamic role transition mechanisms. In this framework, the server uniformly handles role assignment, aggregation weight computation, and global model updates. Training clients perform local training and model uploading in a distributed manner, while validation nodes perform cosine similarity computation and trustworthiness filtering. Meanwhile, blockchain is used to archive and trace all training data, role changes, and model information throughout the entire process. We further propose CT-NodeSelect with Dynamic Weighted Aggregation (CT-NodeSelect with DWA), which models role assignment as a sequential decision problem. It uses a unified quantitative metric to drive TVI role allocation and employs cosine similarity to determine model aggregation weights, balancing immediate performance with long-term robustness. The Monte Carlo Federated State Optimization scheme (MC-FedState) further enables efficient scheduling and scalable resource management. Evaluations on CIFAR-10 and MNIST show that DRFL achieves superior performance over baselines under diverse non-IID settings, owing to its dynamic role scheduling, which accelerates model convergence. Ablation studies quantify the contributions of individual modules and validate the effectiveness of integrating cosine weighting, dynamic scheduling, and long-term optimization.

papers.title: Dropout-Tolerant Privacy-Preserving Aggregation for Federated Mobile Crowdsensing
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a key enabler for privacy-preserving, decentralized sensing systems, giving rise to Federated Mobile Crowdsensing (F-MCS). A well-known bottleneck in such systems is the inefficiency of synchronous training, which stalls for all participants and is susceptible to stragglers in heterogeneous environments. Although asynchronous FL methods have been explored to alleviate this, they often introduce the critical issue of stale updates, which can degrade model convergence and accuracy. To simultaneously address the challenges of efficiency, staleness, and robustness, this paper proposes a novel Dropout-Tolerant Privacy Aggregation (DTPA) scheme for FL that operates without a trusted third party (TTP). Our solution leverages the distributed decryption feature of the lifted EC-ElGamal cryptosystem to enable secure, decentralized model aggregation. We further introduce an efficient worker selection algorithm to systematically reduce waiting time. Moreover, a dedicated dropout-tolerant mechanism is developed to maintain protocol execution even under a high rate of client failures, thereby enhancing robustness. Security analysis confirms that our scheme fulfills essential privacy and security requirements. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed DTPA scheme significantly improves training efficiency and convergence stability compared to state-of-the-art methods, while remaining practical for deployment on resource-constrained mobile devices.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: Federated Learning With Enhanced Privacy via Model Splitting and Random Client Participation
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) often adopts differential privacy (DP) to protect client data, but the added noise required for privacy guarantees can substantially degrade model accuracy. To resolve this challenge, we propose model-splitting privacy-amplified federated learning (MS-PAFL), a novel framework that combines structural model splitting with statistical privacy amplification. In this framework, each client’s model is partitioned into a private submodel, retained locally, and a public submodel, released for global aggregation. The calibrated Gaussian noise is injected only into the public submodel, thereby confining its adverse impact while preserving the utility of the retained local model components. We further present a rigorous theoretical analysis that characterizes the joint privacy amplification achieved through random client participation and local data subsampling under this architecture. The analysis provides explicit bounds on both single-round and total privacy loss, demonstrating that MS-PAFL significantly reduces the noise necessary to satisfy a target privacy protection level. Extensive experiments validate our theoretical findings, showing that MS-PAFL consistently attains a superior privacy–utility trade-off compared with conventional DP-FL baselines and enables the training of highly accurate models under strong privacy guarantees.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: DFL-GC: A Decentralized Federated Framework for Planetary Gearbox Fault Diagnosis Under Domain Shift and Class Imbalance
papers.abstract: In planetary gearbox fault diagnosis, Federated Learning (FL) enables clients to train models while preserving data privacy collaboratively. However, achieving satisfactory performance typically assumes that data are independent and identically distributed across clients, and that class distributions within each client are balanced. In practice, these assumptions rarely hold: data collected at different clients under distinct working conditions induce domain shift, and within each client, predominantly normal operation leaves few fault samples, leading to class imbalance. Domain shift can destabilize model aggregation, and class imbalance biases learning toward the majority class. Therefore, addressing the coexisting domain shift and class imbalance is essential for the practical application of FL. To support serverless collaboration under parameter-only communication, a Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) framework with a Gaussianized Feature Alignment Module (GFAM) and a Class-Balanced Kullback–Leibler loss (CBKL), named DFL-GC, is proposed and aggregated via a ring topology without a central server. During local training, each client applies GFAM to map local features to a standard Gaussian distribution and refines representations with a self-attention mechanism, reducing inter-client distribution discrepancy and improving diagnostic performance; CBKL applies client-specific class-frequency-aware weighting to Kullback–Leibler divergence terms to strengthen intra-class prediction consistency and interclass prediction separation for minority classes, improving minority-class diagnosis. Experiments on two planetary gearbox datasets show improved domain alignment and robustness to class imbalance, yielding superior diagnostic performance and outperforming seven comparative methods.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement

papers.title: Joint Routing and Model Pruning for Decentralized Federated Learning in Bandwidth-Constrained Multi-Hop Wireless Networks
papers.abstract: Decentralized federated learning (D-FL) enables privacy-preserving training without a central server, but multi-hop model exchanges and aggregation are often bottlenecked by communication resource constraints. To address this issue, we propose a joint routing-and-pruning framework that optimizes routing paths and pruning rates to keep communication latency within prescribed limits. We analyze how the sum of model biases across all clients affects the convergence bound of DFL, and formulate an optimization that maximizes the model retention rate to reduce these biases under communication constraints. Further analysis shows that each client’s model retention rate is path-dependent, which reduces the original problem to a routing optimization. Leveraging this insight, we develop a routing algorithm that selects latency-efficient transmission paths, allowing more parameters to be delivered within the time budget and thereby improving D-FL convergence. Simulations show that, compared with unpruned systems, the proposed framework reduces average transmission latency by 27.8% and improves testing accuracy by about 12%; relative to standard benchmark routing algorithms, the proposed routing method further improves accuracy by roughly 8%.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Electrochemical Coupled Federated Multisensor Measurement Framework for GIS Insulation Fault Detection and Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Accurate insulation fault diagnosis in gas-insulated substations (GISs) is hindered by the limited sensitivity of single-sensor systems and the heterogeneity of field data. To enhance both measurement sensitivity and detection reliability of GIS insulation faults, this paper proposes an electro-chemical coupled federated multi-sensor fusion network (FMSFN) that integrates multi-modal sensing and distributed analytics into a unified measurement system. The proposed framework introduces a novel electro-chemical coupled detection mechanism that jointly captures electrical discharge characteristics and gas-chemical decomposition signatures to enable homogeneous and heterogeneous feature fusion under a federated cloud–edge architecture. This design supports distributed, privacy-preserving fault diagnosis across multiple users and devices. Within the proposed FMSFN, a deep fusion network equipped with an adaptive hybrid attention module is employed to strengthen cross-sensor feature interaction and enable dynamic modality-aware weighting, while a federated hierarchical optimization strategy with personalized updates and noise-aware aggregation ensures stable and robust convergence under non-IID data distributions. Experimental results demonstrate that the FMSFN achieves 97.23% accuracy and a 96.83% macro F1-score, consistently outperforming existing single-sensor and centralized diagnostic models. These results confirm the robustness, scalability, and practical applicability of the proposed electrochemical-coupled measurement system, which provides a scalable instrumentation approach for GIS insulation fault diagnosis.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement

papers.title: A Hierarchical Federated Learning Framework for Sustainable Deployment in Dynamic-Cluster-Based Fault Diagnosis
papers.abstract: The inefficiency of fault diagnosis based on federated learning (FL) is attributed to the variability and diversity exhibited by clients in a dynamic cluster. To tackle this issue, a hierarchical federated learning (HFL) framework is proposed, structured in a three-tiered architecture encompassing global clustering, local federation, and global aggregation phases. First, in the global clustering, a dynamic clustering strategy based on client characteristics is designed to divide all clients into multiple subsets and implement local federation. Second, the contribution of local subsets to global aggregation is quantified using Shapley additive explanation (SHAP), and the model parameters are weighted based on their respective contribution values, which aims to alleviate the negative impact of subset model drift on global aggregation. Third, the loss function in model training of clients is redesigned to incorporate two regularization terms, which serve to reconstruct the relationship between new and old samples. This modification avoids full samples training and reduces computation costs. The validation on inter-shaft bearing fault diagnosis dataset of an aero-engine system demonstrates the efficacy of this study in addressing the security joint modeling of a dynamic cluster. This offers a viable solution for achieving sustainable federated deployment within the industrial dynamic clients cluster.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement

papers.title: A Domain-Informed Hierarchical Federated Learning Framework for DDoS Detection in WSN for Critical Infrastructure
papers.abstract: The deployment of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) in critical infrastructure, such as Small Modular Reactors (SMRs), faces cybersecurity threats like Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks that can overload these networks and disrupt monitoring and control functions. Current DDoS detection systems often suffer from high false positive rates, neglect domain-specific operational constraints, and rely on centralized architectures that pose privacy risks, making them less suitable for distributed Internet of Things (IoT) environments. To address these issues, we propose a novel Domain-informed Hierarchical Federated Learning (DHFL) framework for WSN used in SMR monitoring and control applications. Our framework features a dual-branch bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architecture comprising of two parallel processing branches with network-specific constraints, facilitating precise detection of DDoS attacks. It includes differentiable penalty functions to enforce domain-aligned behaviour and employs adaptive trust scoring to evaluate the reliability of individual nodes. These elements operate within a hierarchical Federated Learning (FL) structure organized into three tiers: sensor nodes, local aggregators, and a global coordinator, allowing collaborative training that preserves privacy. Unlike earlier approaches, our method not only maintains privacy by ensuring that raw sensor data never leaves the local nodes and only model updates are shared but also considers the operational importance and trustworthiness of each node through tier-weighted aggregation. Tested on the CICIoT2023 dataset, our system achieved 93.4% accuracy, 94.5% precision, 97.5% recall, 95.5% F1-score, and 98.9% AUC, surpassing state-of-the-art FL methods in both performance and efficiency. Furthermore, it converged in fewer communication rounds (30–50) with reduced communication costs (from 45 MB to 30 MB per round). Our framework can differentiate between normal reactor transients and actual attacks, making it suitable for mission-critical SMR cybersecurity.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: Joint Spatio-Temporal Federated Learning for Cellular Traffic Prediction
papers.abstract: Cellular traffic prediction is essential for the energy-efficient and intelligent management of base stations (BSs). In this context, Federated Learning allows BSs to collaboratively train a shared model without transmitting raw data, thus significantly reducing communication overhead and enhancing privacy protection. Despite these advantages, most existing methods struggle to alleviate the coupled spatio-temporal heterogeneity of cellular traffic data across BSs, resulting in suboptimal global prediction performance. The main reason is that they decouple spatio-temporal relationships by modeling temporal and spatial properties independently, with limited consideration of their dependencies in cellular traffic. To overcome these limitations, we propose FedJST, a joint spatio-temporal federated cellular traffic prediction method that effectively integrates the temporal and spatial properties of cellular traffic from different BSs in two key aspects. Firstly, to capture spatio-temporal dependencies, we propose a multi-scale feature guidance strategy. This strategy leverages global multi-scale feature to incorporate shared spatio-temporal information, encouraging local models to capture complex spatio-temporal interactions. Secondly, we propose a spatio-temporal property-aware BS selection strategy that leverages a lightweight augmented dataset to prioritize representative BSs for training, enabling effective learning of diverse spatio-temporal patterns. We conduct extensive experiments across six cases on two real-world datasets, demonstrating that FedJST achieves average improvements of 5.95%, 4.43%, and 2.99% in RMSE, MAE, andR2metrics, respectively.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: DOCAttack: Data-Oriented Community Attack in Decentralized Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Decentralized federated learning (DFL) relies on peer-to-peer communication, making its convergence highly sensitive to how non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) client data propagate across the network. Existing structural attacks operate purely on topology and therefore miss the vulnerabilities that stem from the interaction between non-IID client data and the network structure. In this paper, we propose a data-oriented community attack (DOCAttack) framework in DFL. First, the proposed framework fuses leaked client data profiles with network structure to learn data-aware node embeddings. Then, it detects data-oriented communities from these embeddings. Finally, it optimizes node and edge removals under a given budget. Experimental results show that DOCAttack produces stronger structural disruption than topology-only baselines and consistently isolates data-oriented communities that these baselines fail to separate. In addition, these disruptions prevent the system from integrating information across communities, leading to degraded learning performance and the collapse of global consensus.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Hash Prototype Personalized Federated Learning for Multi-Site Brain Network Analysis
papers.abstract: Multi-site brain network analysis methods have garnered significant attention due to their ability to leverage diverse samples from multiple hospitals. Meanwhile, the growing emphasis on medical privacy protection has driven the development of secure multi-site learning approaches, such as federated learning. However, the challenges of cross-site data distribution alignment and personalized model construction under privacy constraints remain inadequately addressed, which limits the effectiveness of existing multi-site federated approaches. In this paper, we propose a hash prototype-based personalized federated learning method for multi-site brain network analysis, which enables effective cross-site data distribution calibration and neurological pattern recognition. Firstly, we decouple local models into shared encoders to preserve site-specific features and a hash encoding layer to generate prototype representations with reduced information exposure. Secondly, these hash prototypes are aggregated and disseminated across sites, facilitating the generation of prototypes that guide cross-site data distribution alignment. Additionally, encoder parameters from different sites are dynamically aggregated, fusing global and local knowledge while preserving the personalized feature extraction capabilities of each site. Finally, we validate the personalized models across multiple sites. Extensive experiments on Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE), Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), and Schizophrenia (SZ) datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art multisite methods. Furthermore, our method can more effectively identify multi-site brain network biomarkers due to the learned prototypes.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive and Developmental Systems

papers.title: Meta-PFL: Meta-Based Personalized Federated Learning Against Gradient Inversion Attacks
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without sharing raw client data, but exchanged model updates may still leak sensitive information through gradient inversion (GI) attacks. Existing defenses often rely on gradient perturbation, cryptographic protocols, or architectural bottlenecks, which may introduce utility loss or additional system assumptions. In this work, we study empirical GI robustness in personalized federated learning from the perspective of representation divergence. We observe that personalized models can increase client-level latent misalignment, thereby making DLG/iDLG-style gradient matching less well-conditioned. Based on this insight, we propose Meta-PFL, a personalized FL framework that combines client-private VAE encoders, classifier-side model sharing, group-level meta-adaptation, and inter-group knowledge distillation. Under our threat model, the server or an external eavesdropper can observe uploaded classifier-side updates and knows the training protocol and model split, but cannot access raw data, client-private encoder parameters, encoder-side gradients, or stochastic latent samples. Meta-PFL does not provide formal differential privacy or cryptographic guarantees; instead, it aims to reduce reconstruction quality under the specified GI threat model while preserving utility under non-IID data. Experiments on Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 show that Meta-PFL achieves competitive or superior personalized accuracy and consistently reduces reconstruction quality under DLG/iDLG-style attacks. Additional evaluations with recent personalized FL baselines, stronger-budget GI stress tests, representation-divergence quantification, clustering-quality analysis, and efficiency measurements further support the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Cooperative Network Learning for Large-Scale and Decentralized Graphs
papers.abstract: Graph representation learning has become a vital tool for capturing intricate relationships within networked systems. However, as graphs scale up, data privacy concerns and regulatory restrictions often isolate data within different institutions, hindering collaborative analysis. While federated learning (FL) and swarm learning (SL) offer decentralized solutions, FL relies on a central coordinator, and SL struggles with non-I.I.D. graph data, limiting their flexibility and applicability to complex graph structures. Therefore, establishing a mutual trust mechanism among graph agencies is crucial to unlocking the full potential of graphs. In this article, we introduce a cooperative network learning (CNL) framework to ensure secure graph computing across diverse graph tasks. CNL unifies local and global graph neural network (GNN) perspectives through secure virtual graph connections, enabling collaborative training on decentralized graphs without centralized coordination, while homomorphic encryption and secure communication further preserve privacy. Moreover, CNL enables each agency to maintain autonomy by designing heterogeneous models tailored to its own tasks, going beyond FL and SL. Extensive experiments on contagion dynamics prediction and various traditional graph tasks demonstrate that our CNL architecture outperforms state-of-the-art GNNs developed at individual sites, revealing that CNL provides a reliable, fair, secure, privacy-preserving, and global perspective for effective and personalized network applications. This framework promises to address privacy concerns in graph-related research and integrate decentralized graph data structures to benefit the network research community in cooperation and innovation.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems

papers.title: FedSTGAT: Federated Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Network for Root Alarm Identification in Optical Transport Network
papers.abstract: In Optical Transport Networks (OTNs), faults often generate numerous derived alarms that may obscure the true root alarm. When multiple faults occur within the same time window, their alarm propagation may overlap, so the earliest observed alarm is not necessarily the root alarm. Accurate Root Alarm Identification (RAI) is therefore essential for timely fault management and reliable network operation. Traditional RAI methods rely on handcrafted alarm rules and struggle to capture the spatio-temporal nature of alarm propagation. Existing spatio-temporal methods, however, often focus on a single modality or localized dependencies and therefore overlook the coupled interactions among topology, time, and propagation behavior, which limits their accuracy and scalability in large OTNs. To address these challenges, we propose a Federated Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Network (FedSTGAT). FedSTGAT transforms raw alarm records into spatio-temporal subgraphs and applies STGAT for RAI. We further incorporate a meta-path-consistent learning objective to distill higher-order propagation patterns, improving both accuracy and interpretability. To address data silos and privacy constraints in multi-domain OTNs, we integrate FedSTGAT into a federated learning framework that enables collaborative training without sharing raw alarms. Experimental results show that FedSTGAT achieves an RAI accuracy of 0.9653, improving accuracy by 0.2473 on average over rule-based methods, and remains above 0.91 in the federated setting. Overall, FedSTGAT provides an effective and interpretable framework for intelligent RAI to support fault diagnosis and operational decision-making.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Neural Collapse Based Deep Supervised Federated Learning for Signal Detection in OFDM Systems
papers.abstract: Future wireless networks are expected to be AI-empowered, making their performance highly dependent on the quality of training datasets. However, physical-layer entities often observe only partial wireless environments characterized by different power delay profiles. Federated learning is capable of addressing this limited observability, but often struggles with data heterogeneity. To tackle this challenge, we propose a neural collapse (NC) inspired deep supervised federated learning (NCDSFL) algorithm. Specifically, we first define an NC solution for the multi-binary classification problem and establish its optimality by revealing its connection to the global optimum. We then incorporate the deep supervision technique into deep neural networks and fix the weights at both the output layer and an auxiliary hidden layer using the derived NC solutions. When this strategy is applied in a federated learning setting, it encourages different clients to produce similar hidden features, thereby enabling the proposed algorithm to effectively address data heterogeneity and achieve fast convergence. Simulations for signal detection in OFDM systems confirm the NC phenomenon and demonstrate that NCDSFL outperforms several baselines in terms of convergence speed and accuracy.

papers.title: Split Learning-Enabled Framework for Secure and Lightweight Internet of Medical Things Systems
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices has resulted in significant security risks, particularly the risk of malware attacks on resource-constrained devices. Conventional deep learning methods are impractical due to resource limitations, while Federated Learning (FL) suffers from high communication overhead and vulnerability to non-IID (heterogeneous) data. In this paper, we propose a split learning (SL) based framework for IoMT malware detection through image-based classification. By dividing the neural network training between the clients and an edge server, the framework reduces computational burden on resource-constrained clients while ensuring data privacy. We formulate a joint optimization problem that balances computation cost and communication efficiency by using a game-theoretic approach for attaining better training performance. Experimental evaluations show that the proposed framework outperforms popular FL methods in terms of accuracy, F1-score, high convergence speed, and less resource consumption. These results establish the potential of SL as a scalable and secure paradigm for next-generation IoMT security.

papers.title: FLClear: Collision-Free, Secure, and Visually Interpretable Multi-Client Watermarking for Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables multiple clients to collaboratively train a shared global model while preserving the privacy of their local data. Within this paradigm, the intellectual property rights (IPR) of client models constitute critical assets that must be protected. In practice, the central server responsible for maintaining the global model may maliciously manipulate it to erase client contributions or falsely claim sole ownership, thereby infringing on clients' IPR. Watermarking has emerged as a promising technique for asserting model ownership and safeguarding intellectual property. However, existing FL watermarking approaches remain limited, suffering from potential watermark collisions among clients, inadequate watermark security, and non-intuitive verification mechanisms. In this paper, we proposeFLClear, a novel framework that simultaneously achieves collision-free watermark aggregation, enhanced watermark security, and visually interpretable ownership verification. Specifically,FLClearintroduces a transposed model jointly optimized via contrastive learning to integrate the watermarking and main-task objectives. During verification, the watermark is reconstructed from the transposed model and evaluated through both visual inspection and structural similarity metrics, enabling intuitive and quantitative ownership verification. Comprehensive experiments conducted over various datasets, aggregation schemes, and attack scenarios demonstrate the effectiveness ofFLClearand confirm that it consistently outperforms state-of-the-art FL watermarking methods while incurring acceptable overheads.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Remote Rowhammer Attack Using Adversarial Observations on Federated Learning Clients
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has the potential for simultaneous global learning amongst a large number of parallel agents, enabling emerging AI systems to be trained across demographically diverse data. Central to this being efficient is the ability for FL to perform sparse gradient updates and remote direct memory access at the central server. Most of the research in FL security focuses on protecting data privacy at the edge client or in the communication channels between the client and server. Client-facing attacks on the server are less well investigated as the assumption is that a large collective of clients offer resilience. Here, for the first time, we show that by attacking clients that lead to repetitive clustered memory updates in the server, we can remote initiate a rowhammer attack to corrupt the server memory with induced bit-flips. A reinforcement learning (RL) attacker without backdoor access to the server can learn how to maximize server repetitive clustered memory updates by manipulating the clients' sensor observation. We demonstrate the feasibility of our attack using FL systems with sparse updates, tasked for automatic speech recognition (ASR) as well as CIFAR10 classification, our adversarial attacking agent can achieve around 70% repeated update rate (RUR) in the targeted server model, effectively inducing bit flips on server DRAM. The security implications are that such adversarial observations can cause disruptions to learning or may inadvertently cause elevated privilege, which could pave the way for further research on practical mitigation strategies in FL and hardware design.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Federated Multi-Task Clustering
papers.abstract: Spectral clustering has emerged as one of the most effective clustering algorithms due to its superior performance. However, most existing models are designed for centralized settings, rendering them inapplicable in modern decentralized environments. Moreover, current federated learning approaches often suffer from poor generalization performance due to reliance on unreliable pseudo-labels, and fail to capture the latent correlations amongst heterogeneous clients. To tackle these limitations, this paper proposes a novel framework named Federated Multi-Task Clustering (i.e.,FMTC), which intends to learn personalized clustering models for heterogeneous clients while collaboratively leveraging their shared underlying structure in a privacy-preserving manner. More specifically, the FMTC framework is composed of two main components: client-side personalized clustering module, which learns a parameterized mapping model to support robust out-of-sample inference, bypassing the need for unreliable pseudo-labels; and server-side tensorial correlation module, which explicitly captures the shared knowledge across all clients. This is achieved by organizing all client models into a unified tensor and applying a low-rank regularization to discover their common subspace. To solve this joint optimization problem, we derive an efficient, privacy-preserving distributed algorithm based on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers, which decomposes the global problem into parallel local updates on clients and an aggregation step on the server. To the end, several extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate that our proposed FMTC framework significantly outperforms various baseline and state-of-the-art federated clustering algorithms.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology

papers.title: Federated Learning-Driven Face Forgery Detection via Rich Feature Complementary Fusion
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of cyber–physical–social systems (CPSSs) highlights the critical need for authentic digital interactions. However, this progress is threatened by deepfake technology, which can undermine system security and trust. Existing deepfake detection models, while effective, typically require centralized data and thus create significant privacy and security vulnerabilities. Furthermore, their reliance on single-modal RGB data limits their ability to detect sophisticated forgeries. This work introduces a novel framework that tackles both challenges simultaneously. We leverage federated learning (FL) to enable collaborative model training without sharing sensitive data and preserving privacy. To enhance detection accuracy, we move beyond single-modal inputs by incorporating a spatial-rich model (SRM) to extract high-frequency features indicative of manipulation. These features are then synergistically fused with RGB data via a specialized module to improve the model’s discriminative power. Experimental results on the FF++ dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 92.00% and an AUC of 97.69%, which outperforms other competitors. These results validate the power of the multimodal fusion strategy and FL paradigm.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems

papers.title: Federated Coupled Contrastive Learning on Remote Sensing Image Classification
papers.abstract: Classification for Remote Sensing (RS) images plays a crucial role in various fields such as disaster assessment and urban planning. Nevertheless, due to resource limitations and privacy issues, directly transferring data to the ground for high-performance centralized training is often impractical. Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a revolutionary distributed learning paradigm, which enables collaborative training of a model without data sharing. However, since the RS data is distributed across numerous participants, FL suffers from an inevitable challenge of data heterogeneity for RS image classification. As the local data is more unevenly distributed, this challenge becomes increasingly pronounced, leading to inconsistent local update directions. In this paper, we propose RS-CCL, a novel Federated Coupled Contrastive Learning rule on RS image classification, which expands the feature space, thereby allowing models to better learn the intrinsic structure of the complex RS data effectively. Our RS-CCL mathematically formulates cross-entropy and feature similarity into a unified framework. It is then solved by coupled gradient computation in a consistent optimization direction, overcoming dimensional collapse. In this way, an enriched feature space is created, thereby facilitating the training of more capable models. Within this framework, we further introduce a dynamic fusion mask matrix, which inhibits the model from excessively drawing on inter-class similarity. Empirically, we show that our RS-CCL is in line with robustness theory that a larger feature space brings more robust performance. Extensive experiments on several benchmarks validate the effectiveness and generalization ability of our method. For example, with a high data heterogeneity of α = 0.05, our RS-CCL outperforms other baselines by up to 8.5% on UC Merced dataset with MobileViT-S. The code is available at https://github.com/cxy-xd/RS-CCL.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing

papers.title: A Verifiable Federated Learning Mechanism for Digital Museum Collection Based on Homomorphic Proxy Re-Authentication Technology
papers.abstract: Despite the opportunities presented by information technology and machine learning for the digitization of natural heritage, challenges such as insufficient data sets and inadequate security remain significant obstacles. To address these challenges, this article proposes a cross-regional intrusion detection federated learning scheme based on homomorphic encryption-based re-authentication technology. By integrating homomorphic encryption-based re-authentication, secret sharing, and key negotiation technologies, the scheme achieves an efficient and verifiable private gradient aggregation solution. Furthermore, the scheme introduces intermediary proxy nodes, thwarting collusive attacks between servers and participants and significantly enhancing the overall security of the system. Through these mechanisms, various issues related to privacy protection, data leakage, data forgery, and access control when multiple museums share collection data are effectively addressed. By implementing the designed scheme and amalgamating data from the National Museum of Natural History and the National Museum of Animals in China, a virtual insect exhibition hall has been developed. This endeavor serves to facilitate the creation of an information model for insects within the metaverse. Furthermore, due to the inherent characteristics of the scheme, not only is data security ensured, but it also fosters collaboration between museums, advancing the digital preservation and sharing of cultural heritage.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems

papers.title: CPFL: A Cluster-Based Parallel Blockchain Scheme for Secure and Efficient Federated Learning in Intelligent Connected Vehicles
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Prior-Assisted Personalized Federated Learning for Cooperative Spectrum Sensing
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Joint Communication Topology Reconstruction and Parameter Filtering for Heterogeneous Decentralized Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) has been strongly promoted in wireless edge networks because it facilitates collaborative training of machine learning models while ensuring the privacy and security of individual user data. Among different FL frameworks, Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) framework offers greater flexibility and broader applicability compared to traditional Centralized Federated Learning (CFL) framework. However, existing DFL framework fails to accommodate the heterogeneity of multi-dimensional resources (e.g., communication and computing resources), and further suffer from high communication overhead. These limitations result in reduced training efficiency. To address these issues, this paper proposes SoloDFL1, a framework integrating heterogeneity-aware communication topology reconstruction and parameter filtering. In SoloDFL, each client communicates with only one neighboring client, constructing a one-on-one communication topology, and exchanges only filtered local model parameters during communication. By doing so, SoloDFL copes with the synchronization barriers caused by system heterogeneity and further reduces communication overhead. The convergence of SoloDFL is proved theoretically. Extensive experiments show that SoloDFL achieves up to a 3.9× acceleration and reduces communication costs by an average of 20.5% compared to the benchmark algorithms.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Fast Federated Learning Frameworks, Driven by Powerball Function and Hypergradient Descent
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL), a paradigm of distributed machine learning, aims to utilize user data for model training while safeguarding data privacy. However, numerous challenges arise in practical applications. Among these, accelerating the training rate and improving the generalization performance of FL models are particularly noteworthy challenges. Recent studies are particularly about understanding the role of stochastic optimization in federated optimization, leading to various fast federated optimization algorithms. As a special case, some studies have explored treating the sum of local differences as pseudo-gradients and also introduced the global learning rate. To deal with the challenge, this work develops fast federated optimization algorithms from the perspective of the Powerball function and the hypergradient descent, coined FedPBHD, extending the family of federated optimization algorithms. Different from existing FL algorithms, FedPBHD renews the update direction by using the discretization’s of ordinary differential equations (ODEs). Besides, FedPBHD utilizes an adaptive update rule of the learning rate (an extremely crucial hyperparameter for FL algorithms). The convergence performance of FedPBHD has been established through a rigorous theoretical analysis. Finally, we compare our FedPBHD algorithms against numerous benchmark optimizers for different practical applications of computer vision, natural language processing under both independent identically distribution (IID) and non-IID conditions. Experimental results on different problems have shown encouraging performance of the novel Federated optimization algorithms.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems

papers.title: Federated Domain Generalization Based on Gaussian Mapping and Constrained Quadratic Programming for Rotating Machinery Fault Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Federated learning–based fault diagnosis enables collaborative monitoring of rotating machinery without sharing raw vibration data. In practice, variations in operating conditions and vibration measurement setups across clients lead to domain inconsistencies, which challenge the generalization of federated models. Federated domain generalization (FDG) addresses this issue by enabling cross-condition fault diagnosis. However, feature discrepancies across clients and inconsistent aggregation may still degrade performance. To address this, we propose a FDG framework based on Gaussian mapping and constrained quadratic programming (GCQP). GCQP models and aligns local feature distributions within a unified global Gaussian feature space, providing a stable reference that reduces distribution mismatch of learned features across clients induced by heterogeneous operating conditions. A constrained quadratic programming strategy then regulates gradient aggregation by identifying clients with similar characteristics and assigning optimized aggregation weights. Experiments on three real-world bearing and gearbox datasets show that GCQP achieves better cross-condition diagnostic accuracy and generalization than state-of-the-art methods.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement

papers.title: Privacy-Preserving Digital Publishing Framework for Next-Generation Communication Networks: A Verifiable Homomorphic Federated Learning Approach
papers.abstract: Next-generation communication networks are revolutionizing digital publishing through intelligent content distribution and collaborative optimization capabilities.
