However, existing federated learning approaches face fundamental limitations, including trusted third-party dependencies, excessive communication overhead, and vulnerability to collusion attacks between servers and participants. This paper introduces VHFL-DP, a verifiable homomorphic federated learning framework for digital publishing environments operating within 6G network infrastructures. The framework addresses critical privacy and scalability challenges through four key innovations: a distributed cryptographic key generation protocol that eliminates trusted third-party requirements, Chinese remainder theorem-based dimensionality reduction, auxiliary validation nodes that enable independent verification with constant-time complexity, and an intelligent incentive mechanism that rewards digital publishing platforms based on objective contribution quality metrics. Experimental evaluation on MNIST and Amazon reviews datasets across six baseline methods demonstrates that VHFL-DP achieves superior performance with accuracy improvements of 4.2% over the best baseline method. The framework maintains constant verification time ranging from 2.73 to 2.91 seconds regardless of platform count, increasing from ten to fifty, or dropout rates reaching thirty percent. Security evaluation reveals strong resilience with only 2.4 percentage point accuracy degradation under poisoning attacks compared to 6.7-7.0 points for baseline method, inference attack success near random guessing at 51.3%, and 92.4% successful aggregation under Byzantine adversaries.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: Privacy-Preserving and Hierarchically Fair Federated Learning in IoT Based on Compressed Sensing
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables a larger number of participants to collaboratively train a global while keeping their local privacy-sensitive data locally. This is achieved by sharing the gradient of each participant with the server. Unfortunately, a malicious attacker can infer the sensitive privacy of local training data from captured gradients. Moreover, most existing FL frameworks overlook an essential aspect of participation: fairness. Specifically, all participants receive the same FL model, regardless of their individual contributions. To address these issues, we propose a privacy-preserving and hierarchical FL framework based on Compressed Sensing (CS), which incorporates privacy and fairness into FL models. Specifically, the CS-based gradient encryption scheme is designed to guarantee privacy and accuracy, and a local contribution quantization mechanism is implemented to ensure fairness. We also conduct a formal analysis, demonstrating that our scheme not only achieves convergence, fairness, low overhead, and gradient security but also perfectly resists anti-collusion attacks launched by multiple malicious entities. Extensive experiments on MNIST and GTSRB datasets demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly improves privacy and fairness in practice.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Silent-App-Aware Federated Machine Unlearning for Encrypted Network Traffic Classification
papers.abstract: In recent years, federated learning-based network traffic classification has emerged as a promising Artificial Intelligence (AI) approach for encrypted traffic identification, enabling accurate classification while preserving data privacy. To meet the rising demand for the right to be forgotten, Federated Machine Unlearning (FMU) has been introduced as an AI-driven forget ting paradigm. However, conventional FMU methods overlook silent applications removed due to guideline violations, resulting in reduced classifier stability and limited aggregation scalability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes FedUnSilApp, short for FMU for silent applications, a novel FMU framework that integrates a learning module, a forgetting module, and a scalable aggregation strategy. In particular, the forgetting module prunes neurons associated with silent applications in the classifier, minimizing their residual influence. The scalable aggregation strategy separately processes discriminative layers of clients requesting forgetting and those of other clients, thereby enhancing both stability and scalability of the global model. In addition, FedUnSilApp is applied to the real-world scenario of encrypted network traffic classification, enabling compliance with deletion requests while maintaining robust classification performance. The effectiveness of FedUnSilApp is validated through experiments, which show that FedUnSilApp outperforms state-of-the-art methods, improving accuracy by over 6% on the NJUPT dataset.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: FLAIR: Federated Learning via Adaptive Influence and Resource Coordination
papers.abstract: Adaptive video streaming (also known as adaptive bitrate or ABR streaming) must intelligently balance competing Quality of Experience (QoE) factors-video quality, rebuffering, and smooth playback-under widely varying network conditions. Traditional learning-based ABR algorithms struggle to generalize across users' diverse network environments and QoE preferences [21] [22]. Generic federated learning (FL) approaches, on the other hand, often suffer in this setting due to client heterogeneity (network speeds, device capabilities) and multi-faceted QoE objectives that standard FL algorithms do not explicitly optimize. In this work, we propose FLAIR, a Federated Learning-based framework that employs Adaptive Influence and Resource Coordination for video streaming. FLAIR holistically addresses the challenges of training a global ABR policy model across many users without collecting their data. It introduces: (1) QoE-weighted model aggregation to prioritize updates from clients in critical streaming conditions, (2) influence-guided client selection via an influence matrix that identifies clients most impactful to improving global QoE, and (3) entropy-based scheduling of workload to dynamically include clients with novel or changing network conditions. We integrate a new Influence-Entropy-Diversity (IED) metric directly into FLAIR's optimization objective and convergence analysis, proving it can accelerate convergence by reducing gradient variance. Extensive experiments on both real- world streaming traces and large-scale synthetic scenarios demonstrate that FLAIR significantly improves average QoE (e.g., higher video quality and fewer stalls) compared to conventional federated training and state-of-the-art methods. Notably, FLAIR's global model adapts swiftly to network shifts (such as WiFi-to-cellular handoffs) and scales to thousands of clients, indicating its practical deployability for internet-wide adaptive streaming.

papers.title: FedAIM: Graph-Driven Scheduling for Concurrent Asynchronous Federated Learning in Computing Power Networks
papers.abstract: Asynchronous federated learning (AFL) faces multi-job scheduling challenges in computational power networks (CPNs). In large-scale CPN environments, the decision space is prohibitively large, and it is challenging to extract critical scheduling information. This leads to asynchronous jobs contending for computing and communication resources, which affects the staleness of local models and results in degraded training efficiency.To address these issues, we propose FedAIM, a graph-driven scheduling framework for multi-job AFL in CPNs. FedAIM encodes the system state into computation, communication, and staleness views to capture the interdependence between jobs and computing nodes in resource scheduling and model optimization, and leverages reinforcement learning for job scheduling. It combines two key components: a Mixture-of-Views Router (MoV-R), which applies context-aware gating across multiple graphs to generate lightweight representations that filter redundancy while preserving interference-critical signals; and an asymmetric Actor–Critic scheduler, where the Actor exploits MoV-R features for low-latency job–device allocation and the Critic integrates a global view for long-term evaluation. Experiments on large-scale simulations and a 50-node Raspberry Pi testbed show that FedAIM improves accuracy by 13–19%, reduces communication by 43%, and lowers computation cost by 45%, achieving a favorable trade-off between learning quality and system efficiency.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Differential Privacy Fusion Filtering for Multirate Nonlinear Systems Over SNR-Based Sensor Networks: A Second-Order Center Difference Approach
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on the differential privacy fusion filtering problem for multi-rate nonlinear systems over sensor networks based on signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), in which a compensation strategy with a single exponential smoothing method is employed to handle the multiple time series stemmed from the multi-rate sampling strategy. Considering the inherent vulnerabilities of the SNR-based sensor networks, packet dropouts and eavesdropping attacks may occur during the measurement transmission between adjacent nodes, where the probability of packet dropouts varies with the SNR. In order to prevent potential eavesdroppers from inferring system states through measurement signals and causing sensitive information leakage, the transmitted measurement signals are disturbed with random noises. On this basis, the differential privacy is introduced as a performance metric to evaluate the protection level, and the perturbation noises are designed with the help of privacy parameters and measurement matrices. Firstly, a second-order center difference approach is exploited to deal with the nonlinear function. Subsequently, the upper bound on the local filtering error covariance is obtained by solving the matrix difference equation, and the local filtering algorithm is designed by minimizing the upper bound. Then, the federated fusion criterion is utilized to further improve the estimation accuracy of local filters, and the filtering performance is analyzed from the perspective of monotonicity. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm is illustrated through the simulation of induction machines with comparative experiments.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems

papers.title: Curated Collaborative AI Edge With Network Data Analytics for B5G/6G Radio Access Networks
papers.abstract: Despite advancements, Radio Access Networks (RAN) still account for over 50% of the total power consumption in 5G networks. Existing RAN split options do not fully harness data potential, presenting an opportunity to reduce operational expenditures. This paper aims to reduce energy consumption and operational costs in 5G RANs by effectively leveraging network data through two key contributions. First, a Curated Collaborative Learning (CCL) framework that ensures selective collaboration among correlated data sources for accurate traffic and user count forecasting. CCL optimally determines whom, when, and what to collaborate with, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art approaches, including global, federated, personalized federated, and cyclic institutional incremental learnings by 43.9%, 39.1%, 40.8%, and 31.35%, respectively. Second, the Distributed Unit Pooling Scheme (DUPS) is proposed, leveraging deep reinforcement learning and prediction inferences from CCL to reduce the number of active DU servers efficiently. DUPS dynamically redirects traffic from underutilized DU servers to optimize resource utilization. This improves energy efficiency by up to 89% over conventional strategies, where all DU servers remain turned on regardless of load, thereby translating into substantial monetary benefits for operators. By integrating CCL-driven predictions with DUPS, this paper demonstrates a transformative approach for minimizing energy consumption and operational costs in next-generation mobile networks, significantly enhancing efficiency and cost-effectiveness.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: ARRANGE: A Secure Decentralized Federated Learning Framework for Heterogeneous LEO Satellite Constellation
papers.abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations play an increasingly vital role in Earth observation and data-driven applications. However, traditional centralized processing frameworks are hindered by limited downlink bandwidth and high satellite mobility, making real-time and large-scale data transmission inefficient. To tackle these challenges, we propose ARRANGE,AsecuRe and decentRalized FederAted LearNing framework specifically designed for heteroGeneous LEO satellite ConstEllation. ARRANGE enables inter-satellite task offloading and decentralized model aggregation, while incorporating symmetric and asymmetric encryption to ensure data security and integrity during transmission. To address the straggler effect and data heterogeneity, we introduce an improved Genetic Algorithm (GA) that optimizes task scheduling across satellites with varying resources and institutional affiliations. Simulation results on real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate that ARRANGE significantly reduces system delay and improves model accuracy compared to existing FL strategies. This work provides a scalable and secure solution for enabling on-orbit collaborative intelligence in dynamic satellite environments.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Federated Spiking Network Framework for Spectrum Access Prediction in Interweave Cognitive Communications
papers.abstract: This paper presents FeSAP, a Federated Spiking Adaptive Prediction framework for opportunistic spectrum access in distributed Cognitive Radio Networks (CRNs). FeSAP integrates a Recurrent Temporal Network (RTN), trained using unsupervised Spike-Timing Dependent Plasticity (STDP), with a Feedforward Spectral Network (FSN), trained locally at each Secondary User (SU) via supervised learning using surrogate gradients with Batch Normalization Through Time (BNTT) and globally aggregated at the Fusion Center (FC) using Federated Averaging (FedAvg). This hybrid spiking architecture enables anticipatory prediction of Primary User (PU) activity while addressing key challenges in federated learning, including data heterogeneity, intermittent SU participation, and privacy constraints. Evaluations on 5G Non-Standalone (NSA) downlink transmission data with Long-Term Evolution (LTE) resource reservations, as well as synthetically constructed non-Independent and Identically Distributed (non-IID) scenarios, demonstrate that FeSAP achieves an F1 score of 87.95%, full utilization of all 13 symbols per subframe, and convergence within 25–30 global rounds with only 60–80% SU participation. Temporal offset analysis further confirms its robustness when operating with delayed subframe inputs, while its low parameter count and modest computational footprint underscore its suitability for deployment in edge-based CRNs with limited processing resources.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Cluster Selection for Network-Layer Performance Guarantee in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a privacy-preserving technique that enables local model training on devices without raw data sharing. However, a critical challenge in FL lies in the communication requirement of uploading the trained models to servers, which can be hindered by interference from ambient devices, particularly in unreliable wireless environments. To address this, hierarchical FL (HFL) introduces an additional intermediate layer where the edge server performs work aggregation from the devices nearby, aiming at reducing the communication load and improving the efficiency of model training. However, existing approaches suffer from two critical limitations. First, they fail to fully quantify the impact of device competition-induced interference on transmission performance, which leads to unacceptably high upload latency and low success upload probability (SUP). Second, they lack a targeted optimization strategy to balance model accuracy and transmission efficiency under dynamic interference conditions. To address these critical limitations and mitigate their adverse impacts on FL performance, we take these gaps as the core motivation of our work and propose a targeted solution. Specifically, we first model the network as a two-layer binomial point process (BPP), which allows us to analyze the network-layer performance and calculate the SUP for the trained model. Based on this model, we propose optimizing cluster selection to balance accuracy and latency, thereby enhancing overall FL performance. We formulate this optimization as a Markov decision process (MDP) and solve it using a twin-delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3)-based cluster selection algorithm (CS-TD3). In addition, to guarantee network-layer performance and enhance the efficiency of HFL, we employ an experimental exhaustive search algorithm to find the best solution within a limited range. The experimental results show that our algorithm overperforms other commonly-used algorithms in terms of HFL accuracy and model transmission latency, achieving a 10.95% improvement over the other methods.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: GOF-Based DMI Integrated Solution to Seamless Navigation for Autonomous Vehicles During GNSS Outages
papers.abstract: Autonomous vehicles rely on the integration of inertial navigation system (INS) and global navigation satellite system (GNSS) for most transportation applications. However, GNSS signals are often degraded in challenging environments such as urban canyons and tunnels, etc. To achieve seamless navigation with continuity and safety, it is necessary to deploy an auxiliary or backup navigation system that does not rely on GNSS. This paper proposes a Dual Micro-electro-mechanical INS (DMI) architecture comprising both rotating and fixed inertial measurement units (IMUs), and utilizes vehicle chassis information to aid the INS during GNSS outages. In terms of multi-sensor fusion, traditional optimal multi-sensor fusion takes the Centralized Kalman Filter (CKF) as a global optimal criterion. The Decentralized Kalman Filter (DKF), such as the well-known Federated Kalman Filter (FKF), aims to achieve the same accuracy as a CKF, while reducing the computational load. This paper innovatively applies an improved decentralized filtering method - Global Optimal Filter (GOF), and develops a GOF-based DMI integrated solution. This solution optimizes state estimation by fully utilizing multi-source data through spatial projection and orthogonalization. The field test results have demonstrated the GOF-based DMI integrated solution has significant advantages in most evaluation metrics. Specifically, it achieves accuracy improvements of 29.1% in position, 30% in velocity, 22.2% in attitude, and 58.3% in heading over the CKF-based DMI integrated solution. Compared to the FKF-based DMI integrated solution, the accuracy improvements are even more substantial: 70.4% in position, 36.3% in velocity, 70.5% in horizontal attitude, and 72.5% in heading. In addition, the introduction of extended KITTI evaluation metrics also indicates that the GOF-based DMI integration solution has significant advantages compared to the other two solutions.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Client Selection for Federated Learning With Unknown Channel State
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: Blockchain-Enabled Incentive Mechanism for Federated Learning: A Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient Approach
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: Designing Federated Learning Marketplaces: Incentives, Network Dynamics, and Decentralized Learning
papers.abstract: Federated Learning enables collaborative model training across distributed clients without requiring direct access to their private data. However, effective deployment faces critical challenges, including heterogeneous data quality, unbalanced participation, and the lack of incentives. In this paper, we propose a federated learning network structured as a decentralized marketplace, where clients are financially rewarded based on the quality and utility of their contributions. Our framework enhances client selection through utility-driven mechanisms and offers strong incentives that promote sustained, high-quality participation. It also ensures security and transparency for the Task Owner while maintaining data privacy. The architecture can support a wide range of collaborative scenarios; spanning from healthcare and finance to consumer applications; where data privacy, fairness, and scalability are paramount. We demonstrate the practicality and effectiveness of our approach through experiments, showcasing improved global model accuracy, and equitable participation.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Toward Efficient Zero-Trust Space–Air–Ground Integrated Networks via Federated Reinforcement Learning With Blockchain
papers.abstract: As global demand for efficient network services increases, the limitations of traditional terrestrial wireless networks are becoming more apparent. Space-air-ground integrated networks (SAGIN) have emerged as a promising solution to advance next-generation network infrastructure. However, SAGIN faces significant security challenges—including the lack of a robust security architecture, trust and data reliability issues in multi-hop transmissions, and the need to enhance network performance without compromising security—rendering traditional boundary-based defenses inadequate. Therefore, we propose SECURELINK, a decentralized zero-trust architecture tailored for SAGIN, which replaces traditional perimeter defenses with a ”never trust, always verify” approach. This approach strengthens network security and flexibility through continuous verification and adherence to the principle of least privilege. SECURELINK integrates blockchain technology to establish a multi-layered security verification and data processing scheme, addressing the dynamic and decentralized features of SAGIN. Additionally, we introduce DFRIO, a zero-trust traffic offloading method based on decentralized federated reinforcement learning and blockchain, designed to enhance network performance within maintaining security. Simulation results demonstrate that our solution significantly enhances SAGIN’s defense capability without compromising network stability, outperforming the two baseline schemes by 18.3% and 42.6%, respectively.

papers.title: Federated Learning With Layer-Wise Gap for Cyber-Physical-Social Systems in Internet of Vehicles
papers.abstract: Cyber–physical–social systems (CPSS) enabled Internet of Vehicles (IoV) couples cyber computation with physical traffic dynamics and social driving behaviors, resulting in geographically distributed and privacy-sensitive data across vehicles and roadside infrastructures. Federated learning (FL) provides a natural paradigm for learning shared models without centralizing raw data. However, deploying FL in CPSS-oriented IoV remains challenging due to highly non-IID and time-varying data across regions and devices, which exacerbates client drift and degrades generalization to unseen traffic conditions. To address these issues, we propose FL based on layer-wise gaps (FLLG). In contrast to conventional model-level aggregation, FLLG decomposes the model into layers and incorporates the layer-wise discrepancies between local and global models into the computation of aggregation weights, enabling more faithful weighting of client contributions under severe heterogeneity. Moreover, FLLG introduces a gap-based regularization term to dynamically adjust client weights across rounds, further improving cross-domain generalization. Extensive experiments show that FLLG consistently improves performance over representative baselines, including FedBN, MOON, and FedDG, with gains of up to 9% in the most favorable settings, while requiring no additional information beyond standard model updates. In addition, FLLG can be combined with these methods as a plug-in aggregation module, yielding further accuracy improvements of approximately 3% to 8%, which supports its applicability to CPSS-enabled IoV scenarios.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems

papers.title: Energy-Efficient Quantum Federated Learning Over Low-Altitude UAV Networks With Theoretical Guarantees
papers.abstract: This paper studies a novel energy-efficient quantum federated learning (QFL) framework designed for low-altitude quantum-enabled unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks. We develop a novel energy minimization problem by jointly considering UAV’s quantum computing power, computational frequency, transmit power, number of quantum noise measurements, and trajectory. The energy minimization problem we formulate is inherently non-convex and cannot be efficiently solved using conventional convex optimization methods in its original form. To overcome this challenge, we develop an iterative optimization approach that integrates block coordinate descent (BCD) with successive convex approximation (SCA) techniques to effectively find optimal solutions for QFL’s energy optimization. Moreover, we conduct a holistic convergence analysis of federated quantum model training, which reveals the important trade-off between the convergence rate and number of quantum noise measurements. Evaluations under different data settings demonstrate that our theoretical results are consistent with QFL model training simulations, thereby facilitating future QFL algorithm design. Extensive simulation results also show that our optimization methodology significantly improves energy efficiency over baseline methods.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: FedScope—Federated Host Embeddings From Telescope Traffic: Design and Implementation
papers.abstract: network telescope is a range of IP addresses that host no services. Millions of bots and scanners contact it to look for vulnerable systems, and the traffic it exposes is fundamental to understanding malicious activities. The visibility a telescope offers depends on its size and geolocation, and merging the information from multiple telescopes could help increase visibility and uncover more malicious activities. However, sharing raw telescope data is complicated, calling for solutions that allow one to directly share the knowledge rather than the data obtained from multiple deployments. In this paper, we explore the application of Federated Learning (FL) to create and share such global knowledge from the malicious activities seen in distributed telescopes. For that, we introduce FedScope, an FL-based solution for generatinghost embeddingsin a distributed way. We compare FedScope to local and distributed alternatives in downstream tasks, such as sender classification or coordinated activities detection. We show that FedScope (i) produces embeddings of equal or higher quality than those of a single telescope; (ii) increases coverage, allowing the global model to monitor more malicious actors; (iii) avoids the sharing of the raw data, limiting exchanged data.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: Differentially Private Personalized Federated Learning Based on Parameter Partitioning
papers.abstract: Differentially Private Personalized Federated Learning (DP-PFL) aims to address client data heterogeneity while providing formal privacy guarantees; however, most existing methods rely on static parameter partitioning and uniform privacy protection, ignoring parameter-level differences in personalization relevance and sensitivity, which often leads to excessive noise injection, unstable optimization, and degraded performance under heterogeneous (non-IID) data distributions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a posterior-inspired personalized federated learning framework that jointly models parameter uncertainty, personalization structure, and differential privacy. By leveraging temporal parameter dynamics, we construct an uncertainty-aware posterior surrogate that enables dynamic partitioning of model parameters into shared and personalized parameter subsets, without performing explicit Bayesian posterior inference. Based on this partitioning, we further introduce an adaptive clipping mechanism and a differentiated differential privacy strategy that assigns distinct noise levels to shared and personalized parameters under a single client-level privacy budget according to their sensitivity profiles, achieving a fine-grained privacy–utility trade-off. We provide a formal privacy analysis and convergence guarantee, showing that parameter partitioning with differentiated noise allocation under a single client-level privacy budget yields a tighter noise-induced error bound than uniform DP mechanisms. Extensive experiments on FEMNIST, SVHN, MNIST, and CIFAR-10 demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently achieves higher accuracy, faster convergence, and stronger robustness than state-of-the-art DP-PFL baselines, particularly in highly non-IID settings.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: TNT: Breaking the Privacy Barrier of Federated Learning via Targeted Neuron Stimulation
papers.abstract: Federated learning supports decentralized model training while preserving user privacy, yet shared gradients contain sensitive information that exposes systems to privacy attacks. Among these, data reconstruction attacks, where adversaries recover training samples from gradients, pose critical threats. However, existing methods are often limited to small batch sizes and rely on activation patterns that rarely occur naturally, reducing their practical applicability. To address these challenges, we propose a novel attack framework called Targeted Neuron Stimulation (TNT), which systematically generates adversarial perturbations during training to enforce activation patterns conducive to effective data reconstruction. TNT solves a constrained optimization problem to inject subtle, imperceptible noise into target training batches, enabling an honest-but-curious server to extract sensitive data from client gradients with high fidelity. Through extensive evaluations across five datasets, including facial recognition and medical diagnosis, TNT expands reconstructable batch sizes from 8 to realistic levels and accelerates attack processes by up to 10 times, achieving significantly higher reconstruction fidelity compared to existing methods. By exploring latent vulnerabilities in gradient-sharing mechanisms, this work highlights the privacy risks inherent to federated learning systems and calls for stronger defenses to safeguard sensitive user data.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Federated Unlearning via Representation Misdirection with Adaptive Anchor Generation
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Modality-Incomplete Multimodal Federated Recommendation With Bidirectional Modality Reconstruction
Learning-Enabled Elastic Network Topology for Distributed ISAC Service Provisioning
papers.abstract: Conventional mobile networks, including both localized cell-centric and cooperative cell-free networks (CCN/CFN), are built upon rigid network topologies. However, neither architecture is adequate to flexibly support distributed integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) services, due to the increasing difficulty of aligning spatiotemporally distributed heterogeneous service demands with available radio resources. In this paper, we propose an elastic network topology (ENT) for distributed ISAC service provisioning, where multiple co-existing localized CCNs can be dynamically aggregated into CFNs with expanded boundaries for federated network operation. This topology elastically orchestrates localized CCN and federated CFN boundaries to balance signaling overhead and distributed resource utilization, thereby enabling efficient ISAC service provisioning. A two-phase operation protocol is then developed. In Phase I, each CCN autonomously classifies ISAC services as either local or federated and partitions its resources into dedicated and shared segments. In Phase II, each CCN employs its dedicated resources for local ISAC services, while the aggregated CFN consolidates shared resources from its constituent CCNs to cooperatively deliver federated services. Furthermore, we design a utility-to-signaling ratio (USR) to quantify the tradeoff between sensing/communication utility and signaling overhead. Consequently, a USR maximization problem is formulated by jointly optimizing the network topology (i.e., service classification and CCN aggregation) and the allocation of dedicated and shared resources. However, this problem is challenging due to its distributed optimization nature and the absence of complete channel state information. To address this problem efficiently, we propose a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) framework with centralized training and decentralized execution.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Hierarchical Negotiation-Debate Framework for Privacy-Preserving Quality Enhancement in Edge Intelligence Networks
papers.abstract: Deploying high-quality AI services in 6G edge intelligence networks remains challenging due to heterogeneous node capabilities, limited resources, and strict privacy requirements. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Federated Layering Technology (FLT) framework for privacy-preserving collaborative intelligence at the network edge. The framework consists of three tightly coupled components: (1) a hierarchical model decomposition strategy that partitions a monolithic model into lightweight layer groups and assigns them to edge nodes according to their computation, memory, and communication conditions; (2) a negotiation-debate mechanism that enables trust-aware knowledge sharing and consensus formation among distributed models; and (3) a multi-layered security design that combines homomorphic encryption, adaptive differential privacy, commitment-based consistency verification, and reputation-based anomaly detection. Experiments on three benchmark datasets under both IID and non-IID settings show that increasing the collaboration scale consistently improves model accuracy, with five-model collaboration achieving the best performance among the evaluated collaborative settings while approaching the accuracy of a standalone large model at lower per-node resource cost. In our implementation, the measured per-device cumulative privacy loss is reduced by$30.9\%$under IID and by$32.8\%$under non-IID when moving from two-model to five-model collaboration. Comparative results with representative anomaly detection methods further indicate that FLT can improve the robustness of collaborative edge learning. These results demonstrate the potential of FLT as an integrated framework for resource-aware and privacy-conscious AI deployment in edge intelligence networks.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Federated Recommendation Model Based on Personalized Attention and Privacy-Preserving Dynamic Graph
papers.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have been widely adopted in recommendation systems. When integrated into a federated learning framework, GNNs can enhance the model’s expressive capability. However, challenges arise in personalized representation and graph expansion due to the heterogeneity and locality of user data in federated recommendation systems. To address these challenges, we propose a federated recommendation model based on personalized attention and privacy-preserving dynamic graphs. The method first matches neighbor users for each selected client. Subsequently, it counts the interaction frequencies of items for both local and neighbor users to construct personalized weights, which captures the unique characteristics of different users. Additionally, we designs a method for constructing privacy-preserving dynamic graphs. In each round of federated training, the selected client adds pseudo-interaction items to its own interaction subgraph, perturbing the real interactions. After completing local training, the noisy interaction subgraph is incorporated into the global graph to capture higher-order connectivity information among users while safeguarding their interaction privacy. We conduct extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets, and the results demonstrate that the proposed PADG method achieves superior performance while effectively protecting privacy.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: Federated Adapter Learning Under Energy Constraints for Generative Personalization in Consumer Electronics Networks for IoV Deployments
FedACE-Sec: A Secure Asynchronous Federated Learning Framework for Consumer Electronics with Proactive Threat Hunting
papers.abstract: Next-generation consumer electronic devices in intelligent systems are exposed to increasingly sophisticated security threats, as privacy-sensitive data distributed across numerous devices remain vulnerable to malicious attacks and compromise. Centralized data collection for anomaly detection model training is neither secure nor compliant with modern privacy regulations. To address these challenges, we propose FedACE-Sec, an asynchronous and secure federated learning framework that integrates homomorphic encryption and digital signatures. It enables consumer electronics devices to collaboratively train a global anomaly detection model while safeguarding local data privacy, and employs digital signatures to prevent malicious model updates, thereby ensuring both privacy preservation and trustworthy proactive threat detection. Moreover, the framework integrates a buffer-based asynchronous aggregation mechanism that enabling clients to disconnect immediately after uploading their updates. Experimental results on the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets show that the proposed framework provides enhanced security over the original FedCFA and improves model accuracy by 1.75%. Additionally, the framework effectively mitigates privacy leakage and malicious attacks. Ablation experiments further confirm the contribution of each component to security, efficiency, and overall model performance.

papers.title: Transformer-Enhanced Federated Learning for Secure Multimedia Task Offloading in Edge-Centric CIoT Environments
papers.abstract: Consumer Internet of Things (CIoT) devices generate large volumes of sensitive multimedia data under heterogeneous workloads, limited computational resources, and strict latency constraints. Many existing offloading approaches struggle with scalability, context awareness, and consistent privacy protection. To address these issues, we propose Transformer enhanced Federated Deep Reinforcement Learning (Fed-DRL) frameworks for context aware and secure multimedia task offloading in distributed CIoT edge networks. The first model uses Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) local agents coordinated by a centralized Transformer based global agent that learns cross agent relationships while keeping edge side overhead low. The second model introduces lightweight Transformers at both local and global levels, allowing each agent to encode multimodal system states, including task size, deadlines, link reliability, and energy levels, to support fine grained and privacy aware decisions. Both models employ federated learning so that raw multimedia data stays on the device. This preserves security by protecting data ownership, ensuring integrity without direct transmission, and limiting attack risks through compressed, sparse updates. Simulation results show that the proposed frameworks outperform conventional DRL baselines in latency, energy use, task success rate, and security preservation.

papers.title: Efficient Decentralized Federated Generative Adversarial Network Learning Over Multi-Source Heterogeneous Data
papers.abstract: We propose DHetGAN, a decentralized federated generative adversarial network (GAN) learning framework for multi-source heterogeneous data. Unlike standard decentralized federated learning for non-GAN models, DHetGAN requires each node to solve a local minimax GAN game via adversarial training of its discriminator and generator, which are then averaged in a decentralized manner to reach consensus. To address data heterogeneity across nodes, we develop a GAN-intrinsic aggregation strategy that assigns averaging weights using a privacy-preserving divergence proxy quantifying inter-node distributional divergence. The proxy is estimated locally by each node – without revealing sensitive data – from coupled discriminator-genera tor values calibrated by the neighborhood-level maximal discrimina tor confidence, specific to the minimax GAN game. To reduce communication overhead, we present a compression method tailored to DHet GAN. We theoretically analyze convergence guarantees of our frame work, demonstrating strong inter-node coupling, contracting gradient magnitudes, and uniformly bounded consensus dynamics for both discriminators and generators. We also establish a sufficient condition for full mode coverage in DHetGAN and identify practical training set tings under which this condition holds. Extensive experiments and comparisons with benchmarks show that DHetGAN achieves superior generative performance, strong stability, diversity of mode coverage, and fast convergence, while substantially reducing communication overhead, even under extreme non-i.i.d. data heterogeneity.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: FLFaaSPHE: A Lightweight Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning Framework for Serverless Computing Environments
papers.abstract: The Function as a Service (FaaS) paradigm, through abstracting cloud resource management, is regarded as the next-generation cloud computing system. Deploying Federated Learning (FL) on serverless computing platforms alleviates the burden on cloud-native application developers while reducing costs for clients. Unfortunately, due to the short lifespan and stateless nature of serverless functions, model training and aggregation tasks rely on external storage for tracking historical states. Frequent function calls have the potential to result in privacy leakage in the federated learning architecture during transmission and aggregation. Meanwhile, client heterogeneity and latency effects further impact the training efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a lightweight privacy-preserving FL architecture built on serverless computation, designated as FLFaaSPHE. Specifically, to enhance end-to-end privacy and reduce aggregation latency, FLFaaSPHE adopts Paillier-based packed homomorphic encryption, coupled with random masking and partitioning mechanisms, which enable clients to perform batch-encrypted uploads and incremental ciphertext-domain aggregation. Furthermore, to mitigate the straggler effect and balance privacy protection with convergence performance optimally, FLFaaSPHE incorporates a CountSketch-based client selection mechanism. This mechanism selects representative clients using cluster distance, sketch similarity, and historical latency. Experimental results on Amazon Web Services (AWS) demonstrate that FLFaaSPHE significantly reduces end-to-end training latency and aggregation overhead in heterogeneous and asynchronous environments. Meanwhile, it maintains model accuracy and achieves stable speedup across different datasets.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Bridging Domain Gap and Preserving Privacy for Battery Diagnosis in Data Centers
papers.abstract: Data centers, the cornerstone of the digital economy, depend on Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) systems, where battery health is critical for operational continuity. However, the practical application of data-driven anomaly detection is severely hampered by two interconnected challenges: distribution shifts between different battery batches degrade model generalization, while data silos arising from commercial and privacy constraints prevent cross-institutional data aggregation. To overcome these barriers, we systematically formulate this industrial challenge as a Federated Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (FUDA) task, which enables collaborative model training without sharing raw data. The core contribution of this paper is the proposal of a novel scenario-driven adaptation strategy, which posits that no single algorithm is universally optimal. We demonstrate that for homogeneous scenarios with small domain gaps, a lightweight discrepancy-based method (CORAL) paired with a powerful feature extractor (Transformer) is most effective. Conversely, for heterogeneous scenarios with large domain gaps, a stable, decoupled adversarial approach (ADDA) combined with a capacity-constrained feature extractor (DeeperMLP) is superior as it ensures convergence and promotes generalization. Experiments on a real-world data center dataset validate our FUDA approach (F1-score of 0.872) not only significantly outperforms local non-adapted models but also achieves performance highly comparable to, and in some cases exceeding, that of privacy-violating centralized models (0.908).

papers.title: FedCamo: Secure and Dependable Federated Learning With Model Camouflage
papers.abstract: AI driven applications are entering safety critical domains and increasingly rely on federated learning (FL) to coordinate model training across many devices. Although FL limits raw data exposure, its interactive protocol reveals updated model artifacts to curious observers, which enables gradient inversion and threatens privacy. While existing encryption and perturbation methods protect content and statistical summaries, they exhibit limited compatibility and practical deployability. More importantly, they cannot conceal protocol level behavior during communication. Moreover, current concealment methods either cannot be directly extended to FL, or focus on covert message channels without supporting a hidden model. To address these limitations, we propose a novel federated model camouflage framework that covertly embeds a recoverable secret model while preserving the typical external behavior of public FL, namely, FedCamo. First, to enable content camouflage with faithful recovery, FedCamo allocates a protected parameter subspace to the secret model and records only the minimal side information required for extraction. Second, to address cross round stability under partial parameters participation, a dual track aggregation rule applies presence weighted averaging to secret parameters and a standard average to the remaining unprotected parameter subspace. Finally, to enhance robustness under heterogeneity and auditing, a gradient inversion aware personalization procedure selects each client's stego load to balance public utility, secret recoverability, and undetectability. Experiments demonstrate that FedCamo achieves reliable latent model recovery while maintaining public utility close to the encryption baseline, and it remains compatible with existing FL components, which demonstrates strong robustness.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Prototype Margin-Based Client Selection for Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has gained significant attention as a distributed machine learning paradigm, leveraging edge clients for collaborative training while preserving data privacy. However, statistical heterogeneity, arising from diverse client data distributions, poses a significant challenge to FL performance. In this work, we propose a novel heterogeneity-aware client selection scheme based on prototype margin to mitigate these challenges. By utilizing prototype learning, we capture effective data representations, allowing client selection to better account for both data quality and distribution. The proposed scheme is designed for practical wireless communication networks, where clients are clustered and we select participants based on joint prototype margin and wireless channel. To further optimize the training process, we jointly optimize client selection and bandwidth allocation, accounting for dynamic network conditions and heterogeneous client capabilities. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly improves model accuracy and reduces communication overhead.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Blockchain-Based Secure and Efficient Federated Learning Scheme for IoMT Consumer Electronics Devices
papers.abstract: The Internet of Medical Things consumer electronics (IoMT-CE) devices integrated with deep learning (DL) model have achieved remarkable success in the medical field, which provides intelligent diagnostic assistance. However, as DL technologies evolve rapidly, a key challenge lies in how to continuously enhance the intelligent assisted diagnostic capabilities of IoMT-CE devices. Federated learning (FL), an effective distributed learning framework, holds great potential to address this issue. In this article, we propose a novel secure and efficient FL scheme for IoMT-CE devices based on consortium blockchain. In this scheme, all participating hospitals, the aggregation server (AS), and the noise parameter server (NPS) establish a consortium blockchain, where hash values and signature data are stored. Paillier homomorphic encryption (HE) and noise mechanisms are employed to protect patient privacy, while an elliptic curve cryptography-based proxy re-encryption (ECC-PRE) strategy is adopted to ensure model security between the AS and IoMT-CE devices. Furthermore, this scheme guarantees that model updates are applied correctly, even when local models cannot be uploaded to hospitals. Finally, the performance of our proposed scheme is verified. The results demonstrate that the encryption mechanisms have almost no impact on model accuracy, and the proposed scheme proves to be robust and fault-tolerant in cases of disconnection.

papers.title: Jointly optimizing global generalization and local personalization via prompt fusion for Heterogeneous Consumer Electronics
papers.abstract: The proliferation of intelligent consumer electronics necessitates a service architecture capable of delivering personalized services while protecting privacy. Federated Learning (FL), as a privacy-preserving paradigm, enables multiple consumer electronic devices to collaboratively train a model without exposing sensitive user data. However, FL performance (i.e., convergence performance, global generalization, and local personalization) is severely compromised by heterogeneous data distribution across consumer electronic devices, which is prevalent in most real-world scenarios. Prompt learning, as an efficient approach, is introduced to improve either global generalization or local personalization. They typically struggle to balance both directions, as optimizing one often leads to failure in another. To address this problem, we design a novel FL framework named PGA-FL, which fuses local and global prompts by Genetic Algorithm (GA) to update the local prompts on the clients and aggregates the uploaded local prompts based on their semantic similarity to update the global prompts on the server, to achieve a superior trade-off between the global generalization and the local personalization. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our PGA-FL framework, we theoretically prove its convergence performance and perform extensive experiments. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed PGA-FL framework can achieve superior performance in terms of convergence performance, global generalization, and local personalization with respect to other state-of-the-art baseline algorithms.

papers.title: Efficient Federated Learning in IoV: Trajectory-Aware Communication Modeling and Incentive Mechanism
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) faces key challenges such as high communication overhead, strong node heterogeneity, and highly dynamic path connectivity, which impede model convergence efficiency and system scalability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a trajectory-aware communication modeling and incentive-driven Federated Learning framework (TCM-FL). Specifically, the system extracts multi-dimensional QoS features based on real vehicle trajectories from the LuST dataset, calculates node communication trustworthiness scores using a Random Forest model, constructs a delay-weighted communication graph to support RSU-level path analysis and regional division, and introduces a joint weighting strategy considering communication quality and node contribution in the aggregation stage to enhance model training effectiveness. Additionally, a decentralized reward mechanism implemented via smart contracts encourages high-quality participation, utilizing the Gini coefficient and the standard deviation of regional contributions as fairness evaluation metrics. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms baseline schemes in terms of communication efficiency, model performance, and incentive fairness. Specifically, the classification accuracy reached 0.92, the average path length remained stable, the Gini coefficient dropped to 0.177, and regional contribution differences converged significantly. Ablation studies and baseline comparisons further verify the effectiveness and overall advantages of each core module.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Structure-Aware Local Differential Privacy for Multimodal Collaborative Inference in Federated Learning Systems
papers.abstract: Cloud-edge collaborative inference (CI) in federated learning systems for multimodal tasks exposes intermediate features to potential reconstruction attacks. Local differential privacy (LDP), as a widely used privacy-preserving paradigm, has emerged as a practical defense for collaborative inference. Nevertheless, most existing LDP-based methods inject uniform noise across modalities, without accounting for differences in task importance and privacy sensitivity, leading to a suboptimal trade off where task-critical dimensions may be over-perturbed while sensitive components remain inadequately protected. To address these issues, we propose Struct-DP, a structure-aware framework featuring two core mechanisms: (i) shared-private representation decoupling, which utilizes cross-modal correlation learning to iso late task-relevant shared semantics; and (ii) structure-aware noise injection, which adaptively distributes the noise budget based on dimension-wise privacy sensitivity and task importance scores. By allocating more noise to high-privacy, low-task subspaces, our scheme achieves a better balance between privacy protection and task utility. Extensive evaluations on two prevailing datasets (CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI) show that Struct-DP retains 98.2% of the peak task utility while increasing the reconstruction error (MSE) by approximately 7× over uniform-noise baselines.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Efficient and Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning with Gradient Control against Data Poisoning
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across decentralized clients while preserving data privacy. However, practical deployments are often limited by significant communication overhead and vulnerability to Byzantine poisoning attacks. Existing defenses typically rely on post-hoc anomaly detection, but executing complex distance metrics or clustering on encrypted, sparsified updates creates a substantial computational burden for the aggregation server. We present a privacy-preserving FL framework that addresses these challenges by integrating Top-ksparsification, non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs (NIZKPs), and homomorphic encryption. Instead of relying on expensive ciphertext distance computations, our architecture uses a pre-aggregation global mask sign vector, generated through majority voting, to filter anomalous updates. This mechanism treats unselected gradient coordinates as explicit zero-votes, which mitigates malicious coalitions attempting to manipulate disjoint parameter subsets. A local error feedback mechanism ensures that heterogeneous client updates align over successive training rounds. Combined with NIZKPs to enforce coordinate-wise magnitude bounds, the framework provides Byzantine resilience without increasing communication costs or compromising privacy. Evaluations on MNIST and CIFAR-10 show that our approach maintains high communication efficiency and robustness. Under a 40% malicious client poisoning attack and a 50% sparsification ratio, the framework achieves final accuracies of 92.14% and 63.20%, respectively, demonstrating its effectiveness in bandwidth-constrained, hostile environments.

papers.title: Mitigating Membership Inference and Model Inversion in 6G Federated Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: In sixth-generation (6G) networks, federated learning (FL) enables collaborative anomaly detection across distributed edge devices without exposing raw data; however, exchanged gradients can leak privacy via membership inference attacks (MIA) and model inversion attacks (MInvA). Meanwhile, 6G network slicing imposes heterogeneous quality-of-service (QoS) requirements across ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC), enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB), and massive machine-type communications (mMTC), where uniform defenses often incur 30–60% accuracy loss. We propose a slice-aware, defense-in-depth framework that calibrates three coordinated layers: Layer 1 statistical screening with thresholds τURLLC=4.5, τeMBB=5.0, and τmMTC=6.0; Layer 2 slice-aware differential privacy with Gaussian noise σURLLC=0.001, σeMBB=0.05, and σmMTC=0.10, where URLLC uses lightweight perturbation to preserve stringent latency while stronger formal differential privacy is concentrated in eMBB/mMTC; and Layer 3 adversarial retraining using the fast gradient sign method (FGSM). Coordinating these layers yields complementary benefits: screening reduces attack surface, differential privacy masks leakage, and adversarial retraining hardens models. Experiments on CICIDS2017 and N-BaIoT show 95.2% utility retention with 82.15% accuracy, a +16.7% macro-F1 improvement, 91–94% communication reduction, MIA success reduced from 78.3% to 52.1%, model inversion error increased by 34.7%, and an overall privacy accounting budget total≤2.1.

papers.title: BFLS-APIA: A Blockchain-based Federated Learning Scheme Against Poisoning and Inference Attacks for Resource-Limited Consumer Electronics
papers.abstract: Consumer electronics (CE) devices generate privacy-sensitive data while operating under limited computation, memory, and energy budgets. Federated learning (FL) reduces raw-data transmission, but CE-oriented FL must address poisoned updates, update exposure, and cross-organization accountability without placing heavy security functions on terminals. We propose BFLS-APIA, a blockchain-assisted FL scheme based on a cost- and trust-aware placement of security functions. At the intra-organization edge level, an edge gateway performs lightweight Euclidean distance-based screening to reduce the propagation of suspicious updates. During inter-organization collaboration, Shamir secret sharing, encoded homomorphic aggregation, and round-level key management are combined to protect update confidentiality under the stated threat model. At the cross-organization level, a permissioned blockchain records training metadata and encrypted model records as provenance evidence, while computation-intensive operations remain off-chain. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST under label-flipping poisoning attacks and non-IID data partitions show that BFLS-APIA maintains model utility. Under the evaluated settings, it improves test accuracy by 0.47% and 0.82% over the strongest evaluated baselines.

papers.title: LGFR: Towards Lightweight and Gradient-Optimized Federated Recommendation for Consumer Devices
papers.abstract: Federated Recommender Systems (FRS) offer personalized recommendations while preserving user privacy, yet their deployment on consumer edge devices remains challenging due to efficiency demands. Existing methods often rely on oversimplified interaction models and suboptimal objectives that neglect user and item biases or fail to optimize for ranking. To address these challenges, we propose a Lightweight and Gradient-optimized Federated Recommendation (LGFR) framework. This approach establishes an efficient gradient-based paradigm for binary representation learning, enabling more flexible and effective model updates. The framework incorporates several key enhancements: first, learnable user and item bias terms are introduced to better capture intrinsic preferences; second, a synergistic hybrid loss function combines pair-wise ranking with point-wise reconstruction, explicitly optimizing for Top-N recommendation performance; finally, an efficient hard negative sampling strategy is employed to enhance discriminative capability and accelerate training convergence. Extensive experiments on three public benchmarks, Filmtrust, Ciao, and ML-1M, demonstrate the superiority of our framework. LGFR outperforms competing federated baselines with an improvement of up to 3.5% in NDCG@10 on Filmtrust. Moreover, it fully preserves lightweight properties in storage, communication, and inference, proving highly practical for consumer electronics recommendations.

papers.title: CausShield: Sample Reconstruction-Resilient Vertical FL Via Causal Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Vertical federated learning (VFL) is a distributed learning paradigm that leverages vertically partitioned features across isolated parties without sharing raw samples; however, it remains vulnerable to active sample reconstruction attacks. Existing defenses fail to achieve a satisfactory trade-off between model utility and privacy protection, due to either suppressing task-relevant information alongside privacy-sensitive features or relying on end-to-end supervised training to converge the defense module, which exposes the model to early-epoch vulnerability. To address this challenge, we adopt a structural causal model (SCM) insight and construct CausShield. From a task-learning standpoint, causal features within a raw sample are those that are directly relevant and contributory to the learning objective, whereas non-causal features are task-irrelevant but often encode sample-specific private information, thereby facilitating reconstruction. Importantly, we lay a theoretical foundation to prove this insight. CausShield thus decomposes the shared representations between the client and the coordinating server in VFL into task-relevant and task-irrelevant components to ensure full-cycle privacy protection. Nonetheless, the decomposition is inherently challenging due to the dual objectives of preserving model utility while mitigating privacy leakage. We address this via a carefully formulated optimization problem, which is solved through unsupervised representation learning. We further theoretically prove that CausShield preserves the convergence behavior of standard VFL. Extensive experiments compare CausShield against seven SOTAs, including InvL (USENIX Security'25), and evaluate robustness against advanced reconstruction attacks such as URVFL (NDSS'25). Results demonstrate that CausShield consistently outperforms in privacy protection, model utility, and computational efficiency.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Private Metadata-Driven Retrieval-Augmented Reconstruction for Missing Modalities in Multimodal Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Multimodal federated learning (MFL) enables clients with distributed multimodal data to collaboratively train models while preserving privacy, and has been widely used in multi-domain IoT and blockchain-enabled applications where clients collect heterogeneous data such as images, text, and sensor signals. A key challenge is missing modalities, i.e., only some samples have all modalities (i.e., aligned) while many samples lack one or more modalities. Existing reconstruction-based methods usually rely on scarce aligned samples or dispersed global semantic cues, but data heterogeneity and privacy constraints make such global cues difficult to retrieve and exploit effectively. We proposePRAR, which decouples learning into metadata prototype retrieval and prototype-augmented reconstruction. For retrieval, each client summarizes local missing-modality embeddings into compact metadata prototypes and perturbs them via the Gaussian mechanism. The noisy prototypes form a differentially private global metadata prototype pool, whose metadata records support access control and semantic top-$K$retrieval. For reconstruction, we train a prototype-augmented reconstructor that combines aligned supervision with retrieved metadata prototypes through a residual structure. We provide privacy and utility guarantees for retrieval, and show that the residual design minimizes the mean squared error (MSE) for missing-modality reconstruction. Experiments on four multimodal datasets against five strong baselines show thatPRARimproves cross-modal retrieval and multimodal classification by an average of 4.77% and 6.07% over the strongest baseline.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Proactive Federated Anomaly Detection in Consumer Electronic Ecosystems via Adaptive Learning and Lightweight Auditability
papers.abstract: Consumer electronic ecosystems, such as smart vehicles, wearable devices, connected homes, and Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled transportation systems, face increasing cyber threats, privacy risks, and reliability challenges. Although federated learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving collaborative training, its deployment in such environments is still hindered by statistical heterogeneity, hyperparameter sensitivity, and limited training auditability. This paper proposes SABFL, a federated intrusion detection framework for consumer electronic ecosystems. It combines FedProx-based local training, online simulated annealing for adaptive hyperparameter tuning, and lightweight blockchain-assisted audit logging. The framework improves convergence stability under heterogeneous data and provides traceable training records with low additional overhead. Experimental results on the CICIDS2017 dataset show that SABFL achieves performance comparable to existing methods under IID conditions, while yielding significantly stronger robustness under non-IID scenarios. In highly heterogeneous settings, SABFL improves the Macro-F1 score by up to 20.58% compared with standard federated baselines, and outperforms the advanced FedNova approach by 16.43%. These results demonstrate the practicality of SABFL for proactive intrusion detection in distributed consumer electronic environments.

papers.title: Robust and Explainable Federated Learning via Semantic Concept Bottlenecks: A Security-Enhanced Approach
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across decentralized data sources while preserving user privacy. However, its practical deployment is hindered by the opaque black-box nature of deep neural networks and significant vulnerabilities to malicious attacks. Specifically, in Non- Independent and Identically Distributed (Non-IID) scenarios, distinguishing between benign data heterogeneity and malicious model updates remains a critical challenge due to the lack of semantic insight into parameter changes. To address these issues, this paper proposes Explainable Federated Concept Learning (XFedCL), a framework that leverages model interpretability to enhance system robustness. Unlike traditional FL approaches that aggregate opaque gradients, XFedCL employs client-side Bottleneck Concept Learners to extract human-understandable visual concepts. Clients transmit concept-class co-occurrence scores to the server, enabling a semantic-level aggregation process. This transparency allows the server to identify and mitigate malicious outliers based on semantic consistency, effectively defending against poisoning attacks. Extensive experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CUB200 datasets demonstrate that XFedCL delivers clear explanations for classification decisions and achieves competitive clean-data accuracy while significantly outperforming standard FL baselines under non-adaptive poisoning attacks, offering an explicit trade-off among robustness, interpretability, and communication efficiency.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: SepFPL: Structural Entropy Enhanced Privacy Preserving Personalized Federated Prompt Learning
papers.abstract: The deployment of Multimodal Large Language Models in Federated Learning has accelerated Federated Prompt Learning (FPL) as a parameter-efficient tuning paradigm. However, heterogeneous client data make it difficult to simultaneously achieve personalization, cross-client generalization, and privacy protection under strict privacy and communication constraints. To address this trilemma, we proposeSepFPL, a structural-entropy-enhanced privacy-preserving personalized FPL framework.SepFPLdecomposes prompts into global, cluster-level, and local components to separate common, community-specific, and client-specific knowledge. For local prompts, it adopts a hybrid low-rank-plus-residual parameterization that preserves dominant task semantics while retaining long-tail personalization under privacy noise. At the aggregation level,SepFPLconstructs a dynamic collaboration graph from cluster-level gradient trajectories and applies two-dimensional structural entropy minimization to discover hierarchical communities, enabling structure-aware knowledge routing and bi-level aggregation. For privacy,SepFPLuses on-device Gaussian randomization for client-resident local updates, which are not externally released, and applies centralized differential privacy to shared prompts through client-side clipping and server-side noise injection. A time-adaptive budget scheduler further anneals noise intensity to improve convergence. Theoretical analysis bounds cumulative privacy loss via Rényi Differential Privacy. Extensive experiments on multiple visual benchmarks show thatSepFPLconsistently outperforms representative baselines in personalization accuracy, generalization, and privacy robustness under identical or stricter privacy budgets, thereby providing a unified solution to the personalization-generalization-privacy trade-off in federated prompt learning.

papers.title: Evolutionary Federated Learning Resource Allocation Optimization for Medical Consumer Electronics
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving model training for medical consumer electronics (CE) devices, such as wearable sensors, smartphones, and home health monitoring terminals. However, large-scale heterogeneous device resources and Non-IID medical data may bias FL resource scheduling toward resource-rich or data-rich clients, resulting in cross-device service inconsistency, long aggregation delay, and high energy consumption. To address this problem, this paper proposes a medical-CE-oriented FL resource allocation framework for cross-device service consistency. Under a fixed per-round client participation budget, the framework jointly optimizes client selection, local processor frequency, and transmission power. The resource allocation task is formulated as a large-scale four-objective optimization problem, where global model accuracy, model accuracy variance, aggregation delay, and energy consumption are optimized simultaneously, with model accuracy variance used to characterize cross-device service consistency. To solve this problem, a large-scale multi-objective evolutionary algorithm based on fuzzy grouping (LSMOEA/FG) is developed to identify convergence-sensitive and diversity-sensitive variables and optimize them cooperatively. Experimental results show that FL based on LSMOEA/FG improves global model accuracy by 5.83% on average and reduces model accuracy variance, aggregation delay, and energy consumption by 17.22%, 23.01%, and 8.02%, respectively, compared with five state-of-the-art evolutionary methods.

papers.title: FedCF: A Unified Federated Learning-driven Edge Intelligence Framework for Cell-Free Massive MIMO
papers.abstract: Cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF mMIMO) has emerged as a potential technology for 6G. Through coordinated transmission by distributed access points (APs), it significantly enhances system coverage and throughput. However, this distributed architecture results in highly fragmented network states, hindering the further development of CF mMIMO toward the convergence of computation and communication. Specifically, it becomes challenging to train and deploy centralized AI within CF mMIMO to achieve intrinsic intelligence such as resource scheduling, AP selection, or to provide AI-enabled services to users. Therefore, we propose FedCF, a unified federated learning (FL)-driven edge intelligence framework tailored for CF mMIMO. This architecture employs central processing units across multiple edge CF mMIMO as training nodes for efficient, collaborative FL training. It empowers APs as intelligent edge nodes to deploy the trained global model, thereby achieving low-latency, high-efficiency service delivery and fostering the intelligent transformation of CF mMIMO through AI enablement. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to conventional approaches, FedCF exhibits significant advantages in both model convergence and inference service latency.

papers.title: Decentralized Federated Learning for Consumer Electronics in Smart Healthcare Service Systems with Performance Guarantees
papers.abstract: Emerging smart healthcare service systems (SHSS) leverage the Internet of Things and artificial intelligence techniques to improve the quality and efficiency of medical services for consumers. To make the underlying processes explicit, this paper develops and analyzes an SHSS service blueprint that systematically characterizes the care pathway and highlights the importance of cross-institutional collaborative training for strengthening medical decision support. Although SHSS cannot centrally aggregate medical data, classical federated learning (FL) still relies on a single trusted aggregation server. To overcome this limitation, a decentralized SHSS collaboration architecture based on decentralized federated learning (DFL) is proposed, where hospitals constitute the physical layer and are modeled as clients at the network layer. In this architecture, each client trains a local deep model and exchanges only differential-privacy-protected model information with its neighbors. On top of this architecture, a differentially private zeroth-order DFL algorithm, termed DODFL, is proposed. DODFL integrates a one-point residual-feedback (OPRF) zeroth-order gradient estimator with Laplace-perturbed message passing, and is shown to satisfy ϵ differential privacy (DP) and achieve a convergence rate ofO(1/t) for ρ-weakly convex objectives via the Moreau envelope. Experiments on four real-world medical image datasets under non-IID partitioning further validate the effectiveness of DODFL for privacy-preserving SHSS collaboration, achieving accuracies of 98.67 ± 0.06 on Brain Tumor, 84.76 ± 0.25 on Alzheimer, 99.31 ± 0.19 on Monkeypox, and 81.26 ± 0.62 on Skin Cancer.

papers.title: Data Re-valuation in Vertical Federated Learning with Importance Sampling: A Case Study in Blockchain
papers.abstract: Vertical federated learning (VFL) enables multiple parties with vertically partitioned data to collaboratively train machine learning models while preserving privacy. In blockchain-enabled collaborative learning systems, contribution scores may further be recorded or executed through smart contracts for incentive allocation and governance. A central challenge in such systems is how to fairly and efficiently re-evaluate each client's data contribution when client-side feature data change over time. Moreover, clients may update or withdraw data over time (e.g., data deletion requests under privacy laws or dataset updates for business reasons), creating dynamic changes that complicate accurate contribution assessment. Existing approaches, which typically rely on full retraining or uniform sampling methods, suffer from prohibitively high computational costs and can fail to capture data dynamics accurately. To address these challenges, we propose Data Re-valuation in Vertical Federated Learning with Importance Sampling (WISR, short forWeightedImportanceSampling forRe-valuation), a novel VFL re-valuation algorithm based on weighted sampling under dynamic data updates. WISR introduces two core innovations:mutual-information-driven weightingwhich allocates resources to clients whose data updates most impact the joint model, andweighted importance samplingwhich allocates priority to coalitions that contain more updated clients to improve sampling efficiency. For changed clients estimated through importance sampling, we provide an unbiasedness analysis under the specified proposal distribution, while historical reuse and fusion are used as practical stabilizers under limited budgets. Experiments on six real-world datasets show that WISR reduces estimation error by up to14×and achieves up to9.17×speedup over state-of-the-art baselines, while maintaining high-fidelity contribution assessments.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: pFedVIReID: Personalized Federated Learning for VI-ReID With Decoupled Local and Global Tuning
papers.abstract: In Visible-Infrared Person Re-Identification (VIReID) model, centralized training paradigm can cause privacy leakage issues and further significant social impact. Previous federated ReID frameworks for privacy protection struggle with heterogeneity across VI-ReID clients. Therefore, we propose the first personalized federated learning method (pFL) for VI-ReID, which focuses on optimizing the performance under heterogeneous paradigm. Existing general pFL methods cannot fully account for the distinct roles of global and local components in both architectural design and training procedures.
