To address these challenges, pFedVIReID adopts distinct architectures for the global and personalized parts of the model and introduces a Global-Local Alternating Optimization Strategy (GLAO) for training. pFedVIReID adopts light-weight non-local attentionbased adapters as local components, which are inserted into intermediate layers of large global backbone to select global features relevant to specific local clients. The GLAO strategy decouples the training of local and global components and applies distinct optimization objectives. Specifically, the global model is trained with an additional distribution-alignment regularization term, guided by a teacher model maintained via exponential moving average. Extensive experiments in both modality-complete and modality-heterogeneous settings demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms the leading federated learning ReID (FL-ReID) and personalized Federated Learning (pFL) methods. In particular, pFedVIReID achieves average improvements of 6.76% in Rank-1 accuracy and 7.42% in mAP, respectively. And results from three datasets show that, after fine-tuning, our federated models achieve comparable or even higher accuracy than solely trained models without federated learning (Standalone training), demonstrating that our pFedVIReID is meaningful for clients.

papers.title: Proactive Threat Hunting and Anomaly Detection in Intelligent Green Transportation: A Federated Edge-AI Framework for In-Vehicle Consumer Networks
papers.abstract: Connected consumer vehicles are central to next-generation intelligent transportation systems, yet face significant cybersecurity threats targeting their internal networks. Traditional cloud-centric security architectures face latency and privacy risks that are incompatible with the real-time, safety-critical requirements of consumer vehicles. This study proposes IDIV-FL, a Federated Edge-AI framework for proactive threat hunting and anomaly detection in in-vehicle networks. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is utilized at a central server, distributed to consumer vehicles, and iteratively trained on local data. Consumer vehicles share only updated weights, which are aggregated using the FedAvg algorithm to form a global model. Using the CICIoV2024 dataset (in binary, decimal, and hexadecimal formats), IDIV-FL achieved near-perfect accuracy on binary data, attributed to its simple 0/1 representation, and up to 99.6% attack detection on decimal and hexadecimal data, with sub-category classification accuracy reaching 99.01% (decimal) and 99.16% (hexadecimal). This demonstrates a scalable, low-latency solution for privacy-preserving intrusion detection in connected consumer vehicles.

papers.title: Mitigating Observability-Induced Inconsistency via State-Dependent Error Transformation for Underwater Integrated Navigation
papers.abstract: Inconsistency induced by observability mismatch remains a fundamental bottleneck in nonlinear filtering for underwater integrated navigation, often leading to severe underestimation of the error covariance and subsequent filter divergence. To address this core challenge, this article proposes a transform-consistent unscented Kalman filter (TCUKF) defined on the$SE_{2}$manifold, integrated within a hierarchical federated architecture. First, the kinematics of the strapdown inertial navigation system (SINS)/Doppler velocity log (DVL)/ long baseline (LBL) system are rigorously modeled on the$SE_{2}$Lie group to preserve geometric integrity. Second, through observability analysis, a state-dependent error transformation matrix$T(\hat {\chi })$is derived. We prove that this transformation decouples the unobservable subspace from the state estimates, thereby preserving observability consistency and effectively mitigating the spurious information injection inherent in standard approximations. Furthermore, a hierarchical federated architecture incorporating a manifold-based adaptive Sigma-point reweighting mechanism and state-augmented delay compensation is designed to handle heterogeneous acoustic measurements. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations and field experiments demonstrate that the TCUKF effectively solves the inconsistency problem. Compared with state-of-the-art algorithms such as UKF on manifold (UKF-M), InUKF, and MLAUKF, the proposed method exhibits superior positioning accuracy, heading stability, and consistency, particularly in scenarios with sparse global observations or measurement outliers.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement

papers.title: An Analytical Federated Learning Method for Scalable Nonintrusive Load Monitoring
papers.abstract: Nonintrusive load monitoring (NILM) infers appliance-level information from aggregate signals, which is expected to be achieved by federated learning over large-scale decentralized data. However, cross-user heterogeneity in appliance types and operating patterns induces strong nonindependent and identically distributed (non-IID) characteristics. Therefore, existing methods suffer from global–local bias, leading to performance degradation and high computational and communication costs as the number of users increases. To address these challenges, we propose an analytical federated learning method for scalable NILM. We first pretrain a shared feature extractor on simulated data to learn general waveform priors without precollected real-world data. The extractor is then frozen locally and analytically adapted through an update branch. We further derive a closed-form cloud aggregation that is equivalent to centralized learning in a single communication round, thereby avoiding global–local bias. Furthermore, our method is optimized for edge-side computation and communication to reduce resource consumption. Experiments across five datasets demonstrate superior performance, comparable to centralized learning even at 800 users. In addition, deployment on STM32 validates real-world efficiency, completing federated learning within 6.8 min. The code is publicly available at:https://github.com/2771618309/An-Analytical-Federated-Learning-Method-for-Scalable-NILM
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement

papers.title: Interference-Resilient Power Allocation for Hierarchical Over-the-Air Federated Learning
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate a large-scale Hierarchical over-the-air federated learning (Hierarchical-Air-FL) network comprising a fusion center (FC) and multiple clusters, where each cluster includes a base station (BS) and several edge devices. The FC coordinates the edge devices and BSs to train shared machine learning models. During the model training process, we leverage over-the-air computation (AirComp) for gradient aggregation to facilitate simultaneous transmission from devices to their respective BSs and from the BSs to the FC. To enhance communication efficiency and reduce transmission overhead, we employ a two-stage amplify-and-forward (AF) relaying mechanism. A significant challenge in such systems is inter-cluster interference due to wireless resources sharing among clusters, which can impede model convergence. To address this, we first conduct a comprehensive convergence analysis focusing on the optimality gap, which accounts for misalignment errors, noise-induced errors, and inter-cluster interference. Building upon this analysis, we propose an optimized power allocation strategy based on weighted and regularized channel inversion to minimize the optimality gap. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits significant advantages over baseline schemes in managing interference and accelerating convergence, thereby effectively enhancing the learning performance of the Hierarchical-Air-FL network.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Explainable Hybrid IoT–Fog–Cloud Framework Leveraging Consumer Electronics for Intelligent and Interpretable Connected Healthcare Systems
papers.abstract: The rapid proliferation of IoT-enabled devices in healthcare has enabled real-time monitoring and integrated care, but challenges in data interpretation, security, and scalability hinder clinician trust. This research presents XHIFC: an Explainable Hybrid IoT–Fog–Cloud Healthcare Framework for intelligent and secure hydatid cyst diagnosis. The primary innovation lies in combining explainable deep learning, dynamic resource allocation, and privacy-preserving data management within a unified framework. Specifically, the framework leverages a hybrid ensemble of CBAM-enhanced DenseNet169 and ResNet152V2 at the fog layer with gradient-based attention and feature attribution for interpretability, federated cloud learning for secure model updates, and a reinforcement learning–based Server Utilization Balancing Algorithm (SUBA) to optimize computational efficiency. Blockchain-enabled lightweight cryptographic mechanisms ensure tamper-proof healthcare record management. Experimental evaluations on hydatid cyst imaging datasets demonstrate 94.59% classification accuracy, a 45% reduction in latency, and a 30% improvement in server utilization compared to baseline approaches. The integration of explainability and resource-aware design enhances transparency, clinician trust, and decision verification, providing a secure and scalable foundation for next-generation connected healthcare systems.

papers.title: FedSNN-WTR: An Energy-Efficient and Channel-Robust Wireless Technology Recognition Framework for Vehicular Communications
papers.abstract: Vehicular communications rely on diverse wireless technologies to enhance traffic safety and operational efficiency. However, efficiently recognizing these technologies remains challenging due to the coexistence of multiple wireless systems, the non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) characteristic of data, and the constraints of resource-limited devices. Wireless technology recognition (WTR) is crucial for spectrum management and communication optimization by analyzing features extracted from radio signals. To overcome these challenges, we propose federated learning with spiking neural networks (FedSNN), which incorporate spiking neural networks (SNNs) into the federated learning (FL) framework. This approach is designed for WTR in complex vehicular communication scenarios. FedSNN showcases outstanding energy efficiency and generalization capabilities, enabling effective operation in resource-constrained environments. Experimental results demonstrate that FedSNN substantially improves recognition accuracy compared with local learning, while reducing the estimated inference computational energy to 11% of artificial neural networks (ANNs). Furthermore, FedSNN exhibits good robustness to channel distortions, including multipath fading and Doppler effects.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: A Bio-Inspired, Privacy-Preserving XAI Framework via Entropy-Driven Federated Learning for Consumer Healthcare devices
papers.abstract: The proliferation of connected consumer healthcare devices has intensified the demand for decentralized artificial intelligence (AI) that learns from sensitive patient data while preserving privacy and ensuring clinical trust. Although Federated Learning safeguards data by keeping raw records on-device, it often yields opaque global models that lack local explainability, hindering regulatory approval and clinician adoption. To bridge this gap, we propose NeuroShield-X, a privacy-preserving Explainable AI (XAI) framework grounded in Entropy-Driven Federated Learning. NeuroShield-X features a defense-in-depth architecture that synergistically integrates: (1)adaptive importance sparsificationfor communication efficiency, (2) a novel XAI Fidelity Regularizer (RXAI) to enforce explanation consistency at the edge, and (3) an Entropy-Driven Aggregation (EDA) scheme that dynamically weights client updates based on information richness and statistical trustworthiness. Evaluated on severely non-IID biomedical datasets, CVD-Health and Diabetic Retinopathy, NeuroShield-X achieves an 18.1% improvement in XAI fidelity over state-of-the-art federated XAI baselines, reduces communication overhead by 67.1%, limits accuracy degradation under poisoning attacks to just 5.2%, and accelerates convergence by 9%. These results establish NeuroShield-X as a robust, efficient, and trustworthy foundation for deploying transparent, privacy-preserving AI in real-world consumer healthcare systems.

papers.title: FedHCG: A Byzantine Robust Federated Learning Framework With Hierarchical Confidence Estimation and Geometric Consistency
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) has become a cornerstone of user-centric intelligence in large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) networks, where heterogeneous devices such as mobile users, sensors, and edge nodes collaboratively train shared models. However, the openness of FL exposes it to Byzantine participants that may upload corrupted updates, thereby degrading global performance. Existing Byzantine defenses fall into two categories: detection and tolerance, but both remain limited. Detection methods typically rely on distance-based heuristics that overlook hierarchical sensitivity and dynamic user trust. While tolerance methods often ignore the low-dimensional manifold structure of user updates, leading to reduced discriminability under complex attacks. To address these challenges, we propose FedHCG, a Byzantine robust FL framework that introduces reliable user selection based hierarchical confidence estimation (HCE) and geometric consistency (GC) based aggregation. The HCE quantifies each user’s hierarchical reliability across temporal and structural layers, enabling adaptive filtering of anomalous participants. The GC embeds user updates into a manifold space and measures their geometric consistency within peer clusters, yielding soft aggregation weights that suppress corrupted updates without complete exclusion. Extensive experiments on the benchmark dataset have shown that our method can improve by 58.86% compared to FedAvg when honest users make up the majority. Even though malicious users dominate, it has improved by 82.1% compared to FedAvg, demonstrating strong robustness. Theoretical analysis further proves its convergence and robustness. Overall, FedHCG provides a principled and scalable foundation for trustworthy, user-centered federated intelligence.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: DIVAS-FL: Diffusion-based Implicit Voice editing via Autoencoder-guided Style transfer in Federated Learning for consumer devices
papers.abstract: Voice-based technologies deployed on consumer electronic devices, such as smartphones, smart speakers, and wearable assistants, operate under strict privacy and computational constraints, limiting the use of centralized data and demanding decentralized learning approaches. In this context, combining controlled voice generation with federated learning offers a promising strategy to enhance voice personalization without compromising user privacy. This work presents DIVAS-FL, a generative framework that integrates controlled voice synthesis with federated learning. A style-aware generative model, based on a hierarchical diffusion process and a latent Style-aware Variational Autoencoder, is centrally pre-trained and then locally adapted to produce diverse synthetic voices conditioned on speaker-specific attributes, such as gender. Consumer devices fine-tune specific model components using local data, enabling personalized style control while preserving privacy and adhering to constrained computational budgets typical of consumer electronics. Integrated into a federated training scheme, the system enhances the style adaptation of transformed speech, ensuring that sensitive voice data remains decentralized and secure, effectively supporting realistic, personalized voice interactions on consumer devices.

papers.title: HAFedRec: Homomorphic Encryption Adaptive Graph Aggregation for Federated Recommendation
papers.abstract: Federated recommendation has emerged as a promising technique to protect user privacy by enabling multiple clients to collaboratively train a recommendation model without sharing their raw data. However, federated recommendation still faces two key challenges: (i) data heterogeneity, in which the diversity of user preferences results in noise when using naive global average aggregation; and (ii) privacy leakage, in which existing personalized aggregation strategies often require sharing user embeddings, thus risking privacy exposure. In this paper, we propose HAFedRec, a federated recommendation framework that addresses these challenges with two novel components. First, the Homomorphic Encryption based Interaction Vector Similarity Measurement Module computes user preference similarities. This is done by homomorphically encrypting the interaction vectors and then applying dimension shuffling. This enables more accurate computation of user preference similarity without exposing any raw user data. Second, the Adaptive Graph Aggregation Module constructs a user-neighbor graph and adaptively adjusts aggregation weights based on both user similarity and the training quality of neighbors’ models, improving personalization and reducing heterogeneity noise in federated. By aggregating model parameters of users with similar preferences, this framework effectively mitigates the impact of data heterogeneity, thereby enhancing personalization and improving recommendation accuracy. Extensive experiments on five real world datasets demonstrate that HAFedRec achieves superior top-Krecommendation accuracy (HR@10 and NDCG@10) compared to nine baseline frameworks, while simultaneously preserving user privacy.

papers.title: EPVFL: Efficient Privacy-Preserving and Verifiable Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL), as a distributed machine learning paradigm, has gained widespread adoption due to its ability to retain user data locally, thereby protecting privacy, while collaboratively training a global model through gradient sharing. However, existing studies have shown that attackers may obtain privacy information from the gradients, and malicious server may return erroneous aggregated results, compromising federated learning model. Although prior studies have addressed privacy preservation and aggregated result verification, these methods often incur significant computation and communication overhead on the user side. In this paper, we propose an efficient privacy-preserving and verifiable federated learning (EPVFL) scheme. Specifically, we group the gradients and employ polynomial encryption to achieve efficient privacy protection. Furthermore, we design a lightweight verification mechanism where users only need to perform lightweight local computation without interaction and transmit just a floating-point vector to verify the correctness of the aggregated gradient. EPVFL supports users going offline at any time, while online users can still obtain the correct aggregated gradient without incurring additional computation or communication overhead. Finally, through security analysis and experiments on real datasets, we demonstrate the correctness, verifiability, and privacy protection of EPVFL. Experiment results indicate that EPVFL protects privacy without sacrificing model accuracy and significantly reduces the computation and communication overheads on the user side compared to the related schemes.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: Energy-Efficient Computing Using Adaptive Model Selection for Mobile Agents in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Multi-agent federated learning requires all agents to stay online until the global model converges, and its multi-round training incurs substantial on-agent computing. However, most edge mobile agents with limited computational capacity and battery life may drop out of FL training prematurely due to low battery, which can degrade the convergence speed and accuracy of the global model. Prior works assign heterogeneous models to different agents to reduce on-agent computational energy, but neglect the changes in data distributions and computational capacities on agents. This makes it difficult to save on-agent computational energy and to support global aggregation. To this end, we propose a hierarchical Federated learning framework based on Adaptive Local Training (FedALT). Specifically, FedALT can adaptively select the most suitable local model for each agent based on its computational capacity and data distribution to reduce on-agent computational energy. To achieve finer-grained savings in computational energy, FedALT dynamically adjusts the number of local epochs for each agent during local training. Furthermore, FedALT conducts edge aggregation through model layer sharing and knowledge distillation to improve the convergence speed and accuracy of the global model. We compare FedALT with three baselines by training six models on two Non-IID datasets. Experiments on both the simulation platform and the hardware platform demonstrate that FedALT can achieve the lowest computational energy, the highest average global model accuracy, and the fastest global model convergence.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: AgriFedCL: A Privacy-Preserving Federated Architecture with Curriculum Learning for Intrusion Detection in Agricultural Consumer Electronics
papers.abstract: In the Agriculture 4.0 era, the Internet of Agricultural Consumer Electronics (IoACE) has become an integral component of precision and sustainable agriculture. The IoACE ecosystem facilitates the autonomous real-time monitoring, decision-making, and data-driven optimization of agricultural operations. However, the lack of robust security measures exposes them to various threats, including device spoofing and malicious intrusions that can compromise their integrity. Such vulnerabilities can severely disrupt the agricultural operations, which can lead to faulty decision-making. Therefore, it necessitates the deployment of intelligent intrusion detection to ensure the resilience, data veracity, and operational trustworthiness of next-generation agricultural systems. Federated Learning (FL) is a striking collaborative framework that allows multiple IoACE devices for distributed edge-centric training to enhance the security of sensor-driven agricultural information. Moreover, the slow convergence of the global model can be mitigated by introducing Curriculum Learning (CL), which gradually presents the difficult samples during training. The proposed AgriFedCL architecture integrates the CL and FL approaches for classifying attacks on IoACE devices. Also, a novel variant of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) has been incorporated to extract temporal features for real-time attack classification. The resilience of the AgriFedCL architecture has been trained and tested on three public datasets, namely X-IIoTID, Farm-flow, and WUSTL-IIOT, for binary and multi-class intrusion detection. The developed method surpasses 5 other State-of-The-Art existing methods by obtaining the highest 95.58% intrusion classification accuracy.

papers.title: Adaptive Satellite-to-Device Association Based Asynchronous Federated Edge Learning in STIN
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: FedPoison: A Dual-Strategy Poisoning Attack on Multi-Agent Federated Learning With Local Differential Privacy
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is increasingly adopted in multi-agent healthcare systems where agents collaboratively train models without sharing sensitive data. While integrating FL with local differential privacy (LDP) offers robust protection against many privacy concerns, these models are still vulnerable to advanced adversarial attacks. A significant challenge is that even with LDP safeguards, FL models can be compromised by malicious attackers who inject poisoned data. In this paper, we introduce FedPoison, an advanced poisoning attack scheme designed to target both the mean and variance of datasets. Our method employs a dual strategy, integrating both input and output poisoning to effectively disrupt the FL process. Specifically, attackers can estimate the mean and variance of training data under LDP protection and inject poisoned data to carry out input poisoning attacks (IPA). The manipulated data in IPA is trained alongside the FL model, ultimately skewing the FL model's output. Additionally, the attackers can bypass the LDP perturbation mechanism to launch output poisoning attacks (OPA) by uploading carefully altered mean and variance values, thus leading to biases in the aggregation of local model updates. Through the rigorous mathematical analyses, we demonstrate that the proposed scheme can successfully execute poisoning attacks on LDP-protected FL models. Extensive experiments conducted on four different datasets using PyTorch validate the effectiveness of our scheme, revealing that it significantly undermines the performance of FL models, even when LDP mechanisms are employed, highlighting its considerable threat to multi-agent collaborative decision-making systems in healthcare.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Differentially Private Model Recombination as a Service for Trustable and Federated Learning in Next-Generation Networks With Non-IID Data
papers.abstract: Next-generation networks demand federated learning (FL) frameworks that ensure both privacy and robustness under heterogeneous non-IID data. Traditional FL approaches, such as FedAvg, suffer significant accuracy degradation in non-IID settings, while naive differential privacy (DP) mechanisms reduce model utility. To address this, we propose Differentially Private Model Recombination as a Service (DP-MRaaS), which integrates layer-wise model recombination, adaptive DP, and a Thompson sampling controller. DP-MRaaS dynamically alternates between aggregation and recombination while allocating noise and clipping based on loss improvements. The service abstraction exposes these decisions as controllable management functions for privacy-aware model training in network and service management systems. Theoretical analysis confirms convergence rates comparable to FedAvg, and extensive experiments on CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST demonstrate its effectiveness. On CIFAR-10 CNN, DP-MRaaS achieves$57.78\pm 0.51\%$accuracy under IID, matching FedAvg (57.78%) while preserving$(\epsilon,\delta) = (3.5,10^{-5})$privacy. On CIFAR-10 ResNet-18, DP-MRaaS attains$66.57\pm 0.54\%$(IID) and$61.30\pm 0.30\%$(Balanced Non-IID), competitive with FedAvg-DP (66.70%, 61.84%) and Ditto-DP (66.86%, 61.76%). On Fashion-MNIST, DP-MRaaS achieves$90.52\pm 0.10\%$(IID) and$90.02\pm 0.07\%$(Balanced Non-IID), the highest among DP-enabled methods. A five-way ablation study confirms that recombination is the primary accuracy driver (+8.6% on ResNet-18), while adaptive DP preserves utility with < 0.1% degradation on CNN. These results show that DP-MRaaS achieves a superior balance between accuracy, stability, and privacy, advancing the trustability of FL for service management in next-generation networks.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: Clustering-Driven Cooperative Caching and Trajectory Optimization Based on Dual-Agent Reinforcement Learning in UAV-Assisted VANETs
papers.abstract: The high mobility and heterogeneity of Vehicular Networks (VANETs) impose significant challenges for edge caching and resource optimization, as rapidly changing topologies and diverse content demands hinder real-time responsiveness. To address these issues, we propose an integrated optimization framework combining dynamic clustering, popularity prediction, and joint caching-trajectory control. Firstly, we design a location-interest-based dynamic vehicle clustering mechanism that groups vehicles according to communication reachability and semantic content similarity, forming stable and service-oriented clusters. Secondly, a hierarchical asynchronous federated prediction model is developed to aggregate local cluster pReferences with global request trends, achieving timely, accurate, and privacy-aware popularity estimation. Finally, we construct a Dual-Agent Collaborative Caching and Trajectory Optimization (DACTCO) framework, where a Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (D3QN) agent governs UAV-assisted caching decisions while a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) agent adapts UAV positions. Through a unified scalarized reward, the two agents jointly minimize average delay and energy consumption in a coordinated manner. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly enhances service quality and resource efficiency, achieving reductions of up to 6.3% in average delay, 42% in average energy consumption, and improvements of up to 36.2% in cache hit rate compared with state-of-the-art baselines.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: PP-FedDT: Securing Digital Twin Federated Learning Against Persistent and Adaptive Poisoning Attacks
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) operates over non-IID client data with heterogeneous distributions and quality, which complicates convergence and makes it hard to distinguish benign irregularities from malicious behavior. FL is increasingly adopted to train edge digital twins (DTs). Healthcare applications such as CVD risk prediction across hospital networks demand both privacy preservation and model integrity, making poisoning resilience critical. Attackers can inject or compromise clients to submit manipulated updates that poison the global model, either untargeted with widespread degradation or targeted via backdoors that misclassify trigger inputs while preserving overall accuracy. DT-FL must protect privacy, preserve integrity, and resist adaptive poisoning where attackers adjust updates after observing global models and defenses. Existing defenses rely mainly on robust aggregation and often assume few adversaries, abundant attack evidence per round, or access to a clean validation set. They also overlook the dynamics of early training phases where small degradations can cause lasting harm. We propose a Privacy-Preserving Federated Digital Twin (PP-FedDT) framework that secures federated digital twin learning using private bounded updates, verifiable update compliance, and DT-assisted participant screening. Each client clips and noise-perturbs its local update, then submits a cryptographic commitment alongside a zero-knowledge proof certifying norm boundedness, encoding validity, and commitment correctness. At the edge, digital twin metadata and update similarity graphs are analyzed to detect Sybil or colluding participants, and suspicious contributions are removed prior to aggregation. The remaining updates are aggregated robustly using parameter-level trimming and adaptive weighting to suppress abnormal coordinate values. Influence is then monitored across rounds to regulate or exclude persistently harmful clients, maintaining correctness, privacy, and resistance to adaptive poisoning. Experiments on standard benchmarks show improved robustness, stability, and accuracy over FedAvg, Krum, Trimmed mean and Median.

papers.title: Securing Multilingual Hate Speech Detection in Federated Few-Shot Learning Against Backdoors
papers.abstract: Effective hate speech detection is paramount for maintaining safe computational social systems, yet it faces challenges from data scarcity in low-resource languages and privacy concerns. Federated few-shot learning (FFSL) addresses these by enabling collaborative model training across distributed clients with limited labeled data. However, FFSL remains vulnerable to backdoor attacks where malicious clients inject triggers to manipulate model predictions, allowing toxic content to evade detection filters. To the best of our knowledge, no prior work has examined backdoor defenses for FFSL in multilingual hate speech detection. To address this unexplored gap, we propose gradient anomaly aware robust defense (GARD), a novel defense framework that combines gradient-based anomaly detection with robust aggregation to protect multilingual hate speech detection models against backdoor attacks. First, GARD performs gradient analysis using adaptive interquartile range (IQR)-based magnitude and similarity thresholds to filter anomalous updates. Then, it applies coordinatewise median aggregation over the remaining benign clients. We evaluate GARD against three backdoor attacks: BadNets, InsertSent, and Layerwise Weight Poisoning (LWP), on Hindi, Spanish, and German datasets using Multilingual Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (mBERT) and Multilingual Distilled Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (mDistilBERT) models in 5-shot and 10-shot configurations under independent and identically distributed (IID) and non- IID settings at poisoning rates of 0.2% and 0.3%. Experimental results demonstrate that GARD reduces attack success rates while maintaining clean accuracy across all configurations, with stronger defense observed in 10-shot settings. These findings validate GARD as an effective defense mechanism generalizable across languages and attack modalities, ensuring the integrity and safety of automated moderation in federated scenarios.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems

papers.title: Edge Collaborative Caching Strategy in Space–Air–Ground Integrated Networks
papers.abstract: Due to constraints in network capacity and coverage, conventional ground-based infrastructures face difficulties in delivering low-latency and high-reliability caching capabilities to users and Internet of Things (IoT) devices located in remote regions, including mountains and oceans. The Space-Air-Ground Integrated Network (SAGIN), envisioned as a foundational structure for 6G communication systems and integrated with Mobile Edge Computing (MEC), can offer a promising solution to efficiently serve the caching demands of users in such underserved locations. Nevertheless, the high heterogeneity and time-varying nature of SAGIN, along with the continuous evolution of the popularity of user requested content, which presents substantial challenges to achieve satisfactory cache hit ratios and low access latency. In this paper, we introduce a novel three-tier edge collaborative caching architecture comprising satellites, Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle (UAV) clusters, and ground edge servers. We formulate the cache replacement task as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). To address concerns over user privacy and heterogeneous local model performance, we propose a Federated Discrete Soft Actor-Critic (FDSAC) approach that employs an attention mechanism guided by server activity levels to adaptively weight client models during parameters aggregation. Additionally, a content popularity prediction module based on Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) is embedded within the DSAC agent to derive the optimal cache replacement decisions. Experimental evaluations indicate that the FDSAC achieves superior performance compared to other baseline algorithms in terms of both cache hit rate and content retrieval delay.

papers.title: A Novel Incentive Mechanism Based on One-to-Many Bargaining in Coalition Federated Edge Learning for MEC-Enabled Consumer Electronics
papers.abstract: Intelligent consumer electronics—smartphones, wearables, and IoT gateways—generate massive personal data at the network edge, driving demand for privacy-preserving collaborative intelligence. Federated edge learning (FEL) integrates federated learning (FL) with mobile edge computing (MEC) to enable distributed model training without exposing raw data. However, centralized FEL imposes prohibitive communication overhead when users are dispersed across multiple edge servers, while decentralized FEL suffers from degraded model accuracy due to limited local aggregation. Both paradigms ignore the fundamental asymmetry between mobile devices, which are resource-limited and intermittently available, and edge servers (ESs), which are fixed and resource-rich. To address this limitation, we propose coalition federated edge learning (CFEL), a framework that partitions users into ES-led coalitions where each ES serves as the coalition leader responsible for model aggregation and payment distribution. We model the incentive mechanism within each coalition as a one-to-many concurrent bargaining game (OCBG) and derive a closed-form Nash Bargaining Solution (NBS) that yields a principled, equal-surplus-sharing payment allocation grounded in MEC-specific communication and aggregation costs. Federated learning experiments on Fashion-MNIST and UCI-HAR demonstrate that CFEL achieves 89.24% accuracy on Fashion-MNIST (vs. 86.47% for decentralized FEL) and 90.80% on UCI-HAR (vs. 84.47% for decentralized FEL), while reducing distance-weighted communication cost by 68% compared with centralized FEL. Under non-IID data, periodic cross-coalition synchronization enables CFEL to surpass baselines on both datasets (82.66% on HAR, 81.44% on Fashion-MNIST). NBS payment allocation is further verified feasible and incentive-compatible under realistic MEC cost parameters. These results demonstrate that CFEL offers a favorable accuracy–communication trade-off for resource-constrained consumer electronics deployments. Source code is available at https://github.com/hl5w/CoalitionFederated-Edge-Learning.

papers.title: Decentralized Federated Adversarial Learning for Proactive Anomaly Defense in Consumer-Grade Agricultural Vision Systems
papers.abstract: Although consumer electronics have enabled the rapid deployment of low cost cotton apical bud recognition systems these traditional centralized terminals face critical privacy and cybersecurity risks notably their vulnerability to adversarial visual deception in open farmlands. To address these issues a novel decentralized framework integrating swarm intelligence with federated adversarial learning named Fed-Cotton-Guard is proposed. First a peer-to-peer swarm architecture is established enabling edge devices to collaboratively train without sharing raw physical images. Second through the introduction of a Min Max game mechanism edge nodes are empowered to proactively generate and defend against adversarial perturbations locally thereby achieving proactive threat hunting. Furthermore a detection strategy based on parameter distribution residuals is designed to proactively intercept malicious parameter poisoning within the decentralized network. Extensive experiments on resource constrained hardware platforms such as the Jetson Nano demonstrate that Fed-Cotton-Guard maintains a high detection accuracy of 96.5% while effectively resisting various adversarial attacks including FGSM and PGD, compared to existing methods this framework significantly enhances collaborative fault tolerance and communication efficiency providing a highly robust.

papers.title: Game-Theoretic Federated Deception for Consumer Electronics: Adaptive Coordination in IoT Security
papers.abstract: Consumer Internet of Things (IoT) networks are vulnerable to complex online attacks due to their distributed architecture, but privacy regulations outlaw centralized security strategies. Current Federated Learning (FL) considers intrusion detection as static classification, whereas deception systems do not have strategic coordination against adaptive adversaries. We propose a Game-Theoretic Federated Deception (GFD) architecture, which combines FL with dynamic deception via Nash equilibrium-based coordination in privacy-preserving distributed cyber defense. The two-phase architecture decouples the establishment of detection foundations (Phase 1: federated neural network training) and strategic coordination (Phase 2: gametheoretic deception optimization), allowing continuous adaptation to be achieved without retraining models. Evaluation on 3.6M TON_IoT samples has shown 95.78% accuracy and 98.86% recall with a detection miss rate of 1.14% and a deception success rate of 60.6% on adaptive attackers. The framework exhibits scalability of 5-50 federated nodes (performance variation less than ±0.0071%) with linear communication scaling, 255 times communication reduction (0.28 KB/round) with complete model exchange. Ablation analysis gives a privacy cost of 2.41% accuracy degradation, and deception gives the highest performance gain (+3.37% F1-score). The coordinated defense of the exploitation of lateral movement is proven by zero spatial compromise in all experiments. The article provides the premises of adaptive, privacy-aware security in distributed consumer IoT settings against intelligent adversaries.

papers.title: CIWGS-FedMed: Channel-Importance Weighted Gradient Sparsification for Communication Efficient Federated Medical Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables hospitals to collaboratively train medical image segmentation models without sharing raw patient data. However, transmitting full model updates in each communication round incurs prohibitive bandwidth costs, particularly in resource-constrained clinical networks.We propose CIWGS-FedMed, a Channel-Importance-Weighted Gradient Sparsification framework. Its primary contribution is a Grad-CAM-inspired channel importance scorer that allocates the per-layer transmission budget proportionally to EMA-smoothed channel activation–gradient products. This enables structured compression that respects the information hierarchy of convolutional feature maps, representing a structural departure from prior unstructured Top-k methods. Three additional components complement the scorer. First, a hyperparameter-light, architecture-aware, layer-adaptive sparsity schedule that protects task-critical early and decoder layers while aggressively compressing the bottle-neck. Second, exponential moving average (EMA) stabilisation of importance scores across mini-batches, which suppresses single-batch gradient noise. Third, a clipped error-feedback residual mechanism, auto-scaled to the median absolute parameter-delta magnitude, which prevents gradient explosion while recovering discarded information across rounds. Experiments on a non-IID synthetic medical dataset with five heterogeneous hospital clients demonstrate that CIWGS-FedMed significantly reduces communication cost while maintaining strong segmentation performance, achieving 78.5% reduction in total communication, relative to uncompressed FedAvg and 14.1% reduction compared to fixed-ratio magnitude-based sparsification. Importantly, the uplink ratio self-reduces from 6.4% in round 1 to 5.2% in round 30 as importance scores concentrate, without any manual scheduling.

papers.title: Energy-Aware Federated Distillation via Quantum-Driven Task Offloading in LEO Satellite Networks
papers.abstract: Low earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks have emerged as a key enabler for delivering real-time and global services to distributed terrestrial nodes, particularly in remote regions. To preserve data privacy, federated learning (FL) provides a decentralized framework for advancing artificial intelligence (AI) in complex tasks. However, the efficiency of FL is constrained by high and imbalanced energy consumption, which limits its practical deployment. To address these challenges, an energy-aware FL framework that integrates knowledge distillation (KD) with task offloading is proposed, where KD is performed at both the FL server and client devices or direct-connected satellites using public datasets. The energy consumption balancing problem is formulated as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) model. To achieve computational efficiency and parallelism, the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is employed to solve the problem with both the mixing and cost Hamiltonians derived and the corresponding quantum circuit designed. In a FL framework over a LEO satellite network comprising 40 satellites and 10 FL clients, the proposed method reduces energy consumption by approximately 26.4%, achieves improved energy balance with a weighted variance of approximately 4.93 and maintains high accuracy of 0.95 in a vehicle classification task, compared with the traditional FL method.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: MediChain-FSL: A Blockchain-Integrated Federated Semi-Supervised Learning System for Secure Breast Cancer Diagnosis in Smart Home Healthcare Devices
papers.abstract: Breast cancer remains the most commonly diagnosed cancer among women worldwide, with early-stage detection improving five-year survival rates to over 90%. Despite advances in artificial intelligence and consumer electronics for home-based healthcare monitoring, security and privacy concerns remain barriers to widespread adoption for sensitive medical applications like breast cancer diagnosis. Given that access to regular screening remains limited in many communities due to infrastructure and cost constraints, this paper introduces MediChain-FSL, a blockchain-integrated federated semi-supervised learning system for secure breast cancer assessment using smart home healthcare devices and wearable sensors. MediChain-FSL addresses data scarcity and privacy preservation through decentralized learning, where blockchain ensures immutable audit trails and secure multi-party computation while federated semi-supervised learning exploits limited expert-labeled data and abundant unlabeled sensor data from consumer electronics. Our framework employs a blockchain-validated quality-aware aggregation protocol combined with homomorphic encryption and differential privacy mechanisms for consensus-based model aggregation, preventing poisoning attacks and ensuring data integrity across distributed IoT devices, including smart mirrors, thermal imaging systems, and biometric wearables. The semi-supervised component combines consistency regularization under stochastic augmentations with confidence-based pseudo-labeling to exploit abundant unlabeled sensor data. Experimental evaluation using a combined multi-modal dataset of 3,800 samples derived from three distinct data sources spanning clinical, thermal, and biosignal modalities demonstrates 93.4% classification accuracy with 54% communication reduction and sub-180ms latency on resource-constrained devices. The system achieves 98.7% of maximum performance using only 5% labeled data, maintains over 90% accuracy under 20% Byzantine attacks with formal differential privacy guarantees, and successfully detected seven early-stage cancer cases during field deployment across 45 smart home environments.

papers.title: FedULBD: Unlearning-Driven Lightweight Backdoor Defense for Resource-Constrained Consumer Electronics Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a key enabling technology for privacy-preserving intelligent applications in resource-constrained consumer electronics. However, its distributed training paradigm exposes the global model to highly stealthy and destructive backdoor attacks. Existing defenses either rely on additional clean data, impose non-negligible computational burdens on clients, or lack robustness in dynamic participation scenarios, making them unsuitable for lightweight consumer devices. To address these challenges, we propose FedULBD, a server-side lightweight backdoor defense framework driven by random unlearning. First, FedULBD leverages the response characteristics of model updates under random unlearning and constructs anomaly indicators through a two-layer standardization process combining intra-layer normalization with cross-client normalization. Without relying on any clean data or introducing additional computation on clients, this yields unified anomaly indicators that stably characterize client abnormality under complex training scenarios. Second, to enhance robustness in dynamic participation settings, FedULBD builds upon these anomaly indicators by integrating a binary clustering mechanism with historical behavior tracking, enabling stable and effective defense even when client participation continuously changes. Finally, a z-score-guided soft-weighted aggregation strategy is introduced to suppress abnormal updates while preserving beneficial contributions, thereby promoting stable model convergence. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that FedULBD substantially suppresses backdoor attacks while maintaining high benign-task accuracy across multiple datasets, attack types, and dynamic participation settings.

papers.title: Privacy-Preserving Vertical Federated Learning via Adaptive Noise-Intensity Regulation for Embodied Intelligence
papers.abstract: As embodied intelligence emerges as a core paradigm in Agentic AI, which enables embodied agents to collaboratively perceive through cross-party modeling, ensuring privacy preservation among distributed parties becomes increasingly critical. Vertical Federated Learning (VFL) enables privacy-preserving collaborative modeling by sharing parameters while keeping data local, yet gradient exchange still leaks informative signals that enable Feature Inference Attacks (FIA), where the attacker infers the private features of other participants, raising serious privacy threats for embodied intelligence. However, existing FIA attacks either ignore the vulnerabilities of passive parties as attackers or assume that passive parties have access to global information, which is unrealistic. To bridge this gap, we take the first step by introducing a novel feature inference attack BlackFIA, aiming to unveil potential vulnerabilities in which the passive party reconstructs private features from locally available data and exchanged gradients, without any global information. To mitigate this privacy risk, we further propose BlackFIA${}_{defense}$, an adaptive differentially private training mechanism that emphasizes protection for high-risk samples and regulates noise intensity to preserve predictive utility. Extensive experiments across tabular and image datasets show that BlackFIA achieves stronger reconstruction quality and higher attack success rate than baselines, while remaining computationally practical during training. More importantly, BlackFIA${}_{defense}$consistently degrades attack success rate to about 55%, and maintains the global model accuracy at about 75% under a strict privacy budget, providing a stronger privacy-utility trade-off than standard DP-SGD based defenses.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: An Efficient and Threshold Private Set Intersection for Privacy-Enhanced Vertical Federated Learning in Consumer Systems
papers.abstract: The industrial consumer field integrates industrial production with financial consumption, aiming to focus on the entire process of the consumption system, with comprehensive data analysis conducted across multiple institutions. Vertical federated learning is a vital component for distributed collaborative data analysis. It allows parties to integrate sample features from all parties while maintaining privacy and conduct comprehensive model training. This paper focuses on vertical federated learning in the industrial consumer field and proposes a vertical federated learning framework for factory economic prediction. In this framework, a factory institution collaborates with multiple consumer institutions to perform vertical federated learning, train a predictive model, and determine whether a factory institution is operating normally. We design a privacy-preserving (t,n)-threshold private set intersection protocol to achieve sample alignment for this framework. This protocol aligns sample data from all parties while protecting their privacy. It also introduces a weighting mechanism to accommodate missing sample data for some non-critical parties. We implement the proposed vertical federated learning framework and conduct a comprehensive security analysis. Evaluation results demonstrate that our private sample alignment protocol performs well, and the predictive model derived from vertical federated learning is highly accurate and practical.

papers.title: SpecGradFilter: A Spectral Gradient Filtering Framework for Taming Federated Heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is fundamentally challenged by statistical heterogeneity, where non-identically distributed (non-IID) data induces "client drift" that severely hampers global convergence. While existing approaches attempt to mitigate this drift through spatial-domain gradient correction or regularization, they overlook the intrinsic spectral structure of optimization signals. In this work, we revisit client drift from a frequency-domain perspective and empirically observe a "Spectral Bias of Drift": in the evaluated training trajectories, a disproportionate fraction of inter-client gradient disagreement is concentrated in the lower-frequency bands of the adopted structured parameter layout. Motivated by this observation, we propose SpecGradFilter, which suppresses a small low-frequency portion of selected layer gradients and can be implemented using an FFT-based projection or spatial-domain detrending approximations. For the FFT-based realization, we establish a conditional convergence guarantee when the projection retains sufficient global descent signal and the post-filtering client heterogeneity is bounded. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, Tiny-ImageNet, and additional benchmarks show improved accuracy and time-to-target in the tested non-IID settings without increasing the per-round communication payload.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

papers.title: FedLifeLLM: A Lifecycle-Aware Federated LLM Framework for Privacy-Preserving Condition and Risk Screening in Women’s Mental Health
papers.abstract: Women’s mental health across the hormonal lifecycle remains critically underserved by consumer health systems that neither account for lifecycle-specific symptom phenomenology nor preserve clinical data privacy. We present FEDLIFELLM, a lifecycle-aware federated learning framework that fine-tunes an 8B-parameter instruction-tuned LLM via 4-bit QLoRA across three biologically-motivated silos—Menstrual, Perinatal, and Menopausal—for simultaneous mental health condition classification and risk severity stratification, without raw patient data leaving the device perimeter. The proposed Tri-Defense Mechanism jointly addresses federated convergence instability (Step-Bounded FedProx), the privacy-utility imbalance of uniform noise (Lifecycle-Proportionate Privacy Noise), and rare-class gradient suppression (Clinical Cost-Weighted Cross-Entropy Loss). Stage-Adaptive LoRA rank allocation further compensates for data-scarce silos by assigning greater representational capacity to smaller cohorts. On LifeMH-FL, a newly constructed 111,299-record lifecycle-stratified corpus, FEDLIFELLM attains 79% condition classification accuracy (macro-F1 0.740 ± 0.001) and 80% risk severity accuracy (macro-F1 0.765 ± 0.003), averaged over three seeds on a held-out set of 22,239 records, with 0.77 precision on suicidal ideation—surpassing the closest prior federated mental-health framework and centralized training on both tasks, within 20 communication rounds that transmit less than 0.1% of full model parameters. Ablations confirm that lifecycle-stage prompting is the dominant contributor (+0.040 macro-F1,p−68) and that proportionate DP recovers most of the utility uniform DP sacrifices, while membership-inference and gradient-inversion analyses indicate the per-silo noise affords empirical privacy at negligible utility cost. These results provide preliminary evidence for a privacy-preserving, precision-oriented screening aid suited to on-device consumer women’s-health applications—e.g., cycle-tracking and perinatal-care apps on smartphones and wearables, where sensitive data never leaves the user’s device.

papers.title: Learning Behavior Consistency-Based Backdoor Defense for Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL), as a distributed machine learning paradigm, enables model training without data leaving local devices, but it is highly vulnerable to backdoor attacks. Attackers can manipulate the global model to output attacker-specified results by embedding backdoor triggers during the FL training phase. Most existing defense methods have limited defensive capabilities due to their excessive reliance on the assumption that backdoor updates are significantly different from benign updates in the parameter space. To address this issue, we propose LBC-Guardian, a learning behavior consistency-based backdoor defense method that leverages the impact of backdoor attacks on clean models to achieve effective defense. Specifically, we first propose an instantaneous state consistency evaluation mechanism that identifies malicious updates within each round by probing their functional impact on a server-side reference dataset. We then design a historical trend consistency gating mechanism that captures cross-round behavioral anomalies to suppress stealthy attackers that evade single-round detection. Finally, based on these two consistency measures, each client is assigned a score to enable robust weighted aggregation. Experimental results across various datasets demonstrate that LBC-Guardian achieves superior defensive performance against diverse backdoor attacks compared to existing state-of-the-art defense methods. In particular, it demonstrates strong robustness against adaptive attacks with full knowledge of the defense mechanism.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Joint UE-BS Association and Resource Allocation for Multi-Cell Hierarchical Over-the-Air Federated Learning with Non-IID Data
papers.abstract: Over-the-air computation (AirComp) has been studied in hierarchical federated learning (HFL) to enable efficient model aggregation by integrating communication and computation, thereby alleviating uplink communication bottlenecks. However, in AirComp-based HFL systems, channel fading, CSI-estimation errors, and receiver noise inevitably introduce aggregation errors. In addition, such systems still face challenges such as user mobility and non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data, both of which can degrade global model performance. To overcome these challenges, we propose MC-AirCompFL, a multi-cell hierarchical FL framework that performs intra-cell aggregation via AirComp and inter-cell aggregation at the cloud. We first derive a system-level convergence upper bound that explicitly captures the impact of AirComp-induced aggregation errors, imperfect CSI, and label-distribution-skewed Non-IID data. Then, we formulate a joint optimization problem for receive scaling at base stations (BSs), transmit-power control at user equipments (UEs), and UE-BS association to minimize the convergence-guided objective and the cell-level label-distribution distance to the IID reference. Furthermore, a Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty-based causal online algorithm is developed to enforce long-term constraints through virtual queues and achieve per-round causal optimization. Numerical results on MNIST and CIFAR-10 demonstrate that the proposed scheme improves learning performance over benchmark schemes while maintaining communication-efficiency and long-term energy-control advantages.

papers.title: A Lightweight and Efficient Probabilistic Authentication Aggregation Scheme for Trusted Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) represents a machine learning that enhances privacy preservation by enabling model training to occur directly on individual devices, with only parameter gradients being transmitted rather than the underlying raw datasets. However, it remains vulnerable to various malicious attacks, including model tampering attack and forgery attack launched by malicious clients. These attacks could compromise the parameters of client and damage trained model. To address these challenges, we propose an efficient probabilistic batch-authenticated FL (PBAFL) scheme. Firstly, we design a lightweight digital signature scheme with aggregation capability to achieve integrity authentication of the gradients submitted by the clients. Secondly, we propose a probabilistic batch authentication scheme that achieves 99% accuracy by authenticating only a small portion of the signatures, significantly improving authentication efficiency. We implement a prototype system of the PBAFL scheme for privacy and security proof analysis, conducting comprehensive experiments on MNIST datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed PBAFL model substantially reduces batch authentication time and communication overhead compared to existing approaches.

papers.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Early Warning of Memory Poisoning for Consumer AI Agents
papers.abstract: Consumer AI agents increasingly rely on persistent long-term memory to support personalization, contextual continuity, and multi-step task execution, but this memory also creates a new attack surface in which memory poisoning can occur through malicious memory insertion, misleading memory updates, retrieval manipulation, or latent records that later induce reasoning errors. Existing studies have examined agent privacy leakage, retrieval corruption, and federated robustness, yet they rarely address the specific problem of forecasting whether a newly written memory record will trigger future reasoning deviation, measured as an observable divergence between the agent’s later reasoning trace and a benign reference trajectory, under privacy-sensitive and heterogeneous deployment settings. To address this gap, this paper proposes FEMP-GUARD, a privacy-preserving federated early-warning framework for long-horizon memory poisoning in consumer AI agents. The proposed method models poisoning risk as a retrieval-conditioned temporal forecasting task, where each client locally encodes memory-writing events, retrieval dynamics, and behavioral context, and then participates in privacy-preserving personalized federated optimization without sharing raw memory traces. The predicted warning score is further coupled with local mitigation through write-time quarantine and retrieval-time reweighting. Experiments on four benchmarks, namely MIMIC-III, eICU, WebShop, and MMLU, show that FEMP-GUARD consistently outperforms representative federated baselines, achieving the best AUC, F1, Precision, Recall, and Early Warning Rate while also producing earlier warnings and favorable security–utility trade-offs. These results demonstrate that retrieval-conditioned federated early warning provides an effective and practical defense paradigm for protecting memory-augmented consumer AI agents against slow and stealthy poisoning behaviors.

papers.title: Toward Efficient Semi-Asynchronous Federated Learning: A Multi-Factor Grouping and Dual-Level Selection Scheme Under Heterogeneous Environments
papers.abstract: Semi-Asynchronous Federated Learning (SAFL) takes advantage of both synchronous and asynchronous FLs to train models. However, existing works in semi-asynchronous FLs fail to fully account for heterogeneities in both data and devices. To address these issues, we first propose a Clustered SAFL (CSAFL) framework and theoretically analyze its convergence loss. Then, a convergence loss minimization problem is formulated under the considerations of heterogeneities in device resources, fairness of cluster selection, and data heterogeneity. To address this complex problem due to nonlinearities and multi-dimensional decision variables, we first design a device clustering algorithm based on both devices’ model parameter differences and gradient directions between local and global models. Then, the original loss minimization problem is transformed into inter- and intra-cluster selection problems. For the inter-cluster selection problem, to ensure fairness, we propose a reinforcement learning-driven Lyapunov approach to fairly select clusters, where reinforcement learning (RL) is used to supervise the cluster selection results by the Lyapunov method. For the intra-cluster selection, we convert it into a constrained multi-armed bandit (MAB) problem in order to let devices within a cluster submit models synchronously. Then, a two-stage Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) scheme is proposed to obtain device selection results. Extensive numerical results with baselines show that our approach achieves up to 25% higher accuracy.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Federated Learning of Satellite Aided Computation in LEO Ubiquitous Edge Computing Networks
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence and low-earth orbit (LEO) satellite edge computing technology, there has been a rapid increase in the demand for intelligence networks and services among users in remote areas, such as federated learning (FL). We propose a satellite aided computation FL (SACFL) system in LEO ubiquitous edge computing (UEC) networks, aiming at improving the efficiency of FL tasks in remote areas. In the considered deployment scenario, the following key factors are considered: 1) terrestrial users in remote areas; 2) offloading data to satellites for aided computation; and 3) global aggregation on satellite. However, the highly dynamic characteristics and the uneven distribution of satellite computation resources pose significant challenges to the low-delay requirements of satellite-based FL tasks. To this end, we formulate an optimization problem to minimize delay by jointly considering access selection, computation offloading, aggregation satellite (AgS) selection, and computation resource allocation. To solve the formulated problem, we propose a novel multi-agent alternating (M2A) optimization method. Specifically, three independent agents are trained alternately to make decisions on access selection, computation offloading, and AgS selection. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other benchmark algorithms in terms of convergence, delay, and FL accuracy.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: PFAdapter: Hierarchical LoRA Decomposition for Personalized Federated MLLMs
papers.abstract: Agentic AI systems are reshaping communications and networking by deploying autonomous intelligent agents capable of collaborative learning while maintaining data privacy at network edges. Within distributed network environments, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) serve as cognitive engines for edge devices, yet federated fine-tuning faces substantial challenges in balancing global knowledge aggregation with local adaptation under heterogeneous network conditions. Conventional federated protocols typically rely on uniform parameter aggregation, which conflates domain-invariant features with client-specific nuances, thereby resulting in suboptimal personalization and excessive communication overhead. To address these challenges, we propose PFAdapter, a communication-efficient framework introducing hierarchical LoRA decomposition to explicitly separate adapter parameters into global-shared and local-private components. Query and key projections are assigned to global synchronization for capturing universal multimodal semantics across the network, while value and output projections remain localized for edge-specific adaptation. Additionally, orthogonality regularization based on the Frobenius norm enforces strict separation between these components, preventing redundant feature learning. Selective aggregation protocols synchronize only global-shared components across the federated network, preserving local expertise and reducing communication costs by nearly 50%. Extensive experiments on VQA-RAD, SLAKE, Hateful Memes, and CrisisMMD datasets demonstrate that PFAdapter consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving accuracy improvements ranging from 2.4% to 4.8% across diverse edge intelligence tasks. Consequently, our framework establishes an efficient solution for agentic AI deployment in resource-constrained communication networks.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Temporal-augmented Source-Free Domain Adaptation for Secure and Robust Federated Time-series Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative model training without exposing raw data, making it well-suited for privacy-sensitive time-series applications. Yet its effectiveness is limited by the scarcity of labeled client data and the substantial heterogeneity across clients. Federated source-free domain adaptation (F-SFDA) alleviates this limitation by allowing the server to pretrain a model on labeled source data while requiring clients to adapt locally using only their unlabeled target data. However, the success of F-SFDA critically depends on the quality of client-side adaptation, which is difficult to ensure under heterogeneous temporal distributions and often leads to noisy updates, client drift, and unstable global convergence. To address these, this work proposes Temporal-augmented sOurce-free Domain Adaptation (TODA), a plug-and-play method designed to provide secure and robust adaptation for federated time-series learning. TODA follows a federated dual-stage design: the server first learns transferable temporal structures from source data, and clients subsequently use these frozen structures as priors to guide source-free adaptation with only local unlabeled data. Two complementary temporal modules are introduced to capture essential time-series characteristics, enabling comprehensive modeling of long-term dependency and temporal proximity. By enforcing temporal structural consistency during client adaptation, TODA mitigates client drift and enhances the security and stability of global aggregation under shifting temporal distributions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TODA consistently improves adaptation performance, outperforming baselines by up to 36.24% in average accuracy and 39.34% in average macro F1-score. Combining TODA with the F-SFDA frameworks significantly enhances their safety and robustness.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: KidneyGuard-FedXAI: A Trustworthy Federated Explainable AI Framework with Adversarial Defense and Privacy-Preserving Mechanisms for Secure Consumer-Centric Kidney Cancer Diagnostics
papers.abstract: Consumer-facing kidney cancer diagnostics encounter persistent challenges, including privacy risk, data scarcity, and limited model transparency, which undermine trustworthiness in healthcare systems. This paper presents KidneyGuard-FedXAI, a trustworthy federated and explainable AI framework that integrates proactive defense against adversarial threats and privacy-preserving protocols for secure kidney cancer detection in consumer applications. The framework employs differential privacy-enhanced federated learning with gradient compression, adversarial training, and LIME-based explainability and supports cyber threat analysis to ensure robust, interpretable, and privacy-compliant diagnostics. Gradient compression reduces communication overhead while preserving feature-level information critical for LIME-based local explanations, thereby jointly enhancing both efficiency and diagnostic interpretability. Our approach addresses critical gaps in current kidney cancer detection systems by providing consumer-accessible explanations while maintaining data sovereignty across distributed healthcare institutions. Experimental validation on multi-institutional kidney datasets demonstrates superior performance with 94.7% accuracy, 92.3% sensitivity, and 96.1% specificity, while ensuring privacy preservation with ϵ-differential privacy guarantees. The framework reduces communication overhead by 67% compared to conventional federated approaches and provides clinically meaningful explanations with 89.2% physician agreement scores. Overall, KidneyGuard-FedXAI advances trustworthy consumer applications by uniting privacy preservation, explainability, and proactive defense for kidney cancer diagnostics in distributed healthcare environments.

papers.title: FedSADP-IDS: Self-Adaptive Differential Privacy Federated Intrusion Detection with Risk-Sensitive Gradient Selection for Internet of Vehicles
ExplainCRC: A Women-Centric Consumer Wearable Framework for Privacy-Preserving Efficacy Stratification in RAS/RAF-Wildtype Colorectal Cancer
papers.abstract: The integration of intelligent consumer electronics into FemTech offers unprecedented opportunities for personalized oncology. However, deploying multimodal wearable systems to monitor treatment responses in specific molecular subtypes, such as RAS/RAF-wildtype colorectal cancer (CRC) in women, requires stringent privacy safeguards and clinical interpretability on edge devices. This paper presents ExplainCRC, an edge-deployable, privacy-preserving consumer wearable framework tailored for the efficacy stratification of female patients with RAS/RAF-wildtype CRC. ExplainCRC fuses consumer-grade sensor streams—photoplethysmography (PPG), electrodermal activity (EDA), skin temperature, and acceleration—into a unified representation using a multilayered attention encoder network. To establish trust with clinical experts and female patients, we employ layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP) to quantify the temporal contributions of each sensor stream to health outcome predictions. Addressing the critical privacy demands of women’s health data, the system leverages federated learning secured by a Gaussian differential privacy mechanism (ϵ = 2.8, δ = 10−5). Furthermore, we developed a mixed-precision model compression pipeline optimizing ExplainCRC for seamless execution on mobile platforms. Extensive evaluations across three public datasets—WESAD, PPG-DaLiA, and TCGA-COAD (utilizing genomic features as static surrogates for outcomes in a 3-category scheme)—demonstrate robust performance. Explain-CRC achieves a high explanation fidelity (0.867 and 0.843 on the two wearable benchmarks; 0.863 averaged across all three), and its throughput on a mid-range mobile platform reaches 21.4 frames per second for the compressed model (12.8 FPS for the full model), a 1.67× latency reduction relative to its own uncompressed counterpart. These technical results motivate, but do not yet establish, a path toward home-based monitoring of targeted-therapy responses, which will require dedicated clinical data collection and validation.

papers.title: TwinChain: Secure Digital Twin–Driven Edge Offloading for Real-Time Consumer IoT Applications
papers.abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) networks has increased the importance of effective task offloading techniques that provide better tradeoffs between energy efficiency, latency, and trust. Current task offloading techniques are mostly based on static scheduling and control, which are not effective in responding to dynamic network environments and are more prone to manipulation attacks in distributed IoT networks. This article proposesTwinChain, a five-stage framework that combines DT-based predictive simulation with Proof-of-Evaluation (PoE) consensus to ensure secure, timely, and energy-efficient task scheduling for IoT networks. TwinChain introduces a closed-loop task offloading technique where DT-based predictive simulation and Proof of Evaluation-based verification are used to ensure secure and efficient task scheduling for IoT networks. The framework starts with task mirroring, which uses digital twin technology to simulate task execution across heterogeneous servers. The Adaptive Evolutionary Twin-based Offloading Scheduler (AETOS) helps each digital twin predictively estimate delay, energy, and trust costs for each possible path. The predicted values are processed using MOFTwin, a federated multi-objective optimizer that computes a global offloading schedule considering capacity and deadline constraints. The offloading schedule is validated using the PoE consensus algorithm and stored as a hashed entry in a distributed ledger managed by digital twin validators. The execution feedback is used to improve the accuracy of digital twin predictions. The simulation results using NS-3, considering 1000 IoT devices and 12 performance metrics, show that TwinChain reduces energy consumption by 21.6%, latency by 29.3%, and achieves an 88.4% task success rate, even at 20% network failures. The simulation results show that TwinChain outperforms six state-of-the-art models while providing scalable trust and reliable offloading for next-generation IoT systems, as envisioned for 6G and cyberphysical systems.

papers.title: Federated Edge Learning Based Multi-Drone Optimal Delivery Routing Approach
papers.abstract: In low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs), multi drone delivery operation poses a crucial challenge for advancing the sustainable development in smart cities. However, existing research studies have only tackled either energy consumption or trajectory optimization problems of multi-drones, disregarding the quality of delivery services. To address this problem, we propose a federated edge learning based multi-drone optimal delivery routing approach, aiming to provide optimal delivery paths under realistic route constraints. Specifically, we formulate the optimization problem as a mixed-integer linear programming problem and solve it in a distributed manner. Meanwhile, the utilization of federated edge learning (FEL) method contributes to the accurate prediction in drone delivery travel time. To assess the effectiveness of the proposed model and its constituent parts, we carry out in-depth case studies. Our case studies show that the proposed approach can efficiently achieve the high quality of delivery services in the different scale of LAWNs. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that the distributed approach produces near optimal solutions in low computational time.

papers.title: Reinforcement Federated Learning With Clustering Expertise for Privacy-Aware Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Reliable detection of unprecedented anomalies is essential in large scale photovoltaic (PV) plants to prevent potential cascade failures. However, operations and maintenance practices in utility-scale plants are highly optimized, making real anomaly events infrequent and rarely observed. Thus, the recorded PV plant database lacks the information on labeled faults. To overcome this, data from multiple PV sites of several independent producers is aggregated, but privacy concerns limit collaborative learning. To address these limitations, a Reinforcement Federated Learning with Clustering eXpertise (ReFLeCX) framework is proposed for distributed PV anomaly detection. The methodology supports both privacy preservation concerns and provides label-efficient learning. It integrates ramp-rate cluster engineering using deep Q-network augmented by long short-term memory.
