Reinforcement layer uses optimal classification policies that learn using reward signals derived from clustering metrics and pseudo-labeled anomalies inferred through ramp-rate threshold. The agent is trained locally at each site and federated learning optimizes the aggregated model parameters and updates across sites without transferring raw measurements. The methodology implements FedDyn aggregation strategy to provide robustness under non independent and identically distributed data conditions and mitigate the data distribution drift across temporal changes. Thus, enhancing the global generalization across heterogeneous operating environmental conditions. The proposed ReFLeCX framework is evaluated on real-world multi-site PV datasets, demonstrating improved anomaly separability and cluster coherence. The results prove that the model is suitable for scalable, privacy-aware deployment in industrial PV monitoring systems.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Privacy-Preserving Federated Distillation for Collaborative Intrusion Detection in Heterogeneous Industrial CPS
papers.abstract: Despite the widespread implementation of various intrusion detection systems (IDSs) in industrial cyber-physical systems (CPS), significant challenges persist, including class imbalance, detection paradox, privacy gap, and arbitrary aggregation. To address these challenges, this article proposes a novel Transformer-based detection with federated privacy-collaborative IDS (TDFP-CIDS) for industrial CPS. First, a Transformer-enhanced external classifier generative adversarial network is designed with Wasserstein distance constraints and label conditioning to stabilize gradient descent, achieving robust semi-supervised classification for class-imbalanced industrial traffic. Second, a hierarchical out-of-distribution detection protocol is proposed to decouple known attack classification and zero-day attack identification into two cascaded stages, resolving the feature entanglement defect of existing single-stage detection frameworks. Third, an adaptive local differential privacy mechanism is integrated into gradient updates to achieve provable privacy guarantees while maintaining detection accuracy. Finally, a decentralized federated distillation scheme is developed to enable architecture-agnostic collaborative training across heterogeneous industrial nodes, realizing the deep integration of knowledge distillation and federated learning without exchanging raw traffic data or model parameters. Experimental results on a real-world industrial CPS dataset show that TDFP-CIDS outperforms state-of-the-art IDS solutions with exceptional detection performance for sparse rare attacks and zero-day attacks.

papers.title: Decoding the Enigma of Collaborative Intrusion Detection Systems: Ensemble Learning vs Federated Learning in the Battle for Collaborative Anomaly Detection Supremacy
papers.abstract: Coordinated attacks, such as large-scale scanning, worm outbreaks, and Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, exhibit distributed cyberattack characteristics that make them challenging to detect with standalone Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS). Collaborative Intrusion Detection Systems (CIDS) address this limitation by aggregating data from multiple network sources and leveraging collective intelligence for anomaly detection, making them more effective in identifying coordinated attacks. CIDS system employs Ensemble Learning (EL) or Federated Learning (FL) to build robust collaborative anomaly detection. EL enhances detection by integrating predictions from multiple models, while FL enables model aggregation from multiple models and preserves privacy. This research examines the comparative effectiveness of EL and FL within CIDS for robust detection of coordinated attacks in heterogeneous network environments. Benchmarking results reveal that network heterogeneity significantly influences detection model performance. Furthermore, this study provides key insights and lessons learned from the comparative analysis, offering a foundation for future research on cyberattack detection using collaborative anomaly detection methods in CIDS.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: FedAggVerify: Publicly Verifiable and Privacy-Preserving Aggregation With Ownership Protection for Federated Learning
papers.abstract: We present${\sf FedAggVerify}$, a novel single-server federated learning (FL) aggregation protocol and the first to providepublicly verifiable, non-interactiveintegrity proofs for each training round while preserving client-update privacy andparticipation anonymity, even when the aggregator is malicious and colludes with compromised clients. Prior publicly verifiable aggregation schemes either lose soundness under server–client collusion or rely on helper-mediated co-signing and recovery procedures that place an adversarial server on the critical path and create availability and communication bottlenecks.${\sf FedAggVerify}$makes inconsistencies between the accepted client contributions and the released aggregate externally verifiable, supports off-path forensic auditing, and binds released models to the owner through an Error Correction Code-protected signature watermark for intellectual-property protection. We formalize correctness, soundness, client-update indistinguishability, and ownership binding under standard cryptographic assumptions. Experiments using real cryptographic primitives and large model dimensions demonstrate practical efficiency and substantially lower communication, verification, and dropout-recovery overhead than prior publicly verifiable aggregation baselines while maintaining verifiable watermark recovery.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Context-Aware Dynamic-Trigger Backdoor Attack in Federated Industrial Intrusion Detection Systems
papers.abstract: Industrial intrusion detection systems (IIDS) secure industrial networks but need diverse data for training. Data sharing across organizations risks privacy, making centralized learning impractical. Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative training without data exchange but is vulnerable to backdoor attacks. Existing backdoor studies mainly target image-based FL, using visual triggers unsuitable for network data with heterogeneous and semantically sensitive features. Network data differ fundamentally from image pixels, making naive manipulation detectable. Most approaches also rely on multiple attackers or rounds (multishot), and modify labels, ignoring the single-shot, protocol-compliant setting of federated IIDS. We propose context-aware dynamic-trigger backdoor attack, a single-shot and multishot, label-consistent, and protocol-compliant backdoor attack for federated IIDS that shows how a calculated context-aware trigger strategy can easily compromise federated IIDS and highlights the need for stronger defenses. Using lightweight feature adaptation and context-aware trigger generation, CDB attack achieves high attack success and stealth on four IIoT datasets compared with five attacks and five defense baselines, highlighting urgent need for resilient federated defense methods.

papers.title: GUARD: Mitigating Backdoors in Federated Learning Via Influence-Guided Unlearning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is increasingly vulnerable to backdoor attacks, where malicious participants inject poisoned updates to implant hidden behaviors within the global model. Existing defenses often rely on ad-hoc aggregation rules, heuristic parameter modifications, or external trusted datasets, severely limiting their robustness, interpretability, and transferability across diverse architectures and attack modalities. To address these fundamental limitations, we propose a Guided Unlearning for Adversarial Robustness and Defense (i.e.,GUARD). It is a unified, data-centric framework, which leverages the principles of machine unlearning to systematically secure FL systems. Specifically,GUARDestablishes a rigorous theoretical link between data influence estimation and backdoor mitigation. It utilizes fast influence-function approximation to efficiently isolate poisoned training contributions without requiring auxiliary clean data. Building on this precise detection, the framework executes a sequential, closed-loop defense pipeline: an influence-guided unlearning stage that explicitly neutralizes malicious parameter biases through reverse optimization, followed by a stability-preserving lightweight fine-tuning stage on internally verified clean data to seamlessly restore standard predictive performance. Comprehensive experiments across diverse datasets, advanced backdoor attacks, and model architectures demonstrate thatGUARDachieves superior threat eradication and clean accuracy preservation compared to state-of-the-art baselines. By transforming backdoor removal into a causally interpretable unlearning process, this work offers a highly robust and principled pathway toward trustworthy FL.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: FedML Parrot: A Scalable Federated Learning Simulation System via Heterogeneity-aware Scheduling on Hierarchical Sequential Training
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborations among clients to train machine learning models while protecting their data privacy. Existing FL simulation platforms, designed from the perspectives of traditional distributed training, suffer from laborious code migration between simulation and production, low efficiency, low GPU utility, low scalability with high hardware requirements, and difficulty in simulating stateful clients. In this work, we demystify the challenges and bottlenecks of simulating FL and design a new FL system named FedML Parrot. It improves the training efficiency, remarkably relaxes the hardware requirements, and supports efficient large-scale FL experiments with stateful clients by: (1) sequentially training clients on devices; (2) decomposing original aggregation into local and global aggregation on devices and server respectively; (3) scheduling tasks to mitigate straggler problems and enhance computing utility; (4) distributed client state manager to support various FL algorithms. In addition, built upon our generic APIs and communication interfaces, users can seamlessly transform the simulation into real-world deployment without modifying codes. We evaluate Parrot through extensive experiments for training diverse models on various FL datasets to demonstrate that Parrot can achieve simulating over 1000 clients (stateful or stateless) with flexible GPU device settings (4 ∼ 32) and high GPU utility, 1.2 ∼ 4 times faster than FedScale, and 10 ∼ 100 times memory saving than FedML. And we verify that Parrot works well with homogeneous and heterogeneous devices in three different clusters. Two FL algorithms with stateful clients and four algorithms with stateless clients are simulated to verify the wide adaptability of Parrot to different algorithms.

papers.title: Encrypted Yet Compromised: A Covert Channel in Homomorphic Encryption-based Federated Learning
papers.abstract: To enhance confidentiality and privacy in Federated Learning (FL) systems, Homomorphic Encryption (HE) is incorporated, which allows the server to aggregate encrypted model updates. However, existing studies have largely overlooked that HE-protected model updates can also be exploited as covert communication channels between colluding malicious clients. This study introduces a novel steganographic mechanism that establishes covert communication channels within FL frameworks secured by the HE algorithm. The proposed method enables colluding clients to embed and transmit hidden messages through model update weights without being detected by the central server or honest participants. To achieve this, we present a spectral-domain embedding technique that adaptively manipulates the magnitude coefficients to encode secret bits while maintaining statistical normality and model integrity. We further design a lightweight server-side defense based on HE-compatible noise injection to disrupt such a covert channel. Comprehensive experiments conducted under representative HE-FL settings with benchmark datasets (MNIST and CIFAR-10) demonstrate the effectiveness and resilience of the proposed attack and defense schemes within the evaluated scenarios. Specifically, our method achieves a high-capacity message embedding of 512 bits per round with nearly zero bit error rate extraction by the receiver in attack scenario. In contrast, under the proposed defense, the bit error rate increases from 0 to 0.17 with Gaussian noise ($std$= 0.1), while reducing the accuracy of the FL model by less than 2%, demonstrating an acceptable mitigation with minimal impact on learning performance.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Self-Correcting Client-Initiated Gradient Inversion via Adaptive Diffusion Control
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) ostensibly safeguards data privacy by sharing only model updates. However, gradient inversion attacks (GIAs) have exposed critical vulnerabilities in this paradigm. While prior literature predominantly assumes a privileged server-side adversary, this work addresses the more insidious and practical threat of client-initiated attacks. Existing client-initiated methodologies remain fragile, treating inversion as a static, single-shot optimization problem that frequently succumbs to catastrophic optimization collapse due to the stochastic nature of FL dynamics. To overcome these limitations, we proposeDCPT(i.e., Diffusion-driven Client-initiated Privacy Theft), a resilient framework that shifts the paradigm toward multi-stage adaptive inversion. Specifically, DCPT integrates a novel adaptive control framework with a closed-loop feedback mechanism, monitoring reconstruction fidelity to dynamically alternate betweenExploitationandExploration, thereby achievingself-correcting. To further guarantee robustness against gradient drift, we incorporate a rolling history constraint fortemporal regularizationand abilevel optimizationfor on-the-fly prior adaptation. Extensive experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 demonstrate that DCPT achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction fidelity. Crucially, it also achieves unprecedented multi-round stability and resilience, highlighting the urgent need for advanced defenses against generative client-initiated adversaries.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: AAFLIS: Resources-Efficient Adaptive Asynchronous Federated Learning for Image Segmentation in Edge Computing Environment
papers.abstract: Image segmentation is critical in edge computing for real-time medical imaging, surveillance, and autonomous driving—where localized, low-latency processing matters—and federated learning (FL), preserving privacy via local data and enabling collaborative training, is increasingly used to advance it. However, traditional synchronous FL faces challenges in such edge environments, including low communication efficiency, resource waste, and poor model convergence caused by data and device heterogeneity, which limit segmentation performance. To address these issues, we propose AAFLIS, an adaptive asynchronous federated image segmentation framework that integrates momentum acceleration and dynamic coordination mechanisms to achieve efficient and robust distributed training. Specifically, 1) a momentum-based iteration update mechanism is employed to accelerate local model training, effectively overcoming discrepancies in device computing power; 2) the theoretical convergence upper bound under resource constraints is derived, laying a mathematical foundation for algorithm optimization; 3) an optimization model for the number of local iterations under resource constraints is proposed to minimize global loss function. Experimental results show that AAFLIS achieves up to 1221.16% higher Dice score with substantial time and energy savings over baselines under three IID image segmentation settings, and attains a peak Dice improvement of 248.68% on the Non-IID Carvana dataset while likewise reducing computational time and energy resources.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: A Communication-Efficient Uncertainty-Aware OPF Method for Distribution-Microgrid Coordination via Event-Triggered Federated Aggregation
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a communication-efficient federated uncertainty-aware Optimal Power Flow (OPF) method with event-triggered federated aggregation for distribution-microgrid coordinated operation under uncertainty. First, we propose a novel federated architecture and uncertainty-aware OPF model, and an event-triggered mechanism is introduced to reduce communication between the distribution network and microgrids while preserving the timeliness of uncertainty representation. Second, we establish a distributed rolling coordination framework for privacy-preserving cross-domain OPF, and introduce a warm-start strategy to reduce repeated iterations and improve online coordination efficiency in adjacent windows. Third, a lightweight feasibility-and-reliability support mechanism with closed-loop safety-margin adaptation and execution-layer affine compensation is developed to enhance online feasibility and reliability under uncertainty, thereby maintaining performance with limited communication and computational overhead. Finally, case studies on the IEEE 33-bus and 69-bus systems demonstrate that, compared with existing methods, the proposed method reduces the total communication volume to 33.3% while maintaining comparable feasibility and reliability performance.

papers.title: Differentially Private Decoupled Clustered Federated Learning under Mixed Heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) facilitates collaborative model training without sharing local data, yet it grapples with issues of gradient leakage and data heterogeneity. Existing solutions utilize Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD) to safeguard client model gradients, while the server uses gradient similarity to group and aggregate client models, thereby adapting to diverse data distributions. However, in mixed heterogeneous data environments, FL faces significant challenges due to the coexistence of concept and label distribution shift, which jointly impact client model gradients and render mainstream client grouping methods ineffective. To address this problem, we introduce Decoupled Clustered Federated Learning (DeCFL), a privacy-preserving Clustered Federated Learning (CFL) framework that can disentangle the effects of concept and label distribution shift to enable model grouping. On the client side, we design a gradient-variance-based label distribution metric leveraging noisy gradients to estimate label distributions without incurring additional privacy costs. On the server side, we develop concept-aware clustering using regression residuals from label-to-gradient similarity mapping for precise client grouping. Moreover, we propose a hierarchical aggregation mechanism that assigns aggregation weights to classification layers based on label distributions, thereby reducing the interference of underfitted classes on cluster models. Extensive experiments conducted on MNIST, FMNIST and CIFAR datasets demonstrate that DeCFL performs excellently in mixed heterogeneous environments.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: A Distributed Difference-Aware Alignment Framework for Robust Federated Graph Learning
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Autonomous CSI Prediction Framework for O-RAN-Enabled 5G mmWave Vehicular Networks
papers.abstract: Establishing and maintaining 5 G mmWave vehicular connectivity poses a challenge due to high user mobility, requiring the design of robust and efficient beam switching procedures. Unlike reactive beam switching based on channel state information (CSI) feedback received from vehicular users, proactive beam switching exploits CSI prediction to prepare in advance for upcoming beam switching decisions. In this paper, we develop a framework forautonomousandself-trainableCSI prediction for mmWave vehicular users. In the proposed framework, base stations (gNBs) collect and label data sets to train a CSI prediction model both independently and using federated learning (FL). The data set combines data extracted from the CSI feedback and cellular vehicle-to-everything (C-V2X) cooperative awareness messages (CAMs) of surrounding vehicles. The framework is placed in the context of machine learning and artificial intelligence (ML/AI)-based Open RAN (O-RAN) applications (rApps and xApps) fed by realistic real-world mobility and CSI data from the DeepMIMO simulator. Detailed evaluation results demonstrate feasibility, accuracy, and flexibility of the proposed CSI prediction framework.

papers.title: Dynamic Weighting and Adaptive Sparse Transformer for Federated Fault Diagnosis
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of the Internet of Things (IoT) and edge computing, the scale and complexity of modern networks have increased significantly, driving the demand for distributed fault diagnosis. Federated learning (FL) effectively addresses the issues of data privacy and dispersion by enabling edge devices to collaboratively train models without sharing raw data. However, existing FL-based fault diagnosis methods still encounter the following challenges. Firstly, static aggregation strategies struggle to balance the contributions of heterogeneous clients dynamically. Secondly, traditional local models are unable to effectively decouple sparse high and low-frequency features in fault signals, thereby limiting the accuracy of fault identification. Finally, the resource constraints of edge devices restrict the deployment of complex diagnostic models. To address these challenges, we propose a federated learning hybrid dynamic weight adjustment method based on delay and model quality, introducing the concept of “accelerated depreciation” in accounting and taxation and the concept of “asset allocation” in economics to improve the communication efficiency of fault diagnosis and reduce the impact of delay differences due to device heterogeneity on the effect of fault diagnosis. Additionally, we propose an adaptive sparse low high frequencies Transformer, introducing a lightweight attention mechanism and an adaptive feature extraction layer, which significantly reduces the computational overhead while maintaining high diagnostic accuracy. The experimental results show that, compared with the most competitive baseline, our method improves the fault diagnosis accuracy by 1% on the Case Western Reserve University Bearing dataset (CWRU), 0.78% on the Xi’an Jiaotong University Gearbox dataset (XJTU), and 0.44% on the Micro service Edge Computing dataset (MICRO).
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning Via Dual-Signal Period Control for Edge Networks
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a privacy-preserving distributed training paradigm in which clients collaboratively optimize a global model by periodically synchronizing with a central server. In mobile services, including vehicular networks, clients generate heterogeneous (Non-IID) data under latency and bandwidth constraints. This heterogeneity and dynamic connectivity increase communication overhead. Although local computation can reduce the number of synchronizations, communication still accounts for more than 80% of the total training time. Therefore, communication remains a key bottleneck to the scalability of FL systems. The communication period$\tau$plays a crucial role in the tradeoff between convergence speed and communication efficiency. However, a fixed$\tau$is inherently inflexible. Furthermore, existing adaptive schemes depend on a single historical-loss signal, which delays the mitigation of client gradient conflicts in Non-IID data scenarios. In this paper, we propose Dual-Signal Adaptive Period Control (DS-APC), which adopts a real-time gradient-conflict degree with the loss trend to adjust$\tau$promptly. DS-APC further employs a hybrid attention-based aggregation mechanism that exploits gradient quality and performance indicators. It also incorporates an accuracy-based early-stopping rule for IID settings and a dynamic temperature scheduling strategy for Non-IID settings. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10, Tiny-ImageNet, STL-10, and SVHN show that, under IID settings, DS-APC improves accuracy over the best baseline by 7.6% on average, and accelerates convergence by reducing training time by about 36% on average. Under Non-IID settings, DS-APC further achieves an average accuracy improvement of 6.6% within fixed time budgets.

papers.title: DAL-FedMF: A Lightweight and Privacy-Preserving Federated Recommendation Framework for Consumer Edge Devices
papers.abstract: Deploying personalized recommender systems on consumer edge devices is impeded by privacy regulations prohibiting centralized data collection and by hardware limits on privacy-preserving computation. Existing federated recommendation approaches either incur prohibitive overhead through cryptographic protocols, suffer from an inherent privacy-utility trade-off via noise-based perturbation, or fail to protect interaction metadata. In response, we propose DAL-FedMF, a privacy-preserving federated matrix factorization framework that breaks this trade-off through a trusted party authority (TPA)-assisted double-anonymization protocol. This protocol enables clients to recover exact global gradients while ensuring the server observes only formally protected updates at minimal computational cost. To accommodate stringent edge resource constraints, we further develop the DAL-FedMF-Light variant via hybrid event-triggered and sparsification mechanisms. Experimental results on three real-world datasets demonstrate that our approach guarantees high recommendation accuracy comparable to non-private baselines, significantly outperforms existing alternatives in efficiency, and provides robust defense against gradient reconstruction and linkage attacks.

papers.title: FL-MPS: Secure Federated LLM Fine-Tuning via Adaptive Parameter Split and Efficient Negotiation
papers.abstract: Security and efficiency are two desirable properties of federated learning (FL). Homomorphic encryption (HE) is widely adopted to enforce data security for FL participants. However, existing solutions based on HE treat FL as a general computation task and apply HE protections indiscriminately at each step without considering FL computations' inherent characteristics, leading to unsatisfactory efficiency. In contrast, we find that the convergence process of FL generally consists of two phases, and the differences between these two phases can be exploited to improve the efficiency of secure FL solutions. In this paper, we propose a secure and fast FL solution named FLSwitch by tailoring different security protections for different learning phases. FLSwitch consists of three novel components, a new secure aggregation protocol based on the Pailliar HE and a residue number coding system outperforming the STATE-of-the-art HE-based solutions, a fast FL aggregation protocol with an extremely light overhead of learning on ciphertexts, and a learning STATE-aware decision model to switch between two protocols during an FL task. Since exploiting FL characteristics is orthogonal to optimizing HE techniques, FLSwitch can be applied to the existing HE-based FL solutions with cutting-edge optimizations, which could further boost secure FL efficiency.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: RBPFL: Redactable Blockchain for Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning in IoV
papers.abstract: Asynchronous federated learning (AFL) improves the adaptability of federated learning (FL) to dynamic Internet of Vehicles (IoV) environments by reducing communication latency during model aggregation. The inherent network asynchrony of the directed acyclic graph (DAG) blockchain further facilitates the deployment of AFL within IoV. However, the immutability and transparency of blockchain pose critical challenges, such as limited storage capacity at edge nodes and potential privacy leakage of shared model parameters. To address these issues, we propose RBPFL, a novel FL framework that combines redactable blockchain with trusted execution environments (TEEs) by leveraging Intel software guard extension (SGX). The redactable blockchain utilizes a dual-layer architecture, consisting of a model storage layer based on the DAG blockchain and a redaction layer based on the hyperledger Fabric blockchain. The model storage layer stores local and global model updates, while the redaction layer, equipped with SGX-enabled processors, securely executes smart contracts and computes chameleon hash collisions to enable controlled on-chain data redaction. Furthermore, RBPFL employs TEE-based secure aggregation to protect the privacy of model parameters during local model aggregation. Finally, we comprehensively evaluate the performance of the proposed RBPFL framework through experiments with various recurrent neural network (RNN) models and datasets to demonstrate its practical effectiveness.

papers.title: Low-Latency Wireless Multimodal Federated Learning Via Semantic-Aware Client Scheduling
papers.abstract: Multimodal federated learning (MFL) over wireless links faces significant challenges due to limited bandwidth, heterogeneous client resources, and non-IID data distributions. In this paper, we propose a semantic-aware multi-agent bandit (SMAB) scheduling framework for wireless MFL, which jointly performs client selection and channel assignment based on compact semantic features instead of full model updates. To quantify the utility of local data, we introduce three semantic metrics, namely coverage, diversity, and contribution potential. Moreover, long-term participation constraints are adopted to replace rigid per-round selection requirements, thereby improving both fairness and scheduling flexibility. The proposed SMAB algorithm combines upper confidence bound (UCB)-based exploration with Lyapunov virtual queues to balance latency minimization, client participation fairness, and energy constraints. Experimental results on a custom multimodal MNIST–AudioMNIST benchmark show that SMAB significantly reduces training latency while maintaining or improving model accuracy compared with random and round-robin baselines. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective trade-off between communication efficiency and learning performance in resource-constrained wireless MFL systems.

papers.title: HongAvg: Hierarchical On-Demand Cognitive Split Federated Learning for Twin Agent Orchestration
papers.abstract: Fusing digital twins (DTs) with world models (WMs) promises a leap from reactive monitoring to proactive control. However, deploying high-fidelity WMs faces a fundamental cognitive gap: the immense computational demand of foundation models conflicts with the resource constraints of 6G edge nodes, while privacy regulations hinder the centralization of raw sensory data required for training. To bridge this gap, this paper presents HongAvg, a hierarchical on-demand cognitive split federated learning framework designed as cognitive infrastructure for next-generation DTs. By establishing a national-basin-edge three-tier architecture, HongAvg introduces foundation models to resource-constrained edges via split computing, offloading heavy cognitive reasoning while preserving data privacy. We propose a dual-stream semantic consistency mechanism to align edge interactions with the foundation model's cognition, ensuring that distributed cognitive primitives serve as valid inputs for global state estimation. Validated on a heterogeneous benchmark, HongAvg serves as a prototype for industrial cognitive computing, improving accuracy in visual monitoring by up to 8.9% and reducing edge memory usage by approximately 75%. This work provides the scalable architectural prerequisite necessary for evolving static DTs into proactive WM-driven multi-agent orchestrated intelligent systems.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: FedShard-DES: Federated Multi-objective Sharded Blockchain for Real-time Secure Smart Home Consumer Electronics
papers.abstract: Smart-home consumer electronics (CE) sharded blockchains face a configuration dilemma: node-resource information is scattered across home gateways, while shard configuration requires global coordination. Centralized optimization exposes local resource states, making it difficult to balance real-time performance and security-related risk exposure. To address this problem, this paper proposes FedShard-DES, a FedPareto-driven double-elite-selection framework for federated multi-objective optimization of sharded blockchain configuration. The proposed model jointly optimizes shard failure probability, transaction throughput, decentralization entropy, and consensus latency. In FedShard-DES, each CE client locally performs double-elite-selection evolutionary search and uploads only its Pareto archive instead of raw node-resource data. The coordinator aggregates local archives through non-dominated sorting, Minkowski-distance-based truncation, and feedback of representative Pareto solutions to support distributed Pareto optimization. Experiments on the smart-home sharded blockchain model and WFG benchmark suites show that FedShard-DES obtains a favorable security-oriented trade-off compared with centralized and federated baselines. The representative and default-budget validations further show that FedShard-DES maintains favorable trade-off performance under comparable federated settings.

papers.title: Failure-Aware Intelligent Task Offloading for Dynamic Vehicular Fog Computing Enabled by GNN-Based Federated Advantage Actor-Critic Learning
papers.abstract: Vehicular fog computing (VFC) enhances compute-intensive task processing by exploiting idle vehicle resources. However, existing offloading mechanisms may fail due to dynamic factors, such as vehicle mobility, unstable links, and service overload. This paper proposes an offloading-failure-aware (OFA) task offloading scheme (OFA-offloading). Although the exact offloading failure probability is difficult to obtain, it is determined by the service capability of the selected service vehicle (SV). Thus a new tractable metric, i.e., vehicle service capability (VSC), is defined to reflect the offloading failure probability, which is a function of vehicle mobility, resource availability, and link status. Based on VSC of each SV and considering that delay is important for VFC networks, an OFA delay utility is designed. Aiming to maximize this utility, a joint offloading SVs selection and computing resource allocation optimization problem is formulated. Since it is NP-hard and the VFC network is highly dynamic, a novel Graph Neural Network based federated Advantage Actor-Critic (GNN-FAC) algorithm is proposed to solve the problem. GNN-FAC can proactively predict environmental dynamics and incorporate VSC as a critical criterion for offloading decisions. Simulation results demonstrate that compared with existing offloading algorithms, OFA-offloading can improve the OFA delay utility by up to 40%.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Rethinking Byzantine Robustness in Dynamic Federated Learning: Participation-Aware Threats and a Dynamic-Aware Defense
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) systems increasingly adopt dynamic client participation to improve scalability, availability, and resource efficiency. However, existing Byzantine-robust defenses are largely developed under static or stable participation assumptions, which may no longer hold in Dynamic FL. We show that time-varying participation introduces previously overlooked security threats: it can cause the effective malicious ratio among active clients to fluctuate across rounds, potentially exceeding the tolerance threshold of robust aggregation rules, and it can create new temporal attack opportunities for adaptive adversaries. Consequently, Dynamic FL can become substantially more vulnerable than static FL, and its security risk may vary significantly across participation patterns even under the same global malicious ratio. To address these challenges, we proposeDRF(Dynamic-aware Robustness Framework), which detects malicious clients before aggregation and enforces robust learning through cross-round consistency verification over clients’ historical loss behaviors. Unlike existing defenses that rely primarily on within-round filtering, DRF explicitly exploits temporal information across rounds to support dynamic-aware pre-aggregation filtering under the stated loss-reporting assumption. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets under multiple participation patterns demonstrate that DRF consistently outperforms representative defenses and effectively mitigates the new threat surface introduced by time-varying client participation, while maintaining robust and stable model convergence.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Mobility-Assisted Decentralized Federated Learning: Convergence Analysis and a Data-Driven Approach
papers.abstract: Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) has emerged as a privacy-preserving machine learning paradigm that enables collaborative training among users without relying on a central server. However, its performance often degrades significantly due to limited connectivity and data heterogeneity. As we move toward the next generation of wireless networks, mobility is increasingly embedded in many real-world applications. The user mobility, either natural or induced, enables clients to act as relays or bridges, thus enhancing information flow in sparse networks; however, its impact on DFL has been largely overlooked despite its potential. In this work, we systematically investigate the role of mobility in improving DFL performance. We first establish the convergence of DFL in sparse networks under user mobility and theoretically demonstrate that even random movement of a fraction of users can significantly boost performance. Building upon this insight, we propose a DFL framework that utilizes mobile users with induced mobility patterns, allowing them to exploit the knowledge of data distribution to determine their trajectories to enhance information propagation through the network. Through extensive experiments, we empirically confirm our theoretical findings, validate the superiority of our approach over baselines, and provide a comprehensive analysis of how various network parameters influence DFL performance in mobile networks.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: pFedRadar: Personalized Federated Learning for Radar-Based Human Activity Recognition
papers.abstract: Radar-based human activity recognition offers a non-contact solution for IoT-enabled smart environments but faces data insufficiency challenges in real-world deployments. Although aggregating radar data from multiple devices and users can mitigate the limitations of single-source data, sharing raw radar data is often impractical due to privacy concerns, particularly when it contains personal or sensitive information. Considering the inherently non-IID nature of radar data from different nodes, this paper addresses the dual heterogeneity of label and feature distributions in radar-based human activity recognition by proposing a personalized federated learning framework, termed pFedRadar. To mitigate label distribution heterogeneity, we introduce a class-aware structural similarity weighting scheme that enables personalized aggregation based on inter-client relationships. To alleviate feature distribution heterogeneity, we design a learnable historical knowledge fusion mechanism that mitigates the “round drop” phenomenon across communication rounds in FL-based training. The effectiveness of the proposed pFedRadar framework is validated by constructing radar-based human activity datasets under two distinct non-IID settings. Comprehensive experiments against eleven state-of-the-art baselines demonstrate that pFedRadar achieves superior performance in dual non-IID scenarios.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement

papers.title: A Trust-Aware Federated Learning Framework for Cyber-Resilient Edge Digital Twins in Consumer IoT
papers.abstract: With billions of consumer Internet of Things (IoT) devices now embedded in everyday environments, ensuring secure data offloading and the trustworthiness of these devices has become a massive challenge. As the IoT ecosystem integrates with the Digital Twin (DT) for real-time monitoring, smart analysis, and intelligent decision making, it also poses security and trust issues. This paper introduces a novel dual-layer trust framework designed to safeguard consumer IoT based electronics and their associated DT. Unlike existing works on Physical Unclonable Function (PUF)-based trust and trusted-Federated Learning (FL), the proposed framework jointly integrates hardware-rooted PUF authentication, real-time behavioural trust assessment, and trust-weighted FL within a DT environment. At the first layer, a lightweight PUF-based authentication verifies the identity of devices and assigns dynamic trust scores by assessing latency, telemetry consistency, and payload validity. At the second layer, we propose trust-weighted FL, where model updates are aggregated using trust-weighted averaging at the edge DT. This prevents low-trust or compromised devices from influencing the global model, thereby protecting system integrity. The proposed framework was implemented on a real IoT-DT testbed comprising lightweight ESP8266 devices, a DS28E38 PUF-chip, an edge DT server running Eclipse Ditto, along with an MQTT protocol under both normal and adversarial conditions (DoS, SlowITe, and malformed data attacks). Experimental results show that legitimate clients achieved trust scores above 0.90, while malicious clients with scores below the 0.5 threshold were excluded from aggregation. As a result, Trust-FedAvg maintained high detection accuracy (up to 95%) and demonstrated superior robustness compared to standard FedAvg under poisoning attacks. The framework highlights a practical pathway to embedding trust, adaptability, and cyber resilience into next-generation smart home, healthcare, and wearable systems, ultimately enhancing consumer confidence in connected technologies.

papers.title: D 2 OFL: Distillation-Enhanced Diffusion Model Assisted One-Shot Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables multiple clients to jointly train a global model without requiring data to be gathered in a central location. The data in FL setups is not identically and independently distributed (non-IID) across clients. Hence, traditional FL algorithms require multiple communication rounds between the server and participating clients to learn a generalized global model, leading to significant communication overhead. One-shot federated learning (OSFL) reduces communication overhead by enabling global model creation with a single round of communication between participating clients and the server, typically achieved through global synthetic dataset generation or knowledge distillation. With the increasing adoption of diffusion models (DMs), they have been used to generate auxiliary datasets on the server for global model training. However, existing DM-assisted approaches do not directly utilize clients' models and instead rely on auxiliary information shared by clients. Furthermore, current distilled one-shot FL (DOSFL) approaches require public auxiliary data, which violates the privacy principles of FL. To address these limitations, we present D$^{2}$OFL, a distillation-enhanced one-shot federated learning approach that utilizes category-specific client embeddings to synthesize new images at the server and further employs distillation to train a global model. On the client side, D$^{2}$OFL improves the category-specific embedding generation process by filtering unrelated image encodings, making it more robust to outliers, and pushing the synthesized image distribution closer to that of the original images. Through extensive experiments across four benchmark datasets, we demonstrate that D$^{2}$OFL outperforms state-of-the-art DM-OSFL and traditional FL approaches, by up to 5% in feature shift and up to 2% in label shift non-IID setups. We also show that the choice of foundational model has little impact on D$^{2}$OFL performance.

papers.title: Performance Optimization for Multi-Cell Aerial Networks-Assisted MEC via Dual-Layer Blockchain-Enabled Federated Election
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: FedIGA: Improving Global Model Aggregation for Federated Self-Supervised Skeletal Action Recognition
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a distributed learning paradigm that collaboratively trains multiple client models to aggregate a generalized global model in server, without revealing data privacy. A key challenge to ideal global model aggregation is the problem of data heterogeneity. Despite many efforts to solve this problem in image data, there is still further exploration needed in skeletal data. Unlike image data, skeletal data is sparser, prompting the Skeleton Recognition Task (SRT) to prioritize fine-grained discrimination of part-body actions. In FL scenario, SRT demands a precise balance between commonalities and differences in local and global model parameters. In this paper, we propose a novel Federated Self-Supervised Skeletal Action Recognition framework (FedIGA). With the mission of mitigating data heterogeneity for improving global model aggregation, two key points are raised. Specifically, Projector-Specialty Regularization (PSR) is presented to indirectly elevate encoder training by deriving the intrinsic specialty of the projector, besides the direct regularization of the encoder. Furthermore, considering the main homogeneity and a few heterogeneity in the global model aggregation, SVD-Divergence Aggregation (SDA) is introduced to leverage the aggregation weight obtained by SVD-Param divergence to reduce the divergence between the client and global model for aggregating, based on the principle of seeking common ground while reserving differences. Extensive experiments show that FedIGA outperforms other baselines significantly on the public datasets.

papers.title: PIRD-PFL: Purifying Injection and Robust Distillation for Backdoor Defense in Personalized Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across decentralized devices without sharing private data. To address the performance degradation caused by statistical heterogeneity (non-IID data), Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) has emerged as a promising paradigm by tailoring models to individual clients. However, the decentralized and heterogeneous nature of PFL makes it highly vulnerable to backdoor attacks, where clients employ diverse architectures and the server cannot directly inspect or compare local model updates. Consequently, traditional defenses based on parameter aggregation or anomaly detection become ineffective. To tackle this challenge, we propose PIRD-PFL (Purifying Injection and Robust Distillation in PFL), a novel model that secures knowledge transfer in heterogeneous PFL without relying on parameter alignment or clean proxy data. The key idea is to purify malicious knowledge at both the sample and feature levels during the collaborative learning process. Specifically, PIRD-PFL consists of two synergistic phases. In the Injection Phase, we design a Channel Shuffling Vaccine (SV) mechanism that identifies and suppresses poisoned samples by exploiting their unstable responses under deep-layer channel perturbations. In the Distillation Phase, we develop a Robust Transmitter with Heterogeneous Attention Transfer (HAT) to enforce attention consistency on clean semantic regions, thereby preventing the propagation of malicious localized triggers. Extensive experiments on bench mark datasets demonstrate that PIRD-PFL effectively mitigates distributed backdoor attacks while maintaining high personalized accuracy, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art defenses in heterogeneous settings.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: ReMerkle: Proof-of-Reputation-Driven Federated Learning with Compact Merkle Verification for Consumer-Centric IoMT
papers.abstract: Consumer-centric Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices, including wearables and in-home health monitors, generate sensitive physiological and activity data for personalized health monitoring. Federated Learning (FL) helps preserve privacy by keeping raw data on local devices, but integrating blockchain-based accountability into FL can introduce prohibitive storage, latency, and gas overhead when model updates are recorded on-chain. This paper introduces ReMerkle, a lightweight blockchain-enabled FL framework for consumer IoMT. ReMerkle combines a three-tier reputation mechanism based on cosine similarity, Beta-history reputation, and entropy-based quality assessment to filter unreliable or low-quality updates before aggregation. To reduce blockchain overhead, ReMerkle stores only a 32-byte Merkle root on-chain through Compact Merkle Tree Verification rather than storing full model updates. Experiments on a WBAN human activity recognition dataset show that ReMerkle achieves 90.2% accuracy after 10 FL rounds, increases honest-node reputation scores from 0.5 to 0.85, and requires 20,180 gas per five-client round, reducing both gas consumption and on-chain storage by 99.96% relative to full-update storage. These results demonstrate a cost-efficient and auditable FL architecture for secure consumer health monitoring.

papers.title: FED-PsyAU: A Unified Framework for Micro-Expression Recognition With Psychological Topology Learning and Federated Privacy Preservation
papers.abstract: Micro-expressions (MEs) are spontaneous, subtle facial movements that reveal genuine emotions, making them indispensable for high-stakes applications like security and clinical diagnosis. However, Micro-Expression Recognition (MER) is currently hindered by a dual bottleneck: the intrinsic difficulty of extracting discriminative features from subtle motions and the extrinsic privacy constraints that restrict centralized training in real-world scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose FED-PsyAU, a unified framework that synergizes psychological insights with privacy-preserving computing. First, addressing the feature representation challenge, we propose a psychological study, which quantifies the coordination and incoordination between upper and lower facial Action Units (AUs). Leveraging these priors, we develop a Dynamic Prior Knowledge-based Graph Attention Network (DPK-GAT) combined with a novel Spatial Position-Aware Transformer (SPAT) and an Expression-Specific Attention (ESA) module. This architecture effectively integrates structural psychological constraints with data-driven statistical patterns to learn hierarchical facial motion features. Furthermore, to tackle data privacy and scarcity, we integrate this model into a Personalized Federated Learning (P-FedProx) framework, enabling collaborative training across distributed clients without raw data exchange. Extensive experiments on standard ME databases demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in both centralized and federated settings, validating the efficacy of incorporating psychological topology into privacy-preserving systems. Our implementation is publicly available athttps://github.com/MELABIPCAS/FED-PsyAU.git.

papers.title: Asymmetric Partial Model Transmission for Federated Edge Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) applications normally employ large deep learning (DL) models, resulting in excessive communication overhead in the deployment of FL over resource-constraint mobile edge networks. To achieve better scalability for DL-based FL, we capitalize on both the asymmetric nature of mobile networks and the distinct effects of partial transmissions on FL training for the global and local models. We proposeFed-DynAmal, an FL framework that decreases the number of parameters transmitted in the uplink (clients-to-server) while concurrently achieving better model performance. The underlying idea is that each selected client sends a partial DL model to the server by omitting several sub-blocks from the trained local model. Crucially, we drop the assumption that transmitted local models can still be used for inference, thereby allowing for greater model variability. At the server, we introduce amalgamation, a process to merge different partial local models into an inference-viable full model. Essentially, amalgamation is a bridge for performing aggregation at the sub-block level. Interestingly, as the key takeaway, communication efficiency versus model performance is not necessarily a trade-off in FL: Our extensive experiments show thatFed-DynAmalcan effectively improve communication efficiency while still concurrently achieving higher accuracy and enhanced robustness.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Feature Decoupling-Based Bilateral Adaptive Personalized Federated Graph Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning shows great promise in enabling collaborative machine learning among distributed devices while protecting data privacy. Graph Neural Networks have demonstrated their superiority in processing structured data such as molecules and social networks. Leveraging the advantages of federated learning, federated graph learning (FGL) enables clients to train powerful GNNs in a distributed manner without sharing their private data. However, the graph data on clients are usually non-IID, causing a single model to perform poorly across all clients. To address this issue, we propose a novel feature decoupling-based bilateral adaptive personalized FGL method (flBAP). Specifically, we decouple structure information from feature information to learn feature-based knowledge in a personalized manner and structure-based knowledge in a shared manner. On the model side, we introduce a bilateral adaptive algorithm executed iteratively through two operations: adaptive model aggregation on the server and adaptive model initialization on the client. To our knowledge, we are the first to integrate global and personalized information from both the data and model sides. We are also the first to adaptively adjust personalized models on both the server and client sides. Compared to existing methods, flBAP offers a more fine-grained and sample-specific approach to personalization. Additionally, flBAP protects privacy and reduces downlink communication costs by only sharing structure encoding parameters. Extensive experiments in non-IID settings across multiple datasets demonstrate that flBAP outperforms the state-of-the-art method GCFL+ by an average of 7.83%. Furthermore, flBAP maintains its advantage even when some clients unexpectedly drop out, a common occurrence in mobile environments.

papers.title: PPVFL-LWA: Privacy-Preserving and Verifiable Federated Learning with Lossless Weighted Aggregation
papers.abstract: Federated learning protects user privacy by sharing only local model parameters rather than raw data, but it is vulnerable to poisoning attacks. Existing defenses rely on plaintext gradient analysis, posing privacy leakage risks; while encryption, though secure, incurs high computational overhead, making detection unaffordable. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Privacy-Preserving and verifiable federated learning scheme with lossless weighted aggregation (PPVFL-LWA), which effectively resists poisoning attacks and supports user dropout while ensuring user privacy. The scheme protects local gradients with obfuscation factors to prevent collusion between the server and users for privacy inference; ensures data integrity and lossless aggregation of local models through a dual-collector mechanism and bilinear aggregation signatures; and introduces verification contracts to eliminate reliance on trusted third parties for verification. Furthermore, this paper designs a semi-trusted dynamic weight adjustment strategy based on gradient similarity and data distribution characteristics to mitigate the impact of poisoning attacks by adaptively adjusting participant weights. Experimental results show that PPVFL-LWA outperforms existing schemes in both training efficiency and attack resistance.

papers.title: Distributed Open-Set Human Activity Recognition for IoMT via Federated Data Stream Mining with Lightweight Auxiliary Novelty Detection on Wi-Fi CSI Edge Devices
papers.abstract: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) in Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) environments is critical for monitoring patient behaviors in hospitals, rehabilitation centers, and eldercare facilities. Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) sensing has emerged as a non-intrusive and infrastructure-friendly alternative to camera-based systems for continuous activity monitoring. While data stream mining algorithms offer the adaptability required for real-time HAR, they remain constrained by a closed-world assumption, where the set of activity classes is fixed in advance. This poses a significant limitation in medical scenarios where patient behaviors naturally evolve from coarse to refined states — for example, a fall incident involves sequential transitions from standing to falling to lying down, potentially forming new, unforeseen activity patterns. Existing concept drift detectors are designed to handle changes in data distribution within known classes but lack the capacity to identify emergent, unseen classes in data streams. To address this gap, we propose LAND (Lightweight Auxiliary Novelty Detection), a distributed federated learning framework integrating auxiliary lightweight novelty detection modules alongside incremental data stream classifiers on Wi-Fi CSI edge devices. LAND enables on-device detection of novel activity patterns, triggers distributed similarity checking across federated nodes, and supports adaptive label evolution without compromising computational efficiency. Experimental evaluations in realistic, hospital‑like simulated environments demonstrate the feasibility and strong prototype‑level performance of LAND in mitigating accuracy degradation during emergent activity episodes, outperforming conventional stream learners in both responsiveness and adaptability. This work advances the development of open-set, lightweight, and adaptive HAR frameworks for sensitive IoMT deployments. The results establish LAND as a robust proof‑of‑concept system, forming a foundation for future clinical deployment studies.

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Point Cloud Analysis via Kronecker Product Factorization
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a vital paradigm for privacy-preserving 3D perception. However, the substantial communication overhead remains a critical bottleneck, hindering FL deployment on resource-constrained devices. In this work, we propose FedKP, a communication-efficient FL framework based on Kronecker Product (KP) factorization for point cloud analysis. By pre-decomposing model parameters into Kronecker factors, FedKP mitigates the communication burden during both uploads and downloads. To further enhance scalability, we extend KP factorization to Sum-of-Kronecker-Products (SKP) factorization, giving rise to FedSKP. Our analysis reveals that FedSKP implicitly achieves multi-branch feature aggregation, enabling the model to capture more diverse local geometric features. Consequently, FedSKP maintains competitive performance while substantially minimizing communication cost. Furthermore, we develop a reconstruction-free computation acceleration strategy to enhance the viability on edge devices. Extensive experiments are conducted on the ModelNet40, ShapeNetPart, and S3DIS datasets. Experimental results show that these frameworks exhibit competitive communication efficiency and model performance compared to relevant baselines.

papers.title: Self-Enhanced Hashing With Semantic Interaction for Federated Cross-Modal Retrieval
papers.abstract: Federated cross-modal retrieval addresses the significant challenges of distributed training on multi-modal data across decentralized data silos. However, current limitations in the mutual utilization of semantic information between modalities often restrict retrieval performance. To tackle this problem, we propose a federated cross-modal retrieval method based on self-enhanced hashing with semantic information interaction (FedSEH-SII). FedSEH-SII leverages logits information derived from various classification tasks to enhance hash encoding through a modality-shared semantic and hash code information conversion module (SHCModule). The SHCModule facilitates the conversion of semantic representations into a public hash-related space via modal interaction. To ensure the quality of both the SHCModule and the other modality-specific parameters, we incorporate hash conversion divergence and modality-wise discriminative loss into the parameter aggregation process. Extensive experiments conducted on five widely used cross-modal retrieval benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed FedSEH-SII, which achieves superior cross-modal retrieval performance compared to exiting federated learning methods.

papers.title: Enhancing Backdoor Attacks in Heterogeneous Federated Learning with Adaptive Model Pruning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving collaborative training across distributed clients without sharing raw data. In practical cross-device deployments, clients exhibit substantial heterogeneity in computation and communication budgets, and consequently model pruning is often adopted to induce sparsity and reduce local training and uplink overhead. Although pruning is introduced for efficiency, it can also change the attack surface by altering model capacity and optimization dynamics. However, these effects do not reliably mitigate back door threats under heterogeneous pruning. Moreover, attackers can exploit sparsity patterns to camouflage malicious updates, thereby increasing the stealthiness of backdoor attacks. To demonstrate this residual vulnerability, we develop a pruning augmented backdoor attack framework. It applies Channel-wise Activation Discrepancy Analysis (CADA) to identify backdoor relevant channels by measuring activation discrepancies between poisoned and benign samples, and employs Continuous Mask Optimization (CMO) to optimize pruning masks through continuous relaxation, thereby preserving backdoor-critical parameters while mimicking benign client sparsity patterns. Extensive experiments under representative defenses demonstrate that the proposed method consistently improves attack success rate (ASR) while maintaining comparable clean accuracy.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Decentralized Federated Learning for Heterogeneous Multi-Task Semantic Communication
papers.abstract: Collaborative training in distributed semantic communication (DSC) networks typically relies on decentralized federated learning (DFL). However, pushing topology-agnostic aggregation into heterogeneous, multi-task environments creates a fundamental bottleneck: it drives negative transfer and overconsensus bias (OCB). This paper introduces a personalized DSC framework that cuts off this cross-task interference. At the node level, a policy-driven multi-path routing mechanism separates task-specific features from shared representations to preserve local fidelity. Across the network, we deploy a "communicationwhile- aggregation" protocol. It calibrates a column-stochastic consensus matrix using task affinities. This limits the system to absorbing complementary knowledge while actively blocking mismatched parameter updates. To bound the convergence, we derive a unified Lyapunov drift analysis. We reveal a strict Ushaped trade-off: deeper topological mixing reduces variance but amplifies structural OCB. Resolving this tension yields a closed-form expression for the optimal aggregation depth. We evaluate the proposed framework on NYU-v2, where the results reveal a clear trade-off between insufficient aggregation and excessive topological mixing. At the analytically derived optimal aggregation depth, our method achieves a 4.77% global relative improvement over the no-aggregation baseline and outperforms decentralized FedAvg, FedAMP, and heuristic max aggregation. We further evaluate the framework on Taskonomy and imperfect wireless links to examine the effects of network-size variation and wireless-link reliability.

papers.title: Maximizing Accuracy-Per-Cost in Vehicular Federated Learning via Active Inference and Two-Stage Resource Optimization
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), helping vehicles overcome data and computational limitations while preserving privacy. However, its performance is constrained by both data heterogeneity and system heterogeneity. Additionally, different FL tasks exhibit diverse preferences regarding energy consumption and end-to-end latency. To address the diverse latency and energy preferences in IoV and improve model accuracy and convergence, this paper proposes a unified framework to optimize accuracy per unit of utility in vehicular FL. Utility is modeled as a weighted sum of energy consumption and latency. We analyze key factors influencing FL model accuracy in IoV environments and establish a joint optimization problem that balances accuracy with utility cost. To match the information asymmetry between the server and clients and reduce computational complexity, we decompose the problem into two coordinated stages: server-side client selection and bandwidth allocation, and client-side computation and transmission power control. On the server side, we model decision-making as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP), and develop an active-inference-based actor–critic method for adaptive client selection and resource management. On the client side, we derive closed-form optimal solutions for resource allocation under heterogeneous latency and energy preferences. By combining learning-based global coordination with lightweight analytical local control, the proposed provides a practical and scalable tradeoff between adaptability, efficiency, and implementation complexity. Extensive simulations validate the effectiveness and superiority of our algorithm.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Energy-Aware Quantum Optimization for Semi-Decentralized Federated Learning in Satellite–Terrestrial Vehicular Networks
papers.abstract: Low earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations with on-board processing capabilities are emerging as an edge-computing platform for satellite–terrestrial vehicular networks (STVNs), enabling global service provisioning to vehicles. Federated learning (FL) is naturally suited to such distributed architectures, enabling privacy-preserving model training across satellites without sharing raw data. However, deploying FL over LEO satellite-enabled STVNs remains challenging due to high communication latency, imbalanced energy consumption among satellites and the computational intractability of optimizations. To address these issues, we propose a novel semi-decentralized FL framework tailored to LEO satellite constellations. Satellites in the same orbital plane are organized into a bi-directional ring that performs intra-plane aggregation, alleviates bottlenecks at a single server and explicitly exploits orbital geometry to accelerate convergence. A recursive latency formulation and a closed-form expression for satellite energy consumption are derived that capture practical link occupancy during inter-satellite links (ISLs). Specifically, energy consumption balancing across related satellites is formulated as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem in the proposed FL, which is solved using the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) with an Ising-form cost Hamiltonian. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces FL round latency and improves energy balancing across aggregation nodes, while maintaining learning performance compared with baseline schemes.

papers.title: PF-DRL: A Personalized Federated Learning Approach for Multi-UAV Trajectory Optimization in Internet of Vehicles
papers.abstract: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) is evolving rapidly, yet providing ubiquitous connectivity and computing services for vehicles in complex urban environments remains challenging due to the sparse deployment and coverage blind spots of terrestrial Roadside Units (RSUs). Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have emerged as flexibleAerial RSUs (ARSUs)to support Vehicular Edge Computing (VEC). However, realizing autonomous trajectory optimization for UAV-assisted IoV faces significant hurdles: the highly dynamic topology of vehicular traffic leads to data scarcity, while the inherent data heterogeneity (non-IID) among UAVs covering different road segments degrades the performance of traditional global models. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Personalized Federated Deep Reinforcement Learning (PF-DRL) framework. Unlike conventional Federated Learning (FL) that enforces a one-size-fits-all model, PF-DRL employs an adaptive convex interpolation mechanism to balance global traffic knowledge sharing with local environmental adaptation. Furthermore, considering the stringent communication and energy constraints of UAVs in vehicular networks, we propose alightweightvariant that selectively aggregates only Critic networks while keeping Actor updates local, thereby reducing communication overhead by approximately 50%. We also derive a theoretical upper bound for the personalization loss to motivate an adaptive weight adjustment strategy. Extensive simulations in realistic 3D urban vehicular scenarios demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines (including FedProx, Ditto, and pFedMe) in terms of convergence speed, system throughput and communication efficiency. Finally, we discuss practical deployment issues, including onboard computation and edge-cloud scalability, paving the way for trustworthy and scalable UAV-assisted IoV management.

papers.title: Latency-Aware Downlink Mutual Information Maximization for RIS-Assisted Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) has emerged as an important framework for distributed edge intelligence over wireless networks, where the wall-clock training efficiency is strongly affected by the communication latency for global model dissemination and aggregation. In reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted wireless systems, improving the downlink transmission quality can support more timely model delivery and, consequently, faster FL progress under a fixed training-time budget. In this paper, we study a multi-user RIS-assisted FL downlink and develop an FL-oriented communication model that relates the global-model dissemination latency to the achievable mutual information (MI). To account for the bottleneck nature of FL downlink transmission, we clarify the relationship between sum-MI maximization and worst-user latency through a rate-dispersion factor, under which sum MI serves as a tractable communication-side surrogate for improving wall-clock FL efficiency. Based on this model, we formulate a joint active and passive beamforming problem under the base station transmit-power constraint and the RIS unit-modulus constraint. To handle the resulting non-convex coupling, we develop an efficient alternating optimization (AO) framework that combines weighted minimum mean-square error based active beamforming and block coordinate descent based passive beamforming, with monotonic objective improvement under the available channel state information (CSI). The impact of imperfect CSI is also discussed to reflect practical RIS-assisted deployment. Simulation results show that the proposed design achieves noticeable MI gains over representative communication-learning benchmarks, which are empirically associated with reduced downlink dissemination latency, improved communication–computation efficiency, and faster FL progress on standard image classification tasks.

papers.title: Unsupervised Federated Learning on Non-IID Graphs via Contrastive Encoding and Cluster Centroid Sampling
papers.abstract: Federated graph learning (FGL) has attracted significant attention for enabling privacy-preserving collaborative model training based on multiple participants’ local graphs. However, a node’s neighbors in one participant’s local graph may be distributed across the local graphs of other participants, resulting in topological nonindependence and creating a specific non-independently and identically distributed (non-IID) problem. Existing unsupervised federated learning approaches under topological nonindependence encounter two problems: 1) the lack of encoding the distances between nodes across different participants’ local graphs reduces the models’ accuracy; and 2) the volume of data transmitted escalates with the increase in inter-edges or nodes, leading to great communication overhead. To tackle these problems, we propose a federated graph learning model based on contrastive encoding and cluster centroid sampling (FCECS), a novel unsupervised FGL model. First, we design a local contrastive strategy based on alignment masking and a global contrastive strategy based on cluster centroid sampling and integrate them to encode node distances both within and across participants’ local graphs, thereby improving the model’s accuracy. Second, the global contrastive strategy based on cluster centroid sampling guarantees a consistent volume of data transmission, thereby reducing communication overhead caused by an increasing number of inter-edges or nodes. Experimental results on real-world datasets demonstrate that FCECS achieves an average accuracy improvement of 57% compared to existing FGL models.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems

papers.title: LungSage: A World-Model-Driven Clinical Decision Engine Fusing TCM Syndrome Patterns with PET-CT Imaging for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Prognosis
papers.abstract: LungSage has concordance index score of 0.77 on NSCLC-Radiomics (up from DeepSurv by 0.02), strong accuracy 76.5% for PGD-based attacks with only 1.2% clean accuracy lost. With ε=8 Differential Privacy tested across six independent public datasets comprising more than 12,000 test cases and obtaining 78 ms of inference from current consumer hardware running ARM TrustZone, accuracy remains within ±1.5% of un-privatized scores. All assessments were conducted using a common recurrent state-space architecture. Adversaries attack diagnostic accuracy of consumer health services that use imaging to diagnose tumors from less than 13% without applying security measure, and federated learning must find an effective mechanism to provide safeguards while delivering the level of quality typically found in clinical-use systems. Establishing modes of world model to assist with creating clinical judgments regarding the integration of clinical syndromes (i.e., TCM) with imaging data will support patient outcome. LungSage will deliver a world model-based framework to enable the integration of multimodal fusion (i.e., PET-CT images, electronic health records, and TCM syndromes), sequential treatment reasoning, and an infrastructure for privacy and security provided by latent-space differential privacy, trusted execution environment, and adversarial training inference. We anticipate that the latent-space world models developed to date will provide the basis for proactive threat mitigation and create resilient security for next-generation consumer electronics environments.

papers.title: Trustworthy Agentic Federated Learning for Multi-Level Data Imbalance in Intelligent Edge Networks
papers.abstract: Intelligent edge networks are increasingly powered by collaborative agentic AI systems, where edge devices operate as autonomous agents. However, non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) edge data introduces severe statistical heterogeneity, causing local models to deviate from the global consensus and undermining the trustworthiness of agent updates. In this work, we systematically study this problem under three representative multi-level data imbalance scenarios:i)local imbalance and global balance,ii)local balance and global imbalance, andiii)dual-imbalance. Under such conditions, agents often overfit their skewed local data while forgetting previously learned global knowledge, leading to unstable collaboration. To address this challenge, we proposeTrustworthyAgenticFederatedLearning (TAFL), a dual-constraint framework that balances autonomous local adaptation with trustworthy global learning. The framework employs a two-stage optimization strategy: a prototype-based semantic alignment stage that establishes a shared feature space with minimal communication overhead, followed by a trustworthy consolidation stage that anchors globally important parameters to prevent the forgetting of global knowledge. Extensive experiments demonstrate thatTAFLconsistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving higher accuracy, faster convergence, and more stable collaboration under the three imbalance scenarios.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for State-of-Health Prediction of Lithium-Ion Batteries With Randomized Quantization-Enabled Data Augmentation
papers.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are extensively used in electric vehicles as efficient energy storage systems, making accurate prediction of their state of health (SOH) crucial. In practice, accurate SOH prediction requires large amounts of battery data for model training. However, individual battery users often lack sufficient data, and centralized learning with multiple users raise data privacy concerns, limiting leverage of distributed data resources. As an emerging technology, federated learning enables multiple clients to collaboratively train models while preserving data privacy. However, insufficient local data at each client still pose significant challenges for collaborative SOH prediction modeling. To address these challenges, we propose a novel collaborative battery SOH prediction modeling framework with randomized quantization-enabled data augmentation.
