The framework first proposes randomized quantization as a data augmentation strategy to expand each user’s local data and improve the accuracy of local models. Subsequently, federated learning is proposed with the Swin Transformer, serving as both the local and global model to enable privacy-preserving collaborative training. The proposed method is evaluated on three battery aging datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving high prediction accuracy while protecting data privacy. This framework provides a new perspective for advancing SOH prediction of lithium-ion batteries with multiple users.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement

papers.title: FedCataract-Sentinel: Privacy-Preserving World-Model-Orchestrated Framework for Automatic Cataract Recognition and Adversarial Anomaly Threat Hunting in Inclusive Connected Health Systems for Elderly Women
papers.abstract: Cataract remains the leading cause of global blindness, affecting approximately 17 million individuals, and this burden falls disproportionately on elderly women—who bear the majority of cataract-related vision impairment worldwide and face the highest per-capita incidence after menopause—yet all existing automated cataract recognition systems assume centralized data access, a fundamental barrier to privacy-preserving deployment on connected health devices where raw fundus images cannot leave local storage under HIPAA and GDPR regulations. We introduce FedCataract-Sentinel, a framework that integrates federated learning for privacy-preserving cataract recognition with a world-model-orchestrated anomaly detection mechanism for proactive adversarial threat hunting in inclusive connected health systems (ICHS) designed to serve elderly women and other under-represented populations in FemTech. The core innovation applies Recurrent State-Space Models (RSSM) to learn the temporal dynamics of federated model updates, enabling prediction-error-based anomaly scoring that detects Byzantine poisoning, backdoor injection, and adaptive attacks that evade static perround defenses such as Krum and FLAME. Evaluation across two public ophthalmic datasets and the FLPoison benchmark demonstrates that FedCataract-Sentinel achieves 0.961 cataract detection AUC under non-IID federated settings, within 1.6 pp of centralized training, while improving Byzantine attack detection accuracy by 7.69 pp over the strongest baseline defense. The advantage concentrates on temporally structured attacks, with a 12.73 pp improvement on Edge-case attacks that evade static perround filtering. The framework maintains real-time inference on edge devices under 8W power, establishing an end-to-end privacy-preserving, adversarially robust cataract recognition pipeline. While we frame the work around inclusive connected health for elderly women, the security mechanism is general and is evaluated on cataract data rather than any FemTech-specific device or cohort.

papers.title: Adaptive Federated Learning with Cross-Dimensional Information Fusion for Privacy-Preserving Generative AI
papers.abstract: With the popularization of consumer devices, collaborative training based on multi-dimensional data fusion in distributed frameworks has shown great potential for improving model performance. However, data heterogeneity and the risk of privacy leakage have become major challenges that limit the effectiveness of collaborative training. Federated learning has emerged as a distributed training paradigm that integrates multi-dimensional data information with privacy protection. Nevertheless, traditional federated learning methods usually adopt a single privacy-preserving mechanism, which is not only difficult to adapt to the non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) characteristics of multi-dimensional data in distributed scenarios, but also prone to privacy leakage during parameter transmission. To address the aforementioned problems, this paper proposes a framework called FedGAN-DP, which integrates multi-dimensional data preprocessing and hierarchical privacy protection. The mechanism consists of two core components: (1) A multi-dimensional data fusion and privacy enhancement mechanism is designed as follows. First, Dynamic data dimension selection is employed to quantify the value of each dimension. Then, the Gramian Angular Field (GAF) combined with Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) is utilized to convert the selected multi-dimensional data into standardized images. Finally, Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) performs feature enhancement and privacy desensitization on the generated images. (2) A mechanism integrates a hierarchical adaptive clipping strategy with a channel-aware noise injection strategy to achieve fine-grained adaptive gradient clipping and differentiated noise injection. Experimental results show that under the dual privacy protection mechanism, the proposed algorithm improves the F1-score by at least 2.18% and 11.28% on UCI-HAR and KU-HAR datasets, respectively, compared with the benchmark without privacy protection, which verifies its favorable trade-off between privacy security and model performance, providing a privacy-preserving federated learning and generative AI solution for consumer electronics.

papers.title: Federated Multi-Center Deep Support Vector Data Description With Lyapunov Convergence Guarantees for Anomaly Detection in IIoT Networks
papers.abstract: Multi-site Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) anomaly detection demands cross-site collaboration without sharing raw data. Federated learning enables such collaboration, yet existing methods overlook challenges unique to one-class detectors. We identify a structural conflict that, to our knowledge, has not been characterized in this depth by prior federated anomaly-detection work. When multi-center Deep Support Vector Data Description (Deep SVDD) detectors undergo standard federated aggregation, each site’s hypersphere decision boundary inflates systematically, and the severity escalates with data heterogeneity. The root cause is a structural conflict between SVDD’s geometric objective and federated parameter averaging. We propose Federated Multi-Center Deep SVDD (FMC-SVDD), which employs radius-aware selective aggregation to share encoder representations while preserving per-site hypersphere compactness. Using Lyapunov stability theory, we prove that per-site SVDD loss converges monotonically to a bounded region. To our knowledge, such guarantees have not yet been established for federated anomaly detection. To handle unknown inter-site distribution shift, we incorporate Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization into the aggregation weight design, ensuring that these guarantees remain valid under distributional uncertainty. Experiments on the SWaT and WADI benchmarks confirm that FMC-SVDD suppresses boundary inflation while unlocking federated gains, outperforming existing baselines in detection accuracy and boundary compactness.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: D 3 em: A Dual-Layer Dynamic Debiasing Evaluation Mechanism for Client Contribution in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Accurate client contribution evaluation is critical for sustainable federated learning and incentive design, yet existing methods face a trade-off between trust, complexity, and robustness. We show that validation-free, similarity-based metrics can suffer from a federated noise coupling effect, where historical low-quality updates become entangled with the global trajectory, causing evaluation noise to accumulate and manifest as systematic bias across rounds. We proposeD3em, a dual-layer dynamic debiasing mechanism built on a parallel local–federated dual-model training framework.D3emextracts a noise-decoupled independent value from the local branch and a collaborative value from the federated branch, and fuses them via a phase-aware weighting schedule to stabilize contribution scores throughout training. Experiments on CIFAR-10, Fashion-MNIST, and SST-5 under diverse heterogeneous partitions show thatD3emimproves global accuracy by 6.15 percentage points on average over representative baselines, and achieves an average fairness of 97.08% when coupled with incentive schemes. Meanwhile,D3emachieves comparable or even better end-to-end overhead in terms of total communication and total latency. The code is available athttps://anonymous.4open.science/r/D_3AM-8A70
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Analyzing Backdoor Vulnerabilities in Interpretable Machine Learning for Wireless Jamming Detection Using Tsetlin Machines
papers.abstract: Interpretable machine learning is increasingly sought in next-generation cellular networks, where trust, accountability, and robustness are essential and jamming remains a persistent threat. Federated learning enables collaborative jamming detection without sharing raw in-phase and quadrature data, while Tsetlin Machines provide a logic-based option for transparent, resource-constrained deployments. However, the security implications of interpretability in federated wireless environments remain poorly understood. We introduce a backdoor threat model for interpretable federated jamming detectors, showing how Tsetlin Machine clause structure can be exploited by a compromised client to induce targeted detection failures. In a federated framework with weighted Coalesced Tsetlin Machines and Krum aggregation, we analyze clause-based vulnerability to spectrogram-domain trigger perturbations and formulate a multi-objective problem balancing trigger effectiveness, model deviation, and aggregation selection. We further show that clause-informed trigger initialization lowers adversarial optimization effort, revealing a tension between transparency and robustness. Evaluation on 60,000 spectrograms from a 5G NR synchronization-signal testbed shows that optimized triggers can exceed 70% trial-level triggered false-negative rates in optimizer benchmarks, reaching approximately 90% in best-case configurations; supplemental multi-round federated evaluation shows that trial-level and global triggered false-negative rate (TFR) can diverge substantially (gaps from -31.4 to +3.0 percentage points across evaluated partitions), with no sustained global TFR$\geq$70% after the last malicious selection round. These results highlight the need for defense-aware design of explainable models in next-generation networks.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Differential Privacy in Vertical Federated Learning With Perturbed Gradients Obtained via Functional Mechanism
papers.abstract: Vertical federated learning enables multiple institutions to collaboratively train models without sharing raw features, thereby addressing data-silo challenges while satisfying privacy-compliance requirements. Existing differentially private vertical federated learning methods typically inject noise directly into exchanged gradients and embeddings, but under strong privacy constraints they suffer from degraded model accuracy, unstable convergence, and excessive communication overhead. To address these issues, this paper proposes FMVFed, a differentially private vertical federated learning framework based on the functional mechanism, which effectively balances privacy protection, model utility, and communication efficiency. FMVFed achieves differential privacy by injecting Gaussian noise into the coefficient space of the training objective, thereby avoiding the utility loss caused by directly perturbing high-dimensional vectors. Meanwhile, it introduces an adaptive random Top-$k$Sparsification communication strategy to significantly reduce cross-party communication overhead. Experimental results show that even under a small privacy budget (e.g.,$\varepsilon =1$), FMVFed outperforms methods that directly perturb algorithm outputs by 13.47%, 3.13%, and 2.43% on CIFAR-10, FashionMNIST, and MNIST, respectively.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Federated Learning-Empowered Jamming Detection for Stochastic Uplink and Downlink Integrated Terrestrial and Non-Terrestrial Networks
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a novel approach that integrates the reliability and fast data transfer capabilities of terrestrial-based infrastructure with the extensive coverage of non-terrestrial networks, thereby creating a seamless and resilient communication network. The proposed integration addresses the issue of adaptive jamming in uplink (UL) and downlink (DL) transmissions, which threatens communication efficiency and reliability. To this end, we first introduce a 3D simulation design that accurately models UL and DL transmissions within stochastic integrated terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks (SI-TNTNs), incorporating adaptive jamming strategies and employing a stochastic node distribution based on the Homogeneous Poisson Point Process (HPPP). Next, in order to train encoder networks deployed on clients for both UL and DL transmissions, we propose a distributed learning framework called the federated partial model aggregation (FedPMA) algorithm that uses the spectral correlation function (SCF) for feature representation. The proposed approach combines encoder parameter aggregation with a multivariate normal (MVN)-based probabilistic reliability estimation derived locally from encoder outputs, which guides the aggregation process. Only encoder parameters and scalar reliability scores are exchanged between clients and the parameter server (PS), while raw data and latent representations remain local. Our experimental results reveal that our approach not only enhances data privacy, but also significantly improves model performance and convergence, thus paving the way for the development of robust, interference-sensitive communications strategies suitable for next-generation non-terrestrial network (NTN)-enabled wireless systems.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: PhysioDrift-Fed: Confronting the Drift-Rate Heterogeneity Problem in Federated Learning for Consumer Cardiac Wearables
papers.abstract: Consumer cardiac wearables increasingly rely on federated learning (FL) to deliver personalized AI without compromising user privacy, yet deployed models silently degrade as user physiology evolves with age, medications, and lifestyle. We identify and formalize this challenge as the Drift-Rate Heterogeneity Problem (DRHP)- users drift at fundamentally different rates, and existing federated frameworks neither detect drift through physiological signals nor distribute its consequences fairly across the user population. This paper introduces PhysioDrift-Fed, the first dedicated FL framework for driftrate heterogeneity, combining three coordinated components: a physiology-aware drift detector that fuses statistical and electrocardiogram-domain signals, a Drift-Rate Fair Aggregation (DRFA) scheme that equalizes representation across heterogeneous drift strata, and an energy-budgeted selective update protocol respecting wearable resource limits. To support reproducible study of this problem, we release DriftBench-ECG, a public driftevaluation benchmark on the PTB-XL dataset. PhysioDrift-Fed delivers higher classification accuracy under drift, lower detection delay, substantially reduced fairness variance, and lower perround energy than five state-of-the-art baselines on real wearable-class hardware.

papers.title: Data Poisoning Detection for Secure Federated Learning With Dropout-Resilient Aggregation
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables multiple clients to train a global model collaboratively without sharing their raw data. However, compromised clients can launch data poisoning attacks by submitting malicious local updates and thereby degrade model accuracy. In addition, unprotected model updates may disclose sensitive information. Moreover, excluding malicious clients reduces the number of available shares and can prevent a conventional secure aggregation protocol from completing. To address these challenges, we propose DPDR, a secure FL framework that combines privacy-preserving, kernel density estimation (KDE)-based poisoning detection with dropout-resilient secure aggregation. DPDR subjects masked local updates to secure$k$-nearest-neighbor ($k$-NN) computation, KDE-based local-density estimation, maliciousness-score computation, and poisoned-update classification. It then excludes poisoned updates and uses Shamir secret reconstruction to aggregate the retained benign updates before broadcasting the resulting global model. Experiments on three benchmark datasets show that DPDR defends against data poisoning, protects model-update privacy, and tolerates client dropout while maintaining competitive global-model performance.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Efficient Federated Learning With Adaptive Model Pruning and Quantization Over Wireless Networks
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables multiple devices to collaboratively train a global model without sharing local data. However, due to limited local computing capability and communication bandwidth, FL suffers from high learning latency, especially when the model size is large. To address these issues, we propose APQ-FL, an adaptive model pruning and quantization method for wireless FL, to reduce the neural network size and improve communication efficiency. Moreover, device selection and wireless resource allocation are also integrated. We first present a convergence analysis of FL with model pruning and quantized transmission, and then jointly optimize the pruning ratio, quantization bit width, device selection, and wireless bandwidth allocation to minimize the convergence upper bound under latency and bandwidth constraints. We prove that the optimized quantization bit width can be obtained via binary search, and derive the closed-form solutions for the optimal pruning ratio and bandwidth allocation. Subsequently, we propose an efficient device selection strategy and further introduce its fairness-aware extension, APQ-FL-Fair. Experiments show that APQ-FL and APQ-FL-Fair improve test accuracy by 4.96%–15.33% while reducing 23.14%–74.45% communication overhead compared to other methods, and exhibit stable and superior performance even under stringent latency constraints.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: FedTVG: Personalized Federated Temporal Video Grounding over Heterogeneous Data
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel Temporal Video Grounding (TVG) setting called Personalized Federated TVG (FedTVG), addressing the current lack of consideration for client heterogeneity in real-world federated TVG research. FedTVG requires learning robust personalized models from clients with significant distributional discrepancies, which then collaboratively optimize a universal model on a central server capable of generalizing well across both seen and unseen clients. We establish personalized federated versions of the standard ActivityNet and Charades-STA datasets, namely ActivityNet-PF and Charades-STA-PF, to serve as datasets for FedTVG. Through careful inspection, we identify the primary challenge in FedTVG: models tend to develop cognitive shortcuts—biased reasoning patterns where they rely on non-essential contextual cues rather than event-specific information due to data distribution shifts among clients. To mitigate this, we propose Context-aware Countfactual Knowledge Transfer(CCKT), which eliminates cognitive shortcuts through causal intervention. Specifically, CCKT first employs Cross-Modal Context Disentanglement to decouple core semantics from contextual noise in the data. It then applies Causal Invariance Constraints to enforce the learning of correct causal relationships while filtering out client-specific spurious correlations. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that CCKT consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in FedTVG, achieving superior performance in both personalized ability of clients and generalizability of server.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology

papers.title: Toward Sustainable Federated Learning: A Learning Incentive Framework Balancing Energy Limits and Fairness
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has gained significant attention for its ability to collaboratively train machine learning models across distributed clients. However, traditional FL approaches often overlook the issues of both participation willingness of clients and their early dropouts due to energy depletions over a long-term training. This will result in insufficient training data in FL, and further weaken model generalizations. In this paper, by considering both energy limits and fairness selection of clients, we propose an iterative Auction and Reinforcement Learning (RL) enabled sustainable FL, i.e., SFARL, in which a sustainable RL, i.e., FSRL, is designed to satisfy clients' energy limits by determining the optimal local training iterations. To promote fairness among clients, a client selection algorithm and a two-part payment rule are further designed. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that SFARL upholds incentive compatibility, individual rationality, and fairness. Experimental results show that SFARL consistently achieves top-tier accuracy on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, while preserving the largest number of surviving clients and the lowest fairness metric among the compared methods. In addition, SFARL exhibits the best energy utilization efficiency and the one-time reporting mechanism significantly reduces the overall system consumption.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: FLCarbon: A Close Look Into the Operational Carbon and Embodied Carbon of Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning has gained prominence as a privacy-preserving distributed learning paradigm, yet its environmental impact, particularly its carbon footprint, remains inadequately quantified and understood. Existing carbon accounting methods for federated learning predominantly focus on operational emissions from electricity consumption, employing oversimplified and deterministic models that neglect embodied carbon from hardware manufacturing and inherent spatiotemporal uncertainties in carbon intensity. To address these limitations, this paper introduces FLCarbon, a probabilistic carbon accounting model that holistically estimates the carbon footprint of federated learning systems by integrating both operational and embodied carbon components while explicitly modeling their uncertainties. We develop parameterized models for embodied carbon of key hardware components, System-on-Chip (SoC), memory, and storage, incorporating factors such as manufacturing yield, energy efficiency, and geographic variability. For operational carbon, we model computing and communication processes under spatially and temporally varying grid carbon intensities and network conditions. To capture parameter distributions, we construct a comprehensive dataset from diverse sources, including ESG reports, industry publications, and real-world electricity data, and apply dual-stage distribution modeling via histograms and Kernel Density Estimation (KDE). Experimental evaluations across multiple datasets (CIFAR-10, ImageNet, FEMNIST, Speech Commands, Common Voice) and federation strategies (FedAvg, FedAdam) demonstrate that FLCarbon provides distribution-aware carbon estimates, revealing significant deviations from state-of-the-art deterministic models (e.g., up to 339% higher in federated settings). These results underscore the critical importance of embodied carbon and uncertainty-aware modeling in accurately assessing federated learning's environmental impact. Our work not only advances carbon accounting for FL but also provides a foundational framework for developing truly carbon-efficient federated learning systems.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Consumer-Centric Digital Twins for Healthcare 5.0 via Personalized Federated Learning with Asynchronous Mobile Updates
papers.abstract: Consumer-Centric Digital Twins (CCDT) require privacy-preserving and personalized intelligence on resource-constrained consumer devices such as smartphones and wearables. To support this setting, we propose Scalable Federated Personalized Aggregation with Posterior Approximation (SFed-PAPA), a scalable personalized federated learning framework that serves as the twin assimilation layer. SFedPAPA models client uncertainty with a Gaussian posterior approximation based on Taylor expansion, empirical Fisher, and KFAC, performs posterior-guided adaptive cohort selection, and generates client-specific weighted aggregates under asynchronous updates. We evaluate SFedPAPA on four healthcare-sensing benchmarks spanning classification and regression, and further analyze asynchronous updates, dynamic client participation, hyperparameter sensitivity, computational overhead, and differential privacy. SFedPAPA achieves 95.73% accuracy on HAR, 79.37% accuracy on WESAD, 2.18 MAE on PT, and 6.93 MAE on PPG-DaLiA, indicating its potential for scalable personalization in consumer-oriented digital twins for Healthcare 5.0.

papers.title: IGPA: Indirect Gradient Poisoning Attack on Federated Graph Learning in Decentralized Multimedia Networks
papers.abstract: Federated Graph Learning (FGL) enables collaborative training of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) across distributed multimedia platforms without sharing raw data. While existing research primarily focuses on privacy leakage, we reveal a more direct and structurally embedded threat: the Indirect Gradient Poisoning Attack (IGPA), which targets the data-generation layer in auxiliary-information-sharing FGL systems. We demonstrate that frameworks designed to reconstruct missing inter-platform connections, such as those used in cross-organizational social media analysis, create a novel and potent attack surface. By manipulating shared gradients during the collaborative training of node generators, a malicious client can stealthily inject corrupted nodes into the local subgraphs of benign clients. These poisoned nodes propagate distorted signals, leading to persistent degradation of the global model. We formalize this gray-box threat model and propose an optimization-based attack that maintains high stealth. Extensive experiments demonstrate that IGPA significantly degrades model performance while evading standard server-side defenses. Our findings highlight a critical vulnerability in FGL systems and underscore the urgent need for robust security mechanisms in collaborative multimedia learning systems that rely on shared data-generation components.

papers.title: Gradient-Driven Collaborative Multi-Stage Compression for Communication-Efficient Federated Learning in IoMT
papers.abstract: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) interconnects medical-grade devices, wearable sensors, and healthcare terminals to enable distributed intelligent diagnosis and remote monitoring. However, the wide heterogeneity of IoMT devices, unstable network conditions, and privacy-sensitive clinical data make traditional Federated Learning frameworks prone to inefficiency and instability. This paper proposes the Federated Efficient Gradient-aware Coordination via Multi-stage Compression in FL (FEGCM-FL), designed for efficient and reliable federated learning in IoMT. The framework employs a gradient-driven two-stage compression strategy that explicitly integrates Hierarchical Momentum-based Sensitivity Pruning (HMSP) with Gradient-aware Low-rank Decomposition (GLoR). HMSP leverages a sliding momentum mechanism to capture multi-round gradient information for dynamic hierarchical sparsification. GLoR adaptively allocates rank resources based on gradient sensitivity and introduces a tunable rank scaling factor to realize a pruning-guided rank adaptation process between pruning and low-rank decomposition, thereby effectively balancing communication costs and model performance. Experimental results across multiple datasets and model architectures demonstrate that FEGCM-FL significantly reduces communication overhead while maintaining high model accuracy.

papers.title: Market-Aware Request Scheduling for Long-Term Benefits in Computing Power Federation
papers.abstract: Driven by the growing demand for computational resources, the computing power network (CPN) model has emerged to enable more flexible and collaborative resource sharing. In this work, we envision a federation of independent computing power providers (CPPs) that collaborate to monetize their idle capacity. A computing power broker is introduced as an intermediary to coordinate resource transactions within the federation. However, the interplay of dynamic pricing between providers, fluctuating demand, and resource heterogeneity poses significant challenges to request scheduling to achieve long-term profitability and market stability. To address this, we propose GRASP, a three-tier framework for adaptive resource reservation and request scheduling in a computing power federation. GRASP employs Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to learn global reservation strategies, in which a virtual-queue-based reward shaping term inspired by Lyapunov optimization discourages persistent service deficits. A greedy strategy determines the reservation quantities per-provider, followed by an optimization based method that allocates resources to requests. Extensive experiments show that GRASP consistently achieves higher long term profit than both classical allocation heuristics and stronger online reservation baselines. Sensitivity analyses on pricing and supply, together with a utilization decomposition and high-value service-quality metrics, further explain where this advantage comes from.

papers.title: LDPAKE: A Unified PAKE–LDP–ZKP Framework for Verifiable Privacy in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative model training without transferring raw data, but practical deployments still lack a unified mechanism that simultaneously provides deployable mutual authentication, context-bound uploads, and verifiable client-side privacy protection. To address this problem, this paper presents a new LDPAKE framework that integrates OPAQUE, oblivious pseudorandom functions (OPRFs), local differential privacy (LDP), and zero-knowledge proofs into a single session-rooted protocol. The core idea is to use OPAQUE to establish a mutually authenticated session, derive a context-bound randomness anchor through an OPRF over the tuple (sid, t, ctr, ver, pid), and then let the client mix this anchor with fresh local entropy to generate the perturbation seed. In this way, the proof system no longer needs to encode the entire randomness-generation chain, but only proves that the uploaded perturbation is derived from the bound seed and satisfies the active clipping and noisebound policy. The resulting design preserves three properties in a unified manner: lightweight mutual authentication without PKI or trusted hardware, explicit binding of each upload to its session and round context, and verifiable client-side perturbation without revealing the plaintext update or the realized noise. The OPRF anchor strengthens context-bound seed provenance under a nonce-respecting execution in which the client fixes its local nonce before learning the anchor and one context counter admits at most one upload; it does not by itself prevent adaptive nonce grinding after the anchor is observed. Experimental results show practical access and upload performance under weak links and concurrent settings, while characterizing proof cost and the security of the explicitly encoded compliance relation.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: FedDPRL: Communication-Efficient Differentially Private Federated Reinforcement Learning With Adaptive Gradient Compression
papers.abstract: Cross-silo federated reinforcement learning (FRL) trains a shared policy across silos that must simultaneously respect a per-round uplink budget and on-device privacy. Although differential privacy (DP) and gradient compression each have mature solutions in supervised federated learning, naively stacking them in the policy-optimisation regime fails, for two structural reasons. First, whole-client DP injects noise whose ratio to the signal scales as$\sqrt {d}/N$, which for neural policies exceeds one at every practical$\varepsilon $, so the policy collapses to random. Second, a single shared compression mask cannot represent each client’s descent direction under non-i.i.d. environments, driving the compressor’s contraction constant toward zero and destroying learning. In this paper, we propose FedDPRL, a federated policy-optimisation algorithm built from two coupled designs. Specifically, a record-level (per-trajectory) Gaussian mechanism clips and noises each trajectory, lifting the effective sample size to$R=NB$and removing the$\sqrt {d}/N$barrier so that DP becomes viable on neural policies. Additionally, an error-feedback Top-$k$compressor with per-client masks preserves each client’s own descent direction while cutting the uplink by an order of magnitude. Experimental results across classic control, continuous control (MuJoCo), and vision with$N=20$clients show that FedDPRL matches dense DP-FedAvg-RL utility at 13–$14\times $less uplink, while a shared mask collapses to near-random.

papers.title: Personalized Exercise Recommendation via Federated Learning With Hierarchical Attention
papers.abstract: Personalized exercise recommendation aims to provide students with suitable learning materials based on their individual knowledge states and learning needs. However, existing recommendation systems still face two challenges: they often overlook the alignment between exercise difficulty and student proficiency, and they usually rely on a shared model that cannot adequately capture the heterogeneity among different schools. In this article, we propose FedPER, a federated personalized exercise recommendation framework that integrates federated learning with a hierarchical attention mechanism to support personalized recommendations across heterogeneous educational environments. In FedPER, each school is treated as an independent client with a two-stage local model consisting of knowledge tracing and exercise recommendation. For knowledge tracing, a graph convolutional network is employed to model the relationships among knowledge concepts based on a Phi-coefficient correlation matrix, while a gated recurrent unit captures the dynamic changes in students' knowledge states over time. Based on the estimated knowledge states, the exercise recommendation module identifies students' weak concepts and selects exercises by jointly considering knowledge relevance and difficulty adaptation. On the server side, a hierarchical attention mechanism (FedHAM) is introduced to perform adaptive model aggregation by considering layerwise differences between global and local parameters, thereby improving the model's ability to handle nonindependent and nonidentically distributed educational data. Experiments conducted on the ASSISTments 2009 dataset show that FedPER achieves competitive performance in terms of difficulty-adaptation accuracy, which measures how closely the difficulty of the recommended exercises matches each student's ability, and novelty compared with existing approaches under both federated and nonfederated settings. The results demonstrate that FedPER can provide effective personalized exercise recommendations while adapting to the heterogeneous data distributions and learning characteristics of different school-level clients.

papers.title: Augmented Edge Sensing Intelligence: A Federated Learning Framework for Resource-Efficient Beam Alignment
papers.abstract: Low-altitude Internet of Things (IoT) networks impose stringent requirements on beam alignment due to highly dynamic environments and limited onboard resources. Conventional beam training approaches incur substantial overhead and exhibit degraded robustness under such conditions. To achieve reliable beam alignment with minimal resource consumption, this paper proposes an edge intelligence framework that integrates sensing, communication, and computation (ISCC). Specifically, a federated learning (FL) mechanism is employed to collaboratively fuse local sensor knowledge across multiple nodes. To enable beam training, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is leveraged as a self-supervised sensor interface to generate labeled sensing datasets directly at distributed edge nodes. Over-the-air computation (AirComp) is then adopted for local model aggregation over shared spectrum, supported by an ISAC-based dynamic transmission control scheme. Apart from designing a resource-efficient system, a joint optimization of sensing, communication and computation resources is formulated to minimize the overall energy consumption. By deriving an FL convergence bound, the optimization problem is solved via Sequential Quadratic Programming algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed system significantly improves beam alignment accuracy in dynamic environments while reducing energy and spectrum consumption.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Fairness-Aware Participant Reputation Evaluation for Federated Learning in Intelligent Wearable Health Monitoring Scenarios
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving collaborative model training on resource-constrained intelligent wearable devices, making it a core technical paradigm for personal health monitoring services. However, traditional reputation evaluation approaches rely heavily on model accuracy while neglecting substantial hardware gaps and variations in data values across wearable devices. As a result, low-spec devices get their contributions unfairly underrated, dampening their participation enthusiasm. To tackle this challenge, we propose a fairness-aware participant reputation evaluation (F-PRE) mechanism for FL in intelligent wearable health monitoring. First, we construct a hierarchical evaluation framework that classifies devices based on inherent hardware constraints and set reasonable basic contribution weights. Both instantaneous and long-term fairness metrics are defined to comprehensively measure real-time training performance and sustained participation value of heterogeneous devices. In addition, we establish a lightweight multi-dimensional reputation model that considers data quality, training stability, participation activity, energy consumption, and collaboration compatibility, combined with peer assessment results to achieve comprehensive scoring. On this basis, we further integrate dynamic deviation calibration and fair incentive strategies into the F-PRE framework to eliminate evaluation bias caused by device performance gaps. Simulation results demonstrate that our F-PRE mechanism reduces reputation evaluation bias for resource-limited wearable devices by approximately 35% on average, effectively balancing the contribution valuation of heterogeneous participants and promoting stable collaboration.

papers.title: FSSG: Federated Semi-Supervised Learning With Self-Supervision and Global Coordination
papers.abstract: Federated learning enables privacy-preserving model training in edge and communication networks with distributed and bandwidth-constrained clients. However, practical deployments often suffer from extremely limited labeled data and severe non-IID distributions, which hinder data-efficient and stable federated optimization. This paper proposes FSSG, a communication-efficient federated semi-supervised learning framework that combines client-side self-supervised representation learning with server-coordinated semi-supervised optimization. To improve robustness under network-induced heterogeneity, FSSG adopts a confidence-weighted aggregation mechanism based on prediction uncertainty evaluated on a small server-side labeled probe set. In addition, a dynamic residual coordination strategy is introduced to stabilize global model updates across communication rounds. Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that FSSG consistently outperforms existing federated semi-supervised learning methods while maintaining moderate communication and computational overhead, making it suitable for data-efficient learning in edge networks.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: FedPriv: Personalized Differential Privacy in Federated Learning for Heterogeneous Data
papers.abstract: With the widespread adoption of interactive, mobile, and wearable technologies, an increasing amount of privacy-sensitive and statistically heterogeneous sensor data is being continuously generated by ubiquitous user devices. Federated learning (FL) enables multiple parties to jointly train a machine-learning model while keeping their raw data private. Nonetheless, under realistic conditions characterized by pronounced statistical heterogeneity across client distributions, traditional FL methods suffer from degraded performance. Moreover, uniform privacy mechanisms fail to accommodate the diverse privacy needs of individual users. To this end, we propose a privacy-preserving FL framework, FedPriv, for heterogeneous mobile sensor data, aiming to improve the performance of the model in a heterogeneous data environment while protecting user privacy. Specifically, FedPriv is built upon two core components that we design: (1) a novel aggregation mechanism that dynamically adjusts each client's contribution according to the discrepancy between local and global data distributions, thereby mitigating adverse effects of data heterogeneity on the model performance; and (2) a personalized differential privacy strategy that allocates privacy budgets adaptively, depending on each client's data sensitivity, enabling fine-grained privacy protection without compromising utility. In addition, FedPriv can be seamlessly integrated as a plug-and-play module into existing FL pipelines, enhancing model performance without requiring architectural modifications. Security analysis demonstrates that FedPriv satisfies formal$\epsilon$-differential privacy guarantees while supporting personalized privacy levels across users. Extensive experiments on six real-world datasets, consisting of four image datasets and two human activity recognition datasets, show that FedPriv achieves a 2.75%-5% improvement in model performance and reduces convergence time by an average of 15% when compared to existing baselines under heterogeneous data settings.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Federated Learning in Fog Computing Within IoT Environments: An Up-to-Date and Comprehensive Survey
papers.abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) connects diverse, resource-constrained devices, driving innovation in domains such as healthcare, smart cities, and industrial automation. However, the exponential growth of IoT devices poses critical challenges in data processing, privacy, security, and latency. Fog Computing (FC) mitigates these issues by decentralizing computational resources, processing and storing data locally to enable low-latency, high-quality services. This makes FC an ideal platform for integrating Federated Learning (FL), a decentralized machine learning paradigm that trains models locally on IoT devices and shares only aggregated updates, preserving data privacy. Since its introduction, FL has garnered considerable attention for enabling privacy-preserving collaborative model training in distributed environments. The convergence of IoT, FC, and FL offers substantial opportunities to advance IoT system performance, but it also presents challenges in resource allocation, security, energy efficiency, computational complexity, and system heterogeneity. This survey provides a comprehensive and up-to-date analysis of the integration of FL and FC within IoT environments, exploring their synergies, challenges, and state-of-the-art advancements.We review critical aspects, including infrastructure enhancements, security mechanisms, and the emerging role of Digital Twin (DT) technology, which creates virtual replicas of IoT devices to optimize system efficiency and real-time performance. Through case studies in healthcare and smart cities, we highlight practical applications of FL-FC integration. We compare our work with existing surveys, highlight its specific focus on the FL-FC-IoT-DT convergence, and identify open challenges and future research directions toward secure, scalable, and intelligent IoT ecosystems.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: FML-AD: A Federated Learning Framework With Meta-Model Refinement for Cyberattack Duration Prediction in 5G O-RAN
papers.abstract: The emergence of fifth-generation (5G) and open radio access network (O-RAN) architectures has expanded the attack surface for cyber threats, creating an urgent need for enhanced and proactive mitigation strategies to ensure the preservation of quality of service (QoS), network reliability, and user data privacy in highly distributed and virtualized environments. In this context, we introduce FML-AD, a federated learning framework with meta-model refinement for adaptive attack duration prediction without centralizing raw training traffic. The proposed method combines a FLAD-trained Transformer for distributed temporal learning with an XGBoost-based second-level regression model that refines the initial predictions using controlled O-RAN testbed examples, thereby reducing prediction errors associated with the benchmark-to-deployment distribution shift. Extensive evaluation on the CICIoT2023 dataset shows that FML-AD improves prediction accuracy compared with conventional centralized and federated baselines. Furthermore, an evaluation on a controlled 5G O-RAN testbed involving ten TCP SYN and UDP flooding scenarios provides a proof-of-concept demonstration of the feasibility of the proposed post-detection prediction pipeline in the evaluated configuration. A separate exploratory transfer-learning assessment using 5G V2X radio-jamming scenarios and leave-one-scenario-out (LOSO) validation further examines whether the duration-prediction pipeline can be adapted to a different disruption mechanism under limited target-domain data. For the considered jamming configurations, several operating points in the early 3–5 sec range also produce favorable prediction results, providing preliminary evidence of transferability.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: Heterogeneous Federated Learning Using Reliable Prototypes with Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Recently, a number of Heterogeneous Federated Learning (HtFL) methods have been proposed to address the problems of data and model heterogeneity using prototypes. However, the prototypes learned by individual clients may be unreliable, and simple server-side averaging may propagate such unreliability to the aggregated prototypes, which would significantly affect the efficacy of global prototypes. To solve this problem, a new HtFL method using reliable prototypes with graph neural networks, named FedRG, is proposed. FedRG assigns distinct reliability aggregation weights to client prototypes and then accordingly constructs their prototype subgraphs. After that, a graph neural network is used to optimize the collaborative relationships among clients within each subgraph, enabling the aggregation of personalized prototypes for local feature alignment. Therefore, FedRG can maintain reliable global information for each client while mitigating feature misalignment. Experiments on a large number of heterogeneous models demonstrate that FedRG achieves the best accuracy in most experimental settings, while still maintaining the communication and privacy advantages of prototype-based HtFL. The code is available at https://github.com/maker27-z/FedRG.

papers.title: Integrated Power–Communication Framework for BESS Scheduling in Multi-Community Active Distribution Networks
papers.abstract: The integration of battery energy storage systems (BESS) in active distribution networks (ADNs) requires reliable communication networks that connect distributed energy resources (DERs) to distribution system operators (DSOs). This paper presents a co-simulation framework that combines parallelized BESS scheduling optimization, packet-level communication network modeling, and DSO supervisory commands to evaluate power–communication inter-dependencies across multi-community ADNs. The framework integrates a scalable OpenDSS-PM power distribution system model, an OMNeT++/INET communication network emulator, and a DSO federate, coupled through HELICS using a lightweight DNP3-over-TCP/IP protocol to enable time-stamped measurement and command signal exchanges. A community-level BESS scheduling approach is utilized to determine optimal charge/discharge setpoints for peak demand shaving. The framework is evaluated under three scenarios on a modified IEEE 13- bus test feeder: ideal communications, shared-network congestion, and contingency event operation. Results demonstrate how communication latency, throughput limitations, and channel utilization affect BESS scheduling, supervisory command signal responsiveness, and the overall reliable operation of the ADN. The framework enables utilities and researchers to assess communication-aware BESS scheduling strategies, exploring infrastructure requirements, and enhancing ADN operation under realistic communication network conditions.

papers.title: Covert Air–Ground Federated Learning With Pruning: Enabling by STAR-RIS
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) can safeguard the data privacy for air-ground networks, while simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS) can help further enhance its channel quality. However, the model exchanges in FL may be detected by wardens, and air-ground links increase this threat. In this paper, we investigate a STAR-RIS aided air-ground covert FL scheme to hide the presence of uploading, where the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) acts as an aerial server to collect local models from the distributed devices. To alleviate the communication burden, each device prunes the local model before transmitting. The minimum detection error probability at the warden is derived with the optimal detection threshold, indicating the worst case for the legitimate covert FL. Then, we analyze the convergence of the proposed FL scheme and provide an upper bound on the expected convergence gap of global loss function. To improve the learning performance, the convergence gap is minimized subject to the covertness and latency constraints. Specifically, the closed-forms of optimal pruning ratio and transmit power are derived, while the phase shifts of STAR-RIS and UAV position can be optimized by semidefinite relaxation and successive convex approximation, respectively. Finally, the overall problem can be solved via an alternative algorithm. Numerical results validate that the proposed covert air-ground FL scheme can achieve excellent test accuracy and convergence performance while guaranteeing the covertness assisted by STAR-RIS.

papers.title: ZK-Trace: Certified Collusion Tracing with Zero-Knowledge Credentials for Federated GNSS Interference Monitoring
papers.abstract: Federated global navigation satellite system (GNSS) monitoring distributes a proprietary classifier to partly trusted stations, any of which may leak its copy. ZK-Trace combines public identity marks, recipient-specific Tardos fingerprints, and zero-knowledge credential verification. The registry supports offline tracing without the leaker's cooperation. We establish conditional false-accusation bounds for arbitrary recovered bit patterns, a finite completeness bound under a hidden-bias residual channel, and a deterministic tracing-score bound for correlated feature-distillation errors. An interval-arithmetic checker makes the conditional bound executable and allocates a common budget across accusation and tamper decisions. Under innocent-row independence, the certificate-based evaluation uses a false-naming budget of 0.001 per investigation. It isolates all 160 single-owner copies and traces 712 of 720 two-owner mixtures without naming an innocent. Experiments use a simulated GNSS federation and CIFAR-10. Feature matching preserves the feature mark in 20/20 runs and cross-architecture transfer in 19/20, at copy-accuracy costs of 4.8 and 6.1 percentage points on GNSS and CIFAR-10. Function-only distillation erases the feature mark, and distillation also removes weight-space marks. These results support verifiable tracing under explicit statistical and cryptographic assumptions. Credential knowledge and recipient evidence serve distinct roles.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems

papers.title: From Uniform to Calibration: Priority-Conditioned Differential Privacy for Federated Vehicular Edge Client Selection
papers.abstract: Vehicular edge computing reduces transmission latency by moving computing resources closer to vehicles. Federated learning further limits raw-data transmission by enabling local model training and uploading only model updates. However, uploaded updates remain vulnerable to model inversion or membership inference attacks by honest-but-curious servers or external adversaries. Moreover, conventional differential privacy (DP) assigns a uniform privacy budget across tasks, failing to accommodate the diverse priorities and privacy requirements of vehicular applications and potentially degrading model utility for less-sensitive tasks. To address these issues, we propose a client selection and resource allocation strategy integrating federated learning with Vehicular Edge Computing, aiming to reduce system processing latency and energy consumption while preserving the user privacy. First, we formulate the client selection and resource allocation decision problem as a Markov decision process. The formulation considers task completion, latency, energy consumption, and model accuracy, while privacy protection is enforced by priority-conditioned DP. Task priority is used to calibrate the privacy budget of uploaded updates, and Laplace perturbation is applied after update clipping. FL_MADDPG is then used to learn adaptive client selection and resource allocation policies in dynamic vehicular environments. Experiments on multiple datasets show that the proposed framework reduces latency and energy consumption compared with representative DRL baselines while maintaining model utility under differentiated privacy protection.

papers.title: Generative Federated Learning-Driven Privacy-Preserving Collaborative Optimization for Multimicrogrid Systems
papers.abstract: Collaborative optimization in multimicrogrid systems (MMSs) is critical for enhancing operational efficiency, yet it is often challenged by excessive conservatism in traditional robust optimization, prohibitive communication payload, and privacy vulnerabilities in standard federated learning. To address these issues, this article proposes a novel privacy-preserving collaborative optimization framework integrating generative federated learning (GFed) with Stackelberg game theory. A time-varying weight uncertainty set is constructed to adaptively characterize wind power fluctuations, so as to mitigate overconservatism. For secure global coordination, a GFed mechanism is introduced where each microgrid locally trains its own denoising diffusion probabilistic model and uploads the preserved local generative parameters together with low-dimensional statistical features to the distribution system operator (DSO). The DSO aggregates these parameters and performs conditional reverse sampling to synthesize personalized proxy responses. The DSO-MMSs interaction is formulated as a Stackelberg game and transformed into a mathematical program with equilibrium constraints via Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions to attain an optimal collaborative equilibrium. Extensive simulations on the IEEE 69-bus system demonstrate that the proposed scheme drastically reduces the online collaborative communication payload compared with existing privacy-preserving algorithms. It decreases reconstruction attack success rates by 55.6%, 55.0%, and 21.3% over FedAvg, loosely coupled federated learning, and differential privacy-alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), respectively, with the membership inference area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) remaining close to the 0.5 random inference baseline. Meanwhile, the proposed framework attains a desirable balance among privacy security, economic performance, and computation efficiency.

papers.title: RBHFL: A Robust Blockchain-Secured Hierarchical Federated Learning Framework for Edge Computing
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in edge computing environments has accelerated the adoption of federated learning (FL) for privacy-preserving model training. However, conventional FL frameworks remain vulnerable to single-point failures and model poisoning, while existing blockchain-based FL schemes often introduce high communication overhead in large-scale edge systems. To address these challenges, this paper proposesRBHFL-aRobustBlockchain-securedHierarchicalFederatedLearningframework tailored for edge computing. RBHFL employs a two-layer architecture: devices perform vanilla FL with their edge server in the lower layer, while a permissioned blockchain coordinates and audits server-layer aggregation in the upper layer. Specifically, aBlockchain-Secured Global Model Aggregation (BSGMA)mechanism integrates aBlockchain Data Model, anAuditor-Guided Model Validationprocess, and aProof-of-Integrity (PoI)consensus to enhance security. Through these mechanisms, model parameters, validation results, and reputation updates are immutably recorded on-chain, enabling transparent auditing and traceability of malicious participants. Extensive experiments show that RBHFL achieves strong resilience against Byzantine corruption and various poisoning attacks, accurately identifies compromised participants, and maintains accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art robust FL methods such as Krum and Trimmed Mean, while reducing total training time by up to 41.28%.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Model-Heterogeneous Federated Fault Diagnosis With Distilled Data Aggregation and Proxy-Based Tridirectional Training
papers.abstract: Mechanical fault diagnosis has become critical with the growing complexity and automation of industrial systems. In practical scenarios, fault data are often distributed across decentralized clients with heterogeneous data distributions and privacy constraints, while different clients may adopt different model architectures due to deployment-specific requirements. Federated learning (FL) facilitates collaborative model training across decentralized clients without sharing raw data; however, standard parameter-aggregation-based FL generally relies on architectural consistency across clients, which is difficult to satisfy in model-heterogeneous mechanical fault diagnosis. To address this problem, this article proposes federated distilled data aggregation with proxy-based tridirectional training (FedDDA-P3T) for model-heterogeneous federated fault diagnosis. More specifically, each client independently distills its local dataset into a compact distilled dataset and uploads it to the server. The distilled data are not used merely as compact substitutes for local datasets; instead, they serve as model-agnostic knowledge carriers and are aggregated on the server to support knowledge transfer across heterogeneous client models. Moreover, the server-aggregated distilled data are redistributed to clients as shared training anchors. A proxy model is further introduced to bridge heterogeneous private models through these shared anchors, forming a proxy-based tridirectional training strategy. Experiments on mechanical fault diagnosis datasets demonstrate that FedDDA-P3T achieves superior diagnostic performance over representative state-of-the-art FL methods under model-heterogeneous settings.

papers.title: Semi-Supervised Vertical Federated Framework for HSI and LiDAR Classification with Soft Linkages
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of remote sensing technology, the joint classification of hyperspectral image (HSI) and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) data has been widely studied. However, in real-world scenarios, multi-modality data are typically distributed across different platforms, making centralized training infeasible due to privacy constraints and communication costs. Moreover, obtaining sufficient labeled samples remains a major challenge. To address these issues, we propose a Shared-Specific Feature Decoupling-based Semi-Supervised Vertical Federated Learning Framework (S$^{2}$F) for HSI and LiDAR classification, which effectively exploits overlapping samples across clients to improve the classification performance under limited labeled overlapping samples without exchanging raw data. Specifically, we design the Cross-Client Self-Supervised Learning module to leverage overlapping samples and disentangle modality-shared and modality-specific features to enhance the representation capability while preserving critical information of each modality. Additionally, we propose a Dual Graph Neural Network-based Feature Aggregation module, which aggregates superpixel-level features across clients based on soft linkages and supplements them with pixel-level details through GraphSAGE. Our method only requires the exchange of superpixel intermediate features, avoiding raw data or gradient transmission, thereby ensuring privacy and reducing communication overhead. Experimental results on three public datasets demonstrate that the S$^{2}$F framework achieves accurate joint classification.

papers.title: High-Performance and Low-Energy NoC Mapping for Real-Time Heterogeneous Parallel DSP
papers.abstract: Privacy boundaries among intellectual property (IP) vendors make conventional centralized Network-on-Chip (NoC) mapping difficult to apply to heterogeneous chiplet-based DSP platforms. The problem is further complicated by non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) design preferences, strict bandwidth and timing constraints, and the large discrete search space arising from energy-latency trade-offs. This paper presents FedMap, a federated deep reinforcement learning approach that separates centralized environment simulation from decentralized policy optimization. Under a trusted-coordinator threat model, participating vendors retain proprietary communication graphs, task information, and traffic characteristics locally, while model updates are protected through gradient clipping, local noise perturbation, and secure aggregation. To improve mapping efficiency, FedMap incorporates a preference-conditioned graph hierarchical Actor-Critic (PC-GAC), which exploits communication dependencies and decomposes the original decision space while adapting to different energy-latency preferences. In addition, a preference-clustered, contribution-aware aggregation strategy (PC²-Agg) is developed to mitigate instability caused by heterogeneous client objectives and constraint conditions. Evaluations on real-time heterogeneous DSP mapping tasks show that FedMap consistently achieves better solutions than representative state-of-the-art approaches. It decreases communication cost, communication energy, and average network latency by 40.95%, 41.38%, and 39.10%, respectively. The framework also maintains stable mapping performance as system scale increases and constraints become more stringent, demonstrating its potential for privacy-preserving collaborative NoC optimization.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

papers.title: FedUCANet-MoE: In-Vehicle Communication Anomaly Detection Based on Federated Mixture-of-Experts Model
papers.abstract: Anomaly detection in vehicular communication is critical for ensuring the safety of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). Although deep learning methods have achieved strong performance, their deployment is limited by privacy concerns and centralized data collection. Federated learning (FL) provides a privacy-preserving solution, but its effectiveness is often degraded by non-IID data, resource constraints, and unstable client participation. To address these challenges, we propose FedUCANet-MoE, a lightweight personalized federated learning framework for in-vehicle anomaly detection. First, we design UCANet, a compact model based on the Universal Inverted Bottleneck (UIB), enabling efficient feature extraction under resource constraints. Then, we introduce a mixture-of-experts (MoE) mechanism that adaptively fuses a global model and a locally specialized model through a lightweight router, achieving sample-level personalization. Experiments on two CAN bus datasets, Car-Hacking and CICIoV2024, demonstrate that UCANet achieves over 99% accuracy with only 1.8M parameters and 0.7ms inference latency, significantly outperforming existing lightweight models. Furthermore, FedUCANet-MoE consistently outperforms FedAvg, local fine-tuning, FedProx, and Ditto under various non-IID settings and partial client participation scenarios. These results indicate that the proposed framework effectively balances global generalization and local specialization, providing a practical and robust solution for privacy-preserving anomaly detection in IoV systems. The source code of this study is available athttps://github.com/chng2504/FedUCANet-MoE
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems

papers.title: Towards Channel-Level Privacy: Exploring Gradient Leakage Attack and Lightweight Defense in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning framework that enhances privacy and data security. However, model parameters communicated between the central server and local clients are still vulnerable to gradient leakage attacks (GLA), where attackers can fully reconstruct the local training data, posing serious privacy risks. To defend against such attacks, differential privacy is commonly used to provide privacy guarantees for FL, but this often comes at the cost of substantial performance degradation. To address this challenge, we explore GLA from a novel perspective of channels and, through comprehensive experiments, discover that using only partial channel information from certain parameters, rather than complete information from all channels, is sufficient to recover original images. Further analysis validates that the channel information in shared parameters is critical, with its amount directly determining the success of the attack. Based on this insight, we propose FedLCP, a lightweight channel-level privacy protection method. It leverages the trace of the empirical Fisher information matrix to estimate the information contained in each parameter channel and injects adaptive channel-level noise, effectively defending against both GLA and our newly explored channel-level attacks. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical analysis for the convergence of FL when applying our method. Extensive experiments conducted on three datasets demonstrate that FedLCP not only provides privacy protection comparable to differential privacy but also achieves significant accuracy improvements, with excellent convergence and only a slight impact on computational costs.

papers.title: Decentralized Federated Edge With Multiagent Coordination and Learnable Aggregator Election for Internet of Vehicles
papers.abstract: Decentralized federated learning (DFL) enables privacy-preserving training without a central server, removing the single-point-of-failure risk of centralized federated learning. In highly dynamic settings, such as the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), device heterogeneity causes stragglers, while time-varying links and no global coordination complicate load balancing and aggregation scheduling. Cooperation relieves stragglers but couples a node's training cost with its neighbors' resources, blurring individual contributions and complicating aggregation-node selection in dynamic networks. To address these challenges, we propose DMASFL, a decentralized multiagent split federated learning (SFL) framework for dynamic edge networks like IoV. DMASFL models each roadside unit (RSU) in the IoV as an autonomous, partially observable agent that self-organizes into clusters and decides participation, resource allocation, and SFL cooperation. Each cluster trains cooperatively and aggregates locally, and cluster heads gossip across clusters for final aggregation. DMASFL includes two mechanisms to optimize cooperation: dynamic adaptive head election elects heads by candidate-induced aggregation-path loss and historical service load, and active bottleneck-set credit assignment estimates key nodes' marginal effect on team utility via single-node counterfactual replacement, with residual correction for multinode interactions. On DroneVehicle, DMASFL outperforms representative mutliagent reinforcement learning and DFL baselines in throughput, training efficiency, and load balancing. Sensitivity, scalability, and MIMII-DUE validation show that DMASFL remains effective under stale information, varying RSU scales, and latency and communication constraints.

papers.title: Over-the-Air Bayesian Federated Meta-Learning-Based Efficient Digital Twin Training for Resources-Constrained Edge Networks
papers.abstract: This paper studies a DT training problem in a resources-constrained edge network scenario. An Over-the-Air Computation assisted Bayesian Federated Meta-Learning (ABFM) framework is first proposed for DT training, which relieves the computing resources constrained problem in DT training by enabling a DT model with fast adaptation capability and relieves the bandwidth resources constrained problem in DT training by using an AirComp scheme for global aggregation. The convergence of the ABFM framework is derived to analyze the main factors that affect the upper bound of a global model’s convergence error. A novel AirComp scheme is proposed for DT training based on the ABFM framework to improve the transmission efficiency for DT training in the network. The DT training problem is formulated as a mixed integer programming problem with an objective to minimize a weighted sum of the convergence residuals of DT models, DT training delay, and the energy consumption of DT training by jointly optimizing the selection of user devices, the design of beamforming, and the allocation of CPU frequencies. An ABFM-based DT Training (ABFM-DTT) algorithm is proposed to solve the formulated problem. Simulation results show that the proposed ABFM framework and ABFM-DTT algorithm can achieve better performance than several benchmark frameworks and algorithms in terms of DT model accuracy, DT training delay and DT training energy consumption.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Trustworthy Learning Analytics in Digital Education: A Robust Federated Affective Modeling Approach
papers.abstract: The rapid digitalization of education worldwide has made learning analytics (LA) a core part of modern educational infrastructure, increasing the need for robust artificial intelligence (AI) systems that can automatically infer students’ learning states and support reliable decisions. Federated learning (FL) enables geographically distributed institutions to jointly train affective recognition models while keeping raw institutional data local. At the same time, deploying FL in educational settings raises important security risks. The nonindependent and identically distributed nature of institution-level educational data and recording conditions can obscure compromised clients, enabling stealthy backdoors that hide indicators of distress or exaggerate engagement-related affective signals. These attacks reduce the trustworthiness of AI-assisted analytics and can distort downstream intervention decisions. To address these risks, we propose a proactive defense framework for federated affective analytics systems. Our method is motivated by the observation that backdoor attacks often exploit model capacity that is rarely used during normal training. Based on this idea, we introduce a server-side redundancy saturation mechanism that uses public out-of-distribution (OOD) data to occupy redundant parameter space, while using synthetic in-distribution (ID) proxy data to stabilize ID behavior and preserve performance on the primary emotion-recognition task. The proposed procedure does not require server access to raw client data and can be integrated into existing FL workflows. Experiments on public affect-recognition proxy benchmarks under diverse federated settings show that, across the main attack evaluations, our framework reduces the worst-case backdoor accuracy from 92.15% without defense to 10.19%, while preserving main-task accuracy, supporting its use as a security component for federated educational affective LA.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems

papers.title: Towards a Fair Incentive Mechanism for Federated Learning in the Internet of Vehicles
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), the explosive growth in data volume has raised concerns about data privacy. Federated Learning (FL), as a decentralized machine learning technology, can effectively protect data privacy. However, FL applications in IoV scenarios still face significant challenges, mainly reflected in the lack of fairness in incentive mechanism design and insufficient consideration of the impact of high vehicle mobility on the FL process. These issues can lead to insufficient vehicle participation, which limits the effectiveness of model training. To address these challenges in the dynamic environment of IoV, we propose a dynamic incentive mechanism based on the Stackelberg game. The mechanism aims to improve the fairness of the incentive mechanism by optimizing reward distribution and contribution evaluation, thereby promoting active vehicle participation and comprehensively considering the impact of vehicle mobility on the incentive process. Theoretical analysis and experimental results demonstrate that our scheme effectively enhances the fairness of the system and improves the performance of the global model.

papers.title: Hierarchical Alignment and Differentiated Prototype Aggregation for Heterogeneous Federated Learning in Industrial Internet of Things
Robust Bidding Strategies under Censored Feedback for Auction-Based Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Auction-based Federated Learning (AFL) provides a principled framework for incentivizing self-interested data owners (DOs) to participate in collaborative learning initiated by data consumers (DCs) through market mechanisms. A central challenge in AFL is to determine how a budget-constrained DC should bid for data-use rights. Existing methods often conflate the submitted bid with the realized payment. This treatment is inconsistent with the widely adopted second-price sealed-bid (SPSB) mechanism, in which the highest bidder wins but pays the market price determined by the competing bids rather than its own bid. Moreover, the market price is observed by a target DC only after a win; after a loss, the DC observes only that the market price exceeds its submitted bid, producing right-censored feedback. To address these challenges, we propose KMM-AFL, a return-on-investment (ROI)-aware bidding framework that explicitly separates bid price from expected SPSB payment and combines DO utility estimation with request-conditioned market-price modeling. KMM-AFL uses a conditional Kaplan Meier (KM) construction to exploit both winning and losing auction records. Because exact repetitions of high-dimensional bid requests are sparse, a conditional Markov Network estimates the observed winning-price and losing-probability terms required by KM. The recovered request-conditioned market-price distribution and the estimated DO valuation are then used to select the largest bid satisfying a common expected-return requirement and the remaining-budget constraint. Extensive evaluations across 6 benchmark datasets show that KMM-AFL outperforms state-of the-art baselines, achieving a 16.56% increase in DC utility and a 3.36% improvement in FL model accuracy.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

papers.title: Joint Optimization of Model Pruning and Bandwidth Allocation for Resource-Constrained Wireless Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Wireless Federated Learning (FL) enables User Equipments (UEs) to collaboratively train a shared model under the coordination of the Base Station (BS) without exposing their private data. However, due to limited computation and communication resources, some UEs may be unable to train the full model, causing the global model to miss important data features and resulting in degraded performance. Even when training is possible, UEs often cannot complete each round at the same pace, leading to the synchronization barrier and increased overall time. In this paper, we propose FedPB, a framework that accelerates wireless FL by dynamically adjusting the pruning ratios and bandwidth allocation. Specifically, we formulate a joint pruning ratio and bandwidth allocation optimization problem that minimizes the total completion time under resource constraints while ensuring convergence. We theoretically analyze the convergence behavior, and based on the analysis, decompose the joint optimization problem into subproblems, which are solved iteratively. Extensive experiments on both CNN-based vision tasks and Transformer-based language tasks demonstrate that FedPB achieves up to 5× speedup under resource constraints while preserving the performance of the global model.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: FL-DPIP: A Privacy-Preserving and Intelligent Paging System Using Federated Learning in 6G Networks
papers.abstract: Paging is a fundamental service in mobile communication networks that enables the network to locate idle user equipment (UE) when downlink data arrives. In emerging 6G networks, the traditional paging mechanism lacks intelligence and faces significant challenges in handling the massive number of mobile terminal accesses, resulting in substantial signaling resource overhead. Moreover, existing paging systems lack effective privacy-preserving capabilities, thereby posing potential privacy risks when user mobility data is used for intelligent analytics. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Privacy-Preserving and Intelligent Paging System (FL-DPIP).
