Current privacy protection methods struggle to balance communication efficiency with attribute privacy protection, especially for identity-related features. Existing methods often provide insufficient protection against sensitive facial-attribute inference while attempting to preserve the usability of protected data. To address these issues, this work proposes FedDP, a federated learning based reversible face differential privacy protection method. It integrates a pre-trained StyleGAN2 generator and a lightweight latent space encryptor to reversibly encrypt facial identity in the latent space, allowing dynamic data recovery with a key and adjustable privacy strength via the privacy budget. In addition, FedDP reduces the risk of sensitive facial-attribute inference by applying image-specific latent-space encryption and a unified local differential privacy mechanism to the complete encrypted latent representation. FedDP does not identify semantic attributes or assign separate attribute-level privacy budgets during the protection process. Clients apply latent space encryption and local differential privacy noise, while the server adds noise to aggregated updates, ensuring end-to-end protection. Experiments show that FedDP achieves 99% feature reversibility, allows the overall privacy level to be adjusted through the unified privacy budgets, and limits the ResNet-based multi-attribute inference attack success rate to 2.15% when all 10 target attributes are correctly inferred, effectively balancing usability and privacy.

papers.title: Structure-Regularized Framework for Federated Incomplete Multi-View Clustering
papers.abstract: Data incompleteness and privacy preservation are critical challenges in federated incomplete multi-view clustering. Although recent studies have proposed several solutions, they often suffer from widespread view-missing issues and the difficulty of establishing cross-client consensus under privacy constraints, which hinders reliable missing-data recovery and high-quality representation learning. To address these issues, we propose a structure-guided missing-data recovery framework for federated incomplete multi-view scenarios. Specifically, each client constructs a dynamic anchor graph to capture local structural relationships and performs reliable missing-view data recovery via anchor-based reconstruction. Global structural information is introduced to constrain this recovery process, thereby improving the consistency and reliability of the recovered data. Concurrently, a compact-statistics communication mechanism is designed to exchange pseudo-labels and centroid matrices for global consensus building. The resulting global consensus labels guide representation learning and structural alignment, while consensus centroids enhance semantic consistency across clients. Furthermore, the framework avoids explicit construction of dense affinity matrices and achieves linear complexity with respect to the number of samples via implicit computation, significantly reducing communication overhead and computational cost. Extensive experiments on eight benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior clustering performance over existing federated methods, and outperforms centralized multi-view clustering approaches in terms of both communication and computational efficiency.

papers.title: Federated Learning With Lossy Lempel–Ziv Gradient Compression
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has gained widespread adoption for distributed model training due to its ability to preserve privacy and deliver promising learning performance. However, the limited availability of communication resources can significantly slow down the training process. To address this issue, this paper proposes two gradient compression schemes based on Lempel-Ziv (LZ) coding: Lossy Lempel-Ziv with element-wise distortion$p$(LLZ-$p$) and Lossy Lempel-Ziv with Side Information (LLZ-SI). The LLZ-$p$algorithm exploits the inherent redundancy within local gradients and introduces a controlled distortion into the vanilla Lempel-Ziv scheme. Our convergence analysis demonstrates that LLZ-$p$can not only notably reduce communication costs, but also achieve a sublinear convergence rate comparable to that of its lossless counterpart. LLZ-SI further enhances compression by exploiting historical gradient information available at both clients and the server, effectively balancing the compression of current and past gradients. Extensive experiments on various datasets and learning models demonstrate that the proposed LZ-based schemes reduce communication by 58% without degrading accuracy and by up to 90% while maintaining nearly the same learning performance.

papers.title: Edge-Enabled Federated BEFAST: A Multimodal Consumer IoMT Framework for Early Stroke Screening
papers.abstract: Early stroke identification in consumer home environments is challenging due to sudden symptom onset, low public awareness, reliance on observer-dependent screening, overlapping non-stroke manifestations, and the lack of continuous multimodal monitoring. To address these challenges, this paper proposes Edge-Enabled Federated BEFAST, a lightweight multimodal Consumer Internet of Medical Things (CIoMT) framework that operationalizes the clinically used BEFAST triage guideline into measurable behavioral indicators derived from wearable motion sensing, speech analysis, and vision-based facial cues. Each modality is processed locally using compact deeplearning models executed on consumer-grade edge devices, while an interpretable edge-level fusion mechanism generates real-time stroke-consistent screening decisions and records stroke onset time based on the first detected BEFAST-aligned abnormality. To handle issues like data privacy, limited labeled stroke samples, and strong inter-user behavioral heterogeneity across homes, the framework employs a federated transfer learning (FTL) strategy. Local models are adapted to individual users under non-IID data distributions while sharing only model updates for global optimization without exposing raw signals. Experimental evaluation using publicly available multimodal datasets under realistic federated settings demonstrates the feasibility, scalability, and effectiveness of the proposed approach for early stroke symptom screening. The proposed system advances consumer-electronics driven healthcare by enabling timely intervention, objective decision support, and privacy-preserving AI-assisted stroke monitoring in ambient-intelligence homes.

papers.title: FedV: Privacy-aware Federated Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dependable Volunteer-supported Edge Computing
papers.abstract: Large-scale edge IoT systems increasingly rely on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) to coordinate distributed devices for compute-intensive tasks. However, existing MADRL paradigms often require a centralized critic or cross device information sharing, which can expose devices' local states and thus raise privacy concerns. This paper develops fedV, a privacy-aware federated deep reinforcement learning framework for volunteer-supported edge computing, where opportunistic volunteer devices are selected to elastically extend edge capacity. Due to intermittent and untrusted volunteer resources, MADRL-based coordination becomes a highly challenging long term optimization problem. To preserve multi-agent cooperation without raw-state exposure, fedV adopts a hierarchical learning architecture based on two-tier federated learning. Specifically, IoT-side agents are trained from local observations, while an edge-side agent aggregates privacy-preserving representations to make global decisions under strict device-side privacy protection. We further introduce a reversed-reward weighted aggregation rule to improve learning efficiency under heterogeneous and non-IID multi-agent interactions. Compared with representative baselines, fedV improves the long-term average reward by up to 30.9% and the converged reward by up to 54.6%. These simulations demonstrate that fedV achieves robust schedulability and scalability under different edge-capacity settings.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Privacy-Preserving Personalized Federated Learning Against Poisoning and Inference Attacks in Intelligent Enterprises
papers.abstract: Data-driven decision-making is a key enabler of intelligent enterprises, yet centralized machine learning (ML) poses privacy and efficiency risks. Federated learning (FL) offers a decentralized solution. Still, it faces 1) high communication cost, 2) vulnerability to poisoning and inference attacks, and 3) degraded performance on non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data. This paper presentsFedAnil+++, a privacy-preserving and communication-efficient FL model with three phases: (i) dynamic gradient compression, (ii) multi-layer protection via cosine similarity (CS) filtering, CKKS-FHE, and blockchain aggregation, and (iii) personalized FL (PFL) through clustering and adversarial learning. Experiments on FEMNIST, CIFAR-10, and TON-IoT show thatFedAnil+++boosts accuracy by 15.75%, cuts communication by 25.87%, and reduces computation by 4.5% over baselines. Privacy metrics, Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence, Shannon entropy, and correlation analysis confirm that CKKS-FHE effectively conceals sensitive patterns. The implementation ofFedAnil+++is publicly available on GitHubhttps://github.com/rezafotohi/FedAnilPlusPlusPlus
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Multidimensional Dynamic Trust Evaluation for False Unlearning Attacks in Federated Unlearning
papers.abstract: Federated unlearning has become a necessary mechanism for removing poisoned, sensitive, or withdrawn data from federated models. However, existing unlearning protocols often treat a client's acknowledgment of deletion as evidence of compliance. This assumption leaves a critical false unlearning vulnerability: malicious clients can return updates that appear consistent with unlearning while retaining backdoor knowledge, which may subsequently contaminate the global model through aggregation. The central problem is therefore to distinguish genuine forgetting from deceptive compliance during the unlearning process and to prevent untrustworthy clients from participating in later training rounds. To address this problem, this paper proposes a multidimensional dynamic trust evaluation framework that transforms unlearning verification into privacy-preserving, evidence-driven trust inference.To prevent attackers from identifying and overfitting the trap probes, the probe reference gradient is protected by CKKS approximate homomorphic encryption, while Johnson-Lindenstrauss random projection compressing. The resulting behavioral and quality trust values are fused through entropy-based weighting and evolved across rounds using Markov trust updating.Experimental results under false unlearning attack demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively identifies malicious clients, suppresses residual backdoor effects, and provides a more robust trust-evaluation solution for securing federated unlearning.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Adaptive Local Aggregation for Personalized Federated Learning in Agricultural Terrain Mapping
papers.abstract: Statistical heterogeneity and non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data remain major challenges in federated learning, particularly for agricultural terrain mapping where geographically distributed sensing devices collect highly diverse remote sensing data. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an Adaptive Local Aggregation (ALA)-based personalized federated learning framework that improves client-specific model initialization while preserving the standard federated learning communication and global aggregation protocol. Rather than directly replacing local models with the received global model, the proposed framework adaptively initializes selected higher-layer parameters using learnable client-specific aggregation weights, thereby balancing globally shared knowledge with local personalization prior to client-side training. The proposed framework is evaluated on four agricultural remote sensing datasets, namely AgriFieldNet, BigEarthNetv1, BigEarthNetv2, and CropHarvest, together with three benchmark image classification datasets, MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, under heterogeneous federated learning settings. Experimental results demonstrate consistent improvements in global classification accuracy and convergence behaviour compared with state-of-the-art federated learning methods, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed framework for privacy-preserving agricultural terrain mapping under heterogeneous client data distributions.

papers.title: IMFR: An Efficient Incentive Mechanism Against Free-Rider Attacks for Differentially Private Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) breaks down data silos through distributed collaboration. Due to the limited motivation of participants, incentive mechanisms are essential for encouraging sustained participation. However, existing incentive mechanisms are vulnerable to free-rider attacks, particularly in differentially private FL (DPFL), where the injected privacy noise obscures intrinsic gradient characteristics and significantly degrades the effectiveness of existing free-rider detection methods. Moreover, most existing incentive mechanisms adopt conventional aggregation strategies without incorporating participant contributions, thereby limiting the performance of the global model. To address these challenges, this article proposes an efficient incentive mechanism against free-rider attacks for DPFL, called incentive mechanism against free-rider (IMFR). Specifically, the central server detects free-riders by performing linear regression on the cosine similarities of consecutive local updates and records their historical behaviors. Based on the historical free-riding behavior, local data size, and privacy budget of each participant, IMFR evaluates participant contributions and performs contribution-weighted model aggregation to improve the quality of the global model. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that IMFR satisfies long-term incentive compatibility, individual rationality, budget feasibility, computational efficiency, low storage overhead, differential privacy guarantee, and aggregation stability. Extensive experiments on two public datasets demonstrate that IMFR consistently achieves superior free-rider detection accuracy, incentive effectiveness, and aggregation performance compared with existing methods.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems

papers.title: Hybrid Fog-Cloud Framework for QoS-Aware Offloading Through Deep Learning-Guided Convex Optimization and Federated Task Splitting Across Collaborative Nodes
papers.abstract: Dynamic fog-cloud task offloading requires coordinated decisions under time-varying workload, resource, energy, and network conditions. Existing approaches do not adequately couple future workload/Quality of Service (QoS) prediction with constraint-feasible allocation, adaptive policy refinement, and collaborative workload redistribution. To address this gap, this paper proposes Structured Predictive Energy-Constrained Convex Optimization (SPEC-CO)-Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), which integrates predictive workload/QoS estimation, prediction-conditioned convex allocation, DRL-based policy refinement, and collaborative fog-node federation. The framework is evaluated using the Intel Berkeley, Edge-Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), and National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) Solar datasets in a simulated fog-cloud environment comprising 20 fog nodes, 2 cloud servers, and 100 IoT devices over 1000 Monte Carlo runs. Across the evaluated scenarios, SPEC-CO-DRL achieves 12.8-25.1 ms latency, 93.4-98.5% task completion, 27.8-42.3 J/task energy consumption, 75.2-85.7% renewable-energy utilization, and 85.4-92.5% federation efficiency. Relative to the evaluated baselines, it reduces latency by up to 35.4%, energy consumption by 33.8%, and the reported privacy metric by 74.4%. These results demonstrate that explicit coupling of prediction, feasible optimization, adaptive refinement, and collaborative redistribution improves QoS-aware offloading under dynamic fog-cloud conditions.

papers.title: Federated Multi-omic Cancer Subtyping with Low-dimensional Feature Perception
papers.abstract: Multi-omic cancer subtyping clusters tumors according to their molecular characteristics and clinical manifestations, serving as the basis for personalized diagnosis and treatment. However, existing federated subtyping models face two critical challenges: (1) they neglect intrinsic relationships among low-dimensional features, and (2) they construct sample similarities directly from these unpurified features, yielding unreliable representations. To tackle these problems, a model named Federated Multi-omic Cancer Subtyping with Low-dimensional Feature Perception (FMCSLFP) is proposed. Specifically, high-dimensional multi-omic data is projected into a low-dimensional space for feature-wise self-representation learning. Furthermore, the ℓ2,1-norm and an orthogonality constraint are applied to the feature self-representation matrices to uncover relationships among low-dimensional features and enhance their representational capacity. Subsequently, the enhanced low-dimensional representations are utilized for sample-wise self-representation learning to generate similarity matrices, which are then stacked into a third-order tensor to explore high-order and low-rank information within the multi-omic data. An optimization algorithm based on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) is designed to solve the proposed FMCSLFP, effectively preserving data privacy by exchanging only model updates rather than raw multi-omic data across distributed devices. Extensive experiments are conducted on six cancer datasets, validating the model’s effectiveness for cancer subtyping.

papers.title: A Pseudo-online Fine-grained Metadata Workload Prediction Scheme for Internet of Things
papers.abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) represents a sophisticated architectural framework that seamlessly connects physical devices via the internet. Leveraging artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies, this framework achieves deep coupling and intelligent synergy among physical devices, digital information flows, and network connectivity.Therefore, workload balancing between nodes in the IoT is crucial to system performance. Here, we introduce a pseudo-online fine-grained meta-computing workload prediction scheme (PERO) for IoT. The scheme first removes workload data noise produced by competitive work in distributed systems through a parallel denoising module, thereby enhancing prediction effectiveness. It then constructs Multi-node Federated Samples with global workload characteristics and designs an MFS layer in the Transformer to effectively drive the training of the prediction model. Furthermore, the scheme employs a historical experience review method to compare model training parameters, significantly reducing model training time. Finally, the significant effect of the imbalance judgment module provides new possibilities for metadata workload balancing in distributed systems in the future. The experiments on three real datasets show that PERO outperforms the baseline methods by at least 19.41% and 30.24% in terms of MAE and MSE metrics respectively. Additionally, PERO also outperforms more advanced metadata workload balancing methods in terms of workload imbalance judgment.

papers.title: Service-Oriented Secure Federated Learning via Blockchain Orchestration and Byzantine-Resilient Consensus
A Distributed Acoustic Measurement and Diagnosis System of Wind Turbine Blades
papers.abstract: Acoustic diagnosis of wind turbine blades (WTBs) relies on measurements acquired by distributed sensing nodes under varying environmental and operating conditions. Such variations may contribute to differences in acoustic data distributions across wind farms. Centralized training requires transferring raw acoustic data from multiple wind farms to a central server, incurring communication overhead. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a distributed acoustic measurement and diagnosis system for WTBs. The proposed system integrates non-contact sensing, local signal processing, and federated learning while maintaining raw acoustic data locally. FedReP (Federated Representation and Personalization Learning) is the federated diagnosis module, where client-specific prompts provide local adaptation and prototype anchoring regularizes shared fault representation learning across wind farms. A stage-specific optimization strategy assigns different objectives to prompt adaptation and backbone refinement under heterogeneous sensing conditions. For edge-side deployment, a compact acoustic encoder, PRePNet, extracts non-stationary time-frequency features with low computational complexity. Experiments on field-collected multi-farm acoustic datasets and a public laboratory dataset show competitive diagnostic performance among representative federated baselines. On-device evaluation on NVIDIA Jetson TX2 NX further reports a local preprocessing to classification latency of 25.744 ± 1.726 ms per 2 s window under the tested configuration.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement

papers.title: Federated Multi-Agent DRL for Active RIS-Assisted Secure Beamforming in Cognitive Satellite-Terrestrial ISAC Systems
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a secure beamforming scheme for a cognitive satellite-terrestrial integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) network assisted by an active recon figurable intelligent surface (RIS). In this system, the active RIS is deployed to assist the terrestrial base station (BS) in suppressing cross-tier interference and enhancing the secrecy rate of primary users against potential eavesdroppers. We formulate a joint optimization problem to maximize the radar output signal to-noise ratio by jointly designing the transmit beamforming at the satellite and BS, and the active RIS reflection coefficients, subject to constraints on secrecy rate, quality of service, and power budgets. To address the non-convexity and high complexity of this collaborative beamforming problem, we propose a federated multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (FMA-DRL) framework. Specifically, a federated deep deterministic policy gradient (F-DDPG) algorithm is developed, where the satellite and BS act as independent agents to cooperatively learn the optimal policy in a distributed manner. Moreover, this algorithm supports continuous action spaces, where agents only transmit action information and shared backbone parameters during cooperative training instead of raw local channel data. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed active RIS assisted scheme significantly outperforms the passive RIS benchmark in terms of both secure transmission and sensing capabilities within the cognitive satellite-terrestrial network.

papers.title: Semantic-Aware Multi-LoRA Orchestration in Edge Federation: Hierarchical Multi-Timescale Optimization Under QoE Constraints
papers.abstract: The rapid scaling of Large Language Models (LLMs) has driven the adoption of Multi-LoRA as a lightweight mechanism for model customization. However, deploying Multi-LoRA in edge federations introduces significant challenges in operational expenditure (OPEX) and latency efficiency. In this paper, we introduce a semantic-aware Multi-LoRA serving framework for edge federations that jointly optimizes OPEX and Quality of Experience (QoE). Specifically, we propose a semantic compatibility model based on behavioral embeddings to enable high-fidelity LoRA substitution, thereby reducing cold-start latency and redundant cross-region data transfers. We further develop a hierarchical multi-timescale architecture that separates long-term model provisioning from real-time request dispatching, allowing the system to adapt to dynamic workload skewness under data sovereignty constraints. Additionally, we design a Lyapunov-based dynamic dispatching algorithm to jointly optimize cross-cluster routing, node auto-scaling, and VRAM execution modes in real time. Extensive discrete-event simulations based on real-world Microsoft Azure Functions traces demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly mitigates the batch-squeezing effect and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in steady-state throughput, long-term OPEX reduction, and 95th-percentile Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) Service Level Objective (SLO) compliance.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: Spatially Aware Lightweight GNN Imputation for Distributed Solid Waste Treatment Process
papers.abstract: The large amount of heterogeneous data poses challenges to the imputation of data from the solid waste treatment. The popular imputation models like RNNs and Transformers ignore the heterogeneity among sensor data. To address the interaction effects among heterogeneous sensor data, a spatially aware lightweight GNN imputation method (SALG) is proposed. First, a lightweight temporal embedding method is designed to recognize complex multilevel dependencies using multilayer linear embedding modules. Second, a spatial conditional attention mechanism is developed to model nested-derived heterogeneous information by leveraging nested-derived edge vectors. The spatial conditional attention method captures heterogeneous spatio-temporal features. Third, a parallel spatio-temporal heterogeneity-aware prototype federated learning method is designed, employing spatio-temporal heterogeneity relationships as prototypes to parallel communications. The proposed SALG produces more accurate imputation results than the comparison methods on three benchmark datasets and two solid waste treatment datasets.

papers.title: A Trilevel Optimization Framework for Privacy Protection in Federated Learning of Takagi–Sugeno Fuzzy Models
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is increasingly been used for fuzzy systems given it allows interpretable and collaborative modeling across decentralized data environments. However, the inherently linear regression structure of Takagi–Sugeno (TS) fuzzy models makes their transmitted parameters or gradients in FL susceptible to inferring both antecedent and consequent components, thereby exposing sensitive information about the underlying client samples. Although defense strategies developed for general machine learning models exist, these methods often disrupt the fine-grained parameter structure that TS models rely on, leading to a substantial loss in predictive performance. For this reason, achieving a meaningful balance between privacy and utility when transmitting the parameters of TS models remains a central challenge in federated fuzzy learning. To address this issue, we developed a trilevel framework, to strengthen privacy when training TS fuzzy models in federated settings. The top level acts as an obfuscator, while the middle and bottom levels form a bilevel reconstruction attacker. In effect, this establishes an adversarial structure in which the obfuscator learns to counter a stable and realistic attack. By optimizing directly against the attacker's reconstruction risk, the framework learns perturbations that improve privacy without sacrificing the model's utility. Experiments conducted in both the standard multi-sample client setting and the challenging single-sample client setting show that the proposed framework yields substantially higher reconstruction errors for both the antecedent and consequent parameters. Additionally, the prediction performance is comparable to FedAvg, outperforming the representative federated defenses in terms of the overall balance between privacy and utility.

papers.title: Sec-UterUS-CLIP: A Privacy-Preserving Cloud-Edge Collaborative Learning Framework for Uterine Ultrasound Diagnostics in Consumer Electronics
papers.abstract: The proliferation of portable uterine ultrasound devices promises enhanced accessibility for women’s healthcare, yet intensifies critical challenges in data privacy, resource limitations, and data silos for artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diagnostics in consumer electronics. Traditional centralized learning is infeasible due to highly sensitive patient data and constrained edge device capabilities. This paper proposes Sec-UterUS-CLIP, a novel privacy-preserving cloud-edge collaborative learning framework for uterine ultrasound diagnostics. Sec-UterUS-CLIP integrates a semantic similarity-enhanced vision-language model UterUS-CLIP as the local learning backbone, which is initialized via cloud pre-training and refined through federated fine-tuning across decentralized consumer devices by exchanging only model parameters. Crucially, we introduce a noise-resilient alignment strategy that leverages semantic similarity constraints to counteract the utility loss caused by differential privacy (DP) noise injection. This approach enables robust client model updates under different privacy perturbation levels, heterogeneous client distributions, and varying federated deployment scales. Evaluated on the large-scale UterUS-11K dataset, Sec-UterUS-CLIP achieves performance comparable to centralized models, while enhancing privacy through a client-level privacy-preserving Gaussian perturbation mechanism. This work establishes a practical paradigm for secure, intelligent, and scalable AI integration into resource-constrained consumer healthcare devices.

papers.title: A Privacy-Enhanced Federated Learning Poisoning Defense Based on Critical Path Identification
papers.abstract: Federated learning is highly vulnerable to poisoning attacks, where malicious participants attempt to corrupt the global model. Developing an effective defense remains challenging due to three coupled issues: the fundamental conflict between preserving strict user privacy and inspecting updates for malicious behavior, the massive computational overhead introduced by cryptographic protection mechanisms, and the non-independent and identically distributed ( non-IID) nature of user data, which heavily blurs the line between benign statistical variations and genuine malicious deviations. To address these issues, we propose a privacy-enhanced poisoning defense framework that selectively identifies and rectifies malicious parameter manipulations at a fine-grained level, rather than blindly discarding entire user updates. By isolating the critical parameter paths associated with poisoning behaviors, the proposed framework preserves useful benign contributions and mitigates main-task performance degradation, particularly under highly heterogeneous non-IID settings. In addition, the framework adopts a lightweight privacy-preserving architecture that protects raw user parameters while avoiding prohibitive cryptographic overhead. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves strong poisoning defense capability and competitive main-task accuracy under adversarial non-IID environments. Cost analysis shows that the additional communication cost scales linearly with model size and the number of participating users, while the additional computation cost at each user scales linearly with model size.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Layerwise Federated Learning based on Joint Device Selection and Bandwidth Allocation
papers.abstract: This paper investigates communication-efficient layerwisefederated learning(FL) within resource-constrainededge intelligencenetworks. To facilitate effective layerwise FL in realworld scenarios, we consider the heterogeneities of CPU frequency, transmit power, time-varying channel states, and battery capacity of edge devices, and adopt a long-term perspective for the overall FL process. We formulate an optimization problem as amixed-integer nonlinear programmingproblem, aiming to minimize the overall learning latency associated with the layerwise FL process under per-device energy budget constraints. To solve this optimization problem, anonline optimization algorithm(OOA) based on Lyapunov theory is proposed, which realizes joint edge device selection and bandwidth allocation during the FL process. Furthermore, a detailed performance analysis of OOA is provided, demonstrating a trade-off between learning latency and energy deficit of the form [O(1/V) ,O(√V) ], whereVis a tunable hyper-parameter. Under the eight-device setting, simulation results demonstrate that applying OOA to layerwise FL reduces the overall learning latency and the overall energy deficit by an average of 7.14% and 67.73%, respectively, compared with layerwise FL under the original fixed uniform uploading schedule. Meanwhile, its overall learning latency remains only 2.03% higher than that of exhaustive search on average. The effectiveness of OOA is further verified when scaling up the number of edge devices and theconvolutional neural network(CNN) architecture.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking

papers.title: Digital Twin Enabled Capability- and Queue-Aware EMS Routing to Improve Time to Definitive Care
papers.abstract: Digital transformation in smart cities can enhance critical public services by using data from ubiquitous sensing and Internet of Things (IoT) sources. However, Emergency Medical Services routing often relies on static protocols or partial traffic data. This approach frequently ignores real-time hospital states such as equipment availability and Emergency Department crowding. Consequently, capability mismatches occur and lead to secondary transfers that compromise patient outcomes. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a “Digital Twin federation” architecture. This architecture integrates heterogeneous urban data streams into a unified decision-making framework. These streams include live traffic sensing, ambulance telemetry, and real-time hospital resource monitoring. The proposed system employs a rolling-horizon optimization controller. This controller uses the fused data to perform capability- and queue-aware routing without disrupting background traffic. We validated the framework on a calibrated scenario of Riyadh. The results show that exposing hospital-side IoT signals to the prehospital transport layer eliminates patient forwarding. It also significantly improves the Time to Definitive Care for critical cohorts like stroke and trauma. These findings highlight the potential of AI-driven data fusion in establishing resilient smart city healthcare infrastructure.

papers.title: Task Relevance-Driven Prompt Expansion for Federated Continual Learning
papers.abstract: Federated continual learning (FCL) has attracted considerable interest by enabling local clients to continually acquire knowledge from new tasks. However, most FCL methods assume that the global server has prior knowledge of the arrival times and number of categories for new tasks, which is unrealistic in the real world. Furthermore, they neglect the importance of positive inter-task semantic relationships when learning new tasks and are significantly affected by irrelevant relationships from old tasks, thereby exacerbating catastrophic forgetting. To resolve the above challenges, we develop a novelTaskRelevance-drivenPromptExpansion (TRPE) model. Specifically, to eliminate the reliance on prior knowledge of new tasks, we propose an out-of-distribution detector to identify the arrival of new tasks within local clients, along with a radius-adaptive DBSCAN to infer the quantity of categories in new tasks on the proxy server. Moreover, to explore positive inter-task relationships, we calculate the affinity between the original gradient for learning new task and its gradient orthogonal to the feature space of old tasks to evaluate semantic relevance between old and new tasks from a global perspective. Then, we use this global task relevance to determine the key-prompt pair for new tasks and identify highly related old tasks. After concatenating their prompts for training, we can leverage such positive inter-task relations to improve the continual learning of newly arriving tasks. To balance the learning of new tasks and the forgetting of old ones, a soft orthogonality constraint is applied to the local key and prompt gradients. Experiments spanning diverse datasets and backbones confirm the efficacy of our TRPE model.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

papers.title: FedGuard-XAI: An Explainable Federated Learning Framework with Adversarial Defense for IoMT-Enabled Multi-Continental Breast Cancer Detection
papers.abstract: We present FedGuard-XAI, a novel federated learning (FL) framework for Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) environments, combining Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture with SHAP-based explainability and gradient-based adversarial defense mechanisms for breast cancer detection. Our approach addresses the critical challenges of data privacy, model robustness, and clinical interpretability in cross-continental healthcare settings where sensitive medical imaging data must remain decentralized across distributed IoMT devices and institutional networks. We evaluated FedGuard-XAI using a private dataset of 8,220 mammograms from South Asian populations (collected from five tertiary hospitals in India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh) combined with public datasets including TCGA-BRCA (1,098 patients), CBIS-DDSM (2,620 cases), and INbreast (410 images). The FL framework incorporates a novel Differential Privacy-Preserving Attention Mechanism (DP-PAM) achieving 94.3% accuracy while maintaining ε = 2.1 privacy guarantee. Building on this privacy foundation, adversarial robustness was evaluated against FGSM, PGD, and C&W attacks, retaining 86.4% average accuracy across all attack settings (a 7.9 percentage-point degradation), compared with 51.5–71.0 points for baseline models. The framework’s explainability module identified candidate biomarkers in South Asian populations, suggesting distinct tissue density patterns that warrant further clinical validation, while enabling secure collaborative learning across geographically distributed IoMT healthcare systems without centralizing sensitive patient data. Clinical validation with radiologists across three experience levels demonstrated 7.4% diagnostic accuracy improvement and 31% reduction in evaluation time, establishing FedGuard-XAI as a practical solution for privacy-preserving, robust, and interpretable AI deployment in real-world IoMT-enabled healthcare environments.

papers.title: IRS and Client-Edge-Cloud Federated Learning Aided Intelligent Evaluation Algorithm for Internet of Things Covert Communication Performance Based on Gramba Neural Network
papers.abstract: The rapid development of the Internet of Things (IoT) and the open and broadcast nature of wireless links such as 5G/6G have made user privacy a critical issue. The complex and dynamic channel environments can degrade communication performance as well as covert transmission. Therefore, this paper proposes an intelligent evaluation algorithm for covert transmission and performance based on federated learning (FL) and a Gramba Neural Network. First, a covert communication model assisted by intelligent reconfigurable surface (IRS) and artificial noise (AN) is established considering N-Nakagami fading channels. IRS is employed to reshape the propagation environment, and AN is used to disrupt signal detection. This model employs hierarchical FL with client-edge-cloud layers to protect data privacy. Edge computing is employed to reduce cloud communication overhead while adapting to data heterogeneity. This also improves privacy protection and mitigates overfitting. The Gramba neural network employs SpatSAGE, which is a spatial domain multi-hop weighted graph convolutional network with hop-interaction, for local feature extraction. A graph-aware MambaMixer is used to improve modeling of long-range dependencies. It integrates a structure-aware attention mechanism to better capture complex topological structures. Two datasets based on covert throughput (CT) and detection error probability (DEP) are generated for performance evaluation. Simulation results are presented that demonstrate superior evaluation performance compared to the GraphSAGE, GraphMamba, GAT, Graphormer and Gramba models. FL-Gramba achieves mean squared error reductions of 17.3% and 16.9% over GraphMamba with the two datasets.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: A Two-Stage Federated Knowledge Distillation Framework for Vehicular Intrusion Detection
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of vehicular network technology, vehicles can obtain entertainment/safety information services through V2V and V2I communication. Vehicular intrusion detection systems (VIDSs) are essential for protecting vehicles against cyberattacks. Existing deep neural networkbased VIDSs have achieved better results in detecting malicious attack traffic. However, most systems rarely account for performance differences among vehicles, such as their computational and storage resources. In particular, the performance difference between older and the latest smart vehicles is more obvious. To accommodate vehicles with different performance levels, a twostage VIDS training framework based on federated knowledge distillation is proposed, which simultaneously produces two types of detection models: 1) a complex model and 2) a lightweight model. In the first stage, considering the distributed characteristics of the Internet of Vehicles, we designed a federated learning algorithm based on representative clients and learning quality to train complex models. This algorithm enhances the detection capability of complex models by selecting optimal model parameters. In the second stage, we design a progressive knowledge distillation algorithm that adaptively adjusts the distillation temperature to transfer detection knowledge from the complex model to lightweight models with lower resource requirements. Experiments on public datasets show that the proposed federated learning method improves the complex model's class-average accuracy, while progressive distillation enhances the detection performance of lightweight models.

papers.title: GRIDS: Generalized Representation-based Intrusion Detection System via Federated Contrastive Learning
papers.abstract: Existing AI-based intrusion detection systems are typically trained for specific network environments, leading to significant performance degradation when deployed in different settings or exposed to evolving attack strategies. We propose GRIDS (Generalized Representation-based Intrusion Detection System), a federated contrastive learning framework for cross-environment intrusion detection that keeps raw traffic data local. GRIDS employs a Transformer-based encoder trained with supervised contrastive learning across distributed network environments, learning a shared representation without exchanging sensitive traffic data. The encoder embeds network flow features into a latent space where semantically similar traffic patterns cluster together, enabling effective anomaly detection via k-nearest neighbor scoring. Evaluated on four heterogeneous NetFlow datasets, GRIDS outperforms existing federated IDS baselines on average with a single unified model. In leave-one-out cross-validation, a substantial portion of the detection capability of GRIDS transfers to network environments unseen during training, and the level of transfer varies across target networks. Deployment at such a network requires no labeled attack data or fine-tuning. It uses the benign traffic of the network as the kNN reference set and its unlabeled traffic for normalization and threshold calibration. The framework targets deployments in which a single model protects multiple heterogeneous networks.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: CRLB-Constrained Resource Allocation for Federated Edge Learning in Internet of Vehicles Via Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Federated edge learning (FEL) has significant advantages in terms of protecting user privacy and reducing communication overhead in vehicular networks. Improving learning accuracy and minimizing communication overhead by adjusting resource allocation strategies is the research focus of FEL. Although FEL helps enhance privacy through data encryption, information leakage caused by localization errors remains a challenging problem. To address this issue, we utilize the Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) to calculate the vehicle localization errors, filter out vehicles that meet the localization accuracy requirements, and then select vehicles from them to participate in FEL. Furthermore, a joint optimization problem for dynamic resource allocation is proposed, in order to balance the learning accuracy and communication overhead. The optimization problem is formulated as a Markov decision process (MDP). To solve such MDP, we adopt a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based approach and propose a novel CRLB-based FEL algorithm, i.e., FC-TD3,which structurally integrates a reliability-filtering mechanism into the twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) framework. By employing this mechanism, the algorithm dynamically constructs a high-confidence candidate pool to select vehicles that meet localization accuracy requirements, thereby ensuring that only reliable agents participate in the FEL process. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional algorithms in dealing with such problems. Finally, we conduct simulations to validate the performance of the algorithm and clarify the impact of different parameters on system performance through numerical analysis.

papers.title: Beyond Similarity: Task-Geometric Filtering for Byzantine-Robust Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) trains a shared model across distributed clients without centralizing their data. Its open participation exposes aggregation to model-poisoning and Byzantine attacks, so the server must admit only updates that advance the shared objective. Existing defenses rely on protocol level authentication or statistical robustness. Neither evaluates whether an admitted update moves the global model along the task-induced descent direction. Under non-IID data and partial participation, authenticated and statistically plausible updates can jointly push training off task. We introduce SATF (Selective Admission via Task-directional Filtering), a server-side admission mechanism. SATF ranks updates by their directional alignment with a round-wise reference direction and applies an interquartile-range gate on update magnitudes. It needs no trusted dataset and does not use the Byzantine fraction as an algorithmic input. We bound the adversarial perturbation of the reference direction and give a worst-case benign-majority bound for the retained set, extended to the accepted set under a stated gate condition. We derive a one-step descent bound and a sublinear multi-round convergence rate up to an explicit Byzantine-dependent bias term, and we characterize the scaling detection threshold of the magnitude gate. On Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 with one hundred clients and three random seeds, against FedAvg, Trimmed Mean, FLAME-Clip, FLTrust, and Multi-Krum, SATF, at moderate heterogeneity, attains the highest mean accuracy under strong-replacement attacks on CIFAR-10 and stays within two points of the best method under strong replacement on Fashion-MNIST and under mixed attacks on both datasets. We also report its limitations under high heterogeneity and scaling attacks.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: PFL-LLMGR: Semantic-Guided Multi-Level Graph Refinement for Hierarchical Personalized Federated Learning in Consumer Electronics
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of consumer electronics (CE) systems introduces significant challenges for Federated Learning (FL), particularly in managing device heterogeneity, ensuring data privacy, and achieving personalized model adaptation. However, existing FL methods often struggle to adequately capture complex multi-level relationships or effectively balance global knowledge sharing with nuanced local adaptation, particularly with heterogeneous consumer devices and user-specific service contexts. In this paper, we propose a Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) framework with Large Language Model (LLM)-Guided Graph Representation, named PFL-LLMGR, to model intricate cross-device semantic relationships, facilitate multilevel collaboration, and achieve refined personalization without sharing raw data in an end-edge-cloud architecture. Specifically, an LLM is incorporated to analyze lightweight device metadata on the cloud, so as to guide global graph pruning and node fusion while capturing deeper semantic relationships. A local subgraph construction scheme based on multi-source information fusion is then introduced on the edge, and an edge-deployed Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) is trained to fuse features within these subgraphs, generating enhanced representations distributed back to clients. Furthermore, local models are decomposed into feature extractors that participate in edge aggregation and personalized classifiers that remain on clients. An alternating training scheme is developed to synchronize local model training based on edge-fused features while GCN parameters are fixed, and update the edge GCN using client-side feedback while local parameters are fixed, effectively balancing shared knowledge and local adaptation. Experiments on CIFAR-10, DIGIT, and the CE-oriented Office-Home benchmark demonstrate that PFL-LLMGR achieves consistently competitive and often superior accuracy under label heterogeneity, domain shift, and varying client scales, with an improvement of up to 2.65 percentage points over the strongest baseline on Office-Home withK= 50, offering valuable insights for advanced FL in consumer electronics systems, especially in enhancing collaborative intelligence and personalization.

papers.title: PAFL: Privacy-Awareness and Adversarial-Resilient Federated Learning for IoVs
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) allows collaborative training with local gradients uploaded by clients instead of sharing their raw data. For scenarios like the Internet of Vehicles (IoVs) where large volumes of sensitive driving data are generated, cryptography techniques are leveraged to encrypt or mask the local gradients. However, these privacy-preserving approaches are vulnerable to poisoning attacks, as it is difficult to detect malicious gradients within the ciphertext. Potential poisoning attacks in IoVs can significantly impact the accuracy and performance of the system. To combat this issue, we propose PAFL, a privacy-awareness and adversarial-resilient FL model. At the heart of our method is an aggregation mechanism delicately designed to protect private data while being robust against poisoning attacks. During the aggregation process, self mask and gradient mask are devised on the original gradient to prevent privacy leakage. Furthermore, an evaluation mechanism is implemented to identify and filter out malicious vehicles from subsequent model updates, ultimately defending against poisoning attacks. Our model suits the characteristics of IoVs, reducing the communication overhead from$O(n^{2})$to approximately$O(nlogn)$, while effectively mitigating poisoning attacks and safeguarding privacy. Experiments have validated the effectiveness and feasibility of PAFL in large-scale IoVs, which outperforms the state-of-the-art methods by reducing the aggregation time by nearly 8 times.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: Federated Machine Unlearning with Deletion Scheduling in Cell-Free C-V2X Networks
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving traffic perception in roadside unit (RSU)-assisted cellular vehicle-to-everything (C-V2X) networks, but vehicle deletion requires removing both historical model influence and subsequent communication participation. In cell-free C-V2X, deletion further affects aggregation, RSU association, vehicle-to-RSU (V2R) transmission, and energy accounting. We propose traffic context-directed Fisher corrective unlearning (TC-FCU), which uses a diagonal empirical-Fisher preconditioner and momentum-stabilized updates for low-cost corrective retraining with traffic-context-adaptive correction. We further formulate machine unlearning (MU) execution as deletion scheduling under deadline and processing-capacity constraints, jointly considering pre-deletion resource consumption, corrective unlearning cost, and the marginal network-side energy change of the remaining vehicles. We analyze the Fisher–Hessian relation under explicit assumptions, local descent, and deletion-cost monotonicity. Simulations show that TC-FCU approaches full-retraining forgetting quality with much lower runtime, while Proposed Timing reduces normalized cost over benchmark scheduling schemes.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Adaptive Clustered Personalized Federated Learning With Knowledge Distillation for IoV
papers.abstract: Statistical heterogeneity in 6 G Internet of Vehicles (IoV) networks severely limits standard federated learning paradigms, leading to significant weight divergence and suboptimal personalization. We proposed ACPFL-KD, an adaptive clustering personalized federated learning framework that synthesizes dynamic topology reconstruction with data-free, duallayer knowledge distillation. Diverging from static clustering regimes and conventional federated distillation, our Affinity Propagation strategy leverages lightweight feature representations and a theoretically grounded, regularized similarity metric to autonomously restructure the network topology without predefined cluster constraints, even with sparse client participation. We devise a synergistic dual-layer knowledge-sharing architecture to stabilize convergence. At the intra-cluster level, coordinatewise median aggregation yields robust teacher models that guide clients in extracting group consensus; simultaneously, an inter-cluster adaptive regularization strategy fuses heterogeneous knowledge increments to effectively bridge information silos. Experiments on five datasets, including the real-world autonomous driving dataset BDD100 K, together with rigorous theoretical convergence analysis, validate this framework. In highly non- IID settings, ACPFL-KD consistently outperforms state-of-theart personalization and distillation baselines (e.g., Fed-DFA, FedPer), achieving superior classification accuracy, particularly in complex mobility scenarios. Furthermore, it maintains this lead while demonstrating accelerated convergence and drastically reducing central communication bandwidth overhead compared to current baselines. Future work will explore cross-domain adaptation to further enhance scalability in dynamic, real-world deployments.

papers.title: Multi-agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Scheme for On-Demand Federated Learning
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

papers.title: FedVPC: Softening Parameters Via Hierarchical Pyramid for Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Personalized federated learning (PFL) addresses statistical heterogeneity by adapting models to individual clients, but its utility can degrade substantially under client-level differential privacy (DP). Two major causes are rigid parameter partitioning and isotropic update clipping, which overlook the continuous importance distribution and distinct optimization roles of model parameters. We propose FedVPC, a privacy-preserving PFL framework consisting of two complementary components. First, the Variable Hierarchical Pyramid (VHP) uses an empirical diagonal Fisher proxy to softly stratify parameters into personalized, bridging, and globally aligned groups. Second, the Parameter-Customized Constraint (PCC) applies group-aware regularization before client-level clipping and Gaussian perturbation to reduce optimization distortion. We establish a client-level DP guarantee through update clipping, distributed Gaussian perturbation, and RDP accounting, while secure aggregation restricts the server to aggregate-only observation. We also characterize convergence under heterogeneous data. Experiments on five datasets show that FedVPC consistently outperforms representative DP-FL and DP-PFL baselines, with improvements of up to 7.66 percentage points across the evaluated settings. FedVPC also demonstrates robustness to data heterogeneity, client scale, and model architecture while showing empirical resistance to gradient inversion under the evaluated diagnostic setting.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: FedAED: Federated Aggregation with Editing Direction Alignment
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed devices without exposing raw data, thus ensuring privacy compliance. However, data heterogeneity among participants introduces significant challenges for effective federated optimization. While prior research has attempted to address this issue typically by regularizing local updates or fine-tuning the global model, the aggregation weights in most FL frameworks are still determined solely by dataset size. This simplistic strategy may hinder convergence and limit overall model effectiveness, highlighting the ongoing need for adaptive and secure aggregation methods. This paper proposes FedAED, a novel FL framework that Adaptively adjusts aggregation weights through Editing Directions derived from client model updates. The editing direction vector encodes the semantic trajectory of local model updates, effectively capturing the underlying data heterogeneity across clients. This approach enables more accurate aggregation that is well aligned with global optimization goals, preserves privacy, and requires no auxiliary data. As a result, FedAED enhances both the stability and generalization ability of the global model. Comprehensive experimental results confirm that our approach consistently surpasses strong baselines and significantly improves the effectiveness of FL under heterogeneous environments.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology

papers.title: Dynamic Federated Learning With Tensor-Based Aggregation and Latent-Attention Modeling for Anomaly Detection in IIoT
papers.abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) anomaly detection faces significant challenges due to dynamic network topologies, non-IID data distributions, high-dimensional multi-modal features, and privacy preservation. Conventional federated learning (FL) approaches suffer from high communication overhead, poor adaptation to concept drift, and difficulty in preserving cross-modal correlations. To address these limitations, we propose a dynamic federated learning (DFL) framework that integrates attention-based generative anomaly detection with tensorized aggregation. Client-side multi-modal statistics, including detection losses, KL divergence, attention distributions, PCA features, and metadata, are unified into a six-mode tensor on the server, which is incrementally updated via incremental tensor-train decomposition (ITTD). This enables efficient updates, preserves structural correlations across modalities, and provides explicit monitoring of drift through rank variation and reconstruction error. A hard-soft coupled decision mechanism further selects and weights client updates by combining adaptive thresholding, latent-space clustering, and variance-aware weighting. Experimental results demonstrate that on the IoT-23 dataset, our method achieves an F1 score of 95.89% with a reduced false positive rate (FPR) of 1.58%, while on the SECOM manufacturing dataset it attains 95.02% F1 with 2.04% FPR under the full tensorized DFL setting. Moreover, the proposed DFL with tensor aggregation reduces communication overhead compared with baseline FL methods, indicating its potential to enable scalable, privacy-preserving anomaly detection in dynamic IIoT environments.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Strict Partitioning for Real-Time Configurable Non-Preemptive Gang Tasks
papers.abstract: Gang scheduling is becoming increasingly important in real-time AI and accelerator-driven systems, where work-loads execute in parallel on multiple processing units. Motivated by real-time DNN inference workloads with parallelism-dependent execution times, this paper introduces configurable non-preemptive gang (cNPG) tasks as an abstraction that captures their key execution characteristics. It proposes a strict partitioning framework for scheduling real-time cNPG tasks that jointly determines task parallelism levels, processor partitions, and task assignments. By enforcing a uniform parallelism level within each partition, the framework eliminates cross-partition interference and enables schedulability analysis using well-understood uniprocessor techniques. To solve the resulting offline design problem, this paper introduces Pruned Adaptive Beam Search (PABS), a search-based heuristic that explores partitioning and parallelism assignments while pruning unpromising partial solutions. Evaluations with large-scale synthetic workloads and real-world Edge TPU benchmarks show that the proposed method achieves a higher schedulability ratio than the state-of-the-art global and federated gang scheduling techniques, as well as a previous strict partitioning heuristic.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

papers.title: Robust Federated Unlearning in Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks: Joint Model Splitting and Resource Allocation
papers.abstract: The space-air-ground integrated network (SAGIN) is expected to support ubiquitous edge intelligence in sixth-generation (6G) mobile networks, where federated learning (FL) can exploit distributed data without exposing raw samples. In SAGIN, resource-constrained ground devices and heterogeneous wireless links make synchronous FL vulnerable to stragglers, which may cause excessive training delay. A naive attempt to reduce this delay by excluding straggling devices can introduce distribution drift under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data, especially when these devices contain rare or complementary samples. To address these coupled latency and robustness issues, this paper proposes a hierarchical split federated learning (HSFL) framework for SAGIN. In this framework, ground devices execute shallow model layers, Autonomous Aerial Vehicles (AAVs) process the remaining layers and perform edge aggregation, and low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites conduct satellite-level aggregation. We derive a convergence upper bound to capture the effects of split layer selection, user association, and data distribution on convergence. A joint optimization problem is formulated to minimize training delay by optimizing split layer selection, device-AAV association, AAV-LEO association, and communication and computing resource allocation. To solve this mixed-integer nonlinear problem, we first design a tabu-assisted block coordinate descent (TA-BCD) algorithm that alternately updates topology association, resource allocation, and split layer selection. We further develop a robust device-admission extension of TA-BCD (RDA-TA-BCD), which jointly optimizes device admission, topology association, and resource scheduling and incorporates federated unlearning to approximately remove the historical model influence of excluded devices. The resulting scheduler protects data-critical bottleneck devices while removing redundant ones, thereby balancing delay reduction with model robustness. Simulation results on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 show that the proposed algorithms reduce training delay while maintaining model accuracy under heterogeneous SAGIN and non-IID data settings.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: PVFUnlearn: Privacy-Preserving and Verifiable Data Circulation for Edge-Assisted Federated Unlearning
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose PVFUnlearn, a privacypreserving and verifiable data circulation framework for edge assisted federated unlearning in hierarchical federated learning systems. Particularly, local model updates are decomposed into sign and magnitude vectors, where additive homomorphic encryption is applied to the magnitude vectors to achieve efficient secure aggregation with reduced cryptographic overhead. To support efficient federated unlearning, edge-level and serverlevel calibration mechanisms are designed in the way that reconstructs calibrated model updates without requiring the participation of clients under non-unlearning edge servers, thereby avoiding expensive retraining from scratch. In addition, homomorphic commitments are integrated into both aggregation and unlearning processes to guarantee aggregation correctness and unlearning verifiability. Extensive experiments conducted on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 datasets demonstrate that PVFUnlearn achieves forgetting performance close to retraining-based federated unlearning while significantly reducing computational and communication overhead. The results further show that PVFUnlearn effectively maintains model utility and provides strong auditability for secure and trustworthy data circulation in edge-assisted federated unlearning systems.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

papers.title: SplitKD: Enhancing Generalization and Straggler Resistance of Federated Learning via Parameter Split and Distillation
papers.abstract: Federated learning can achieve collaborative training while protecting user privacy and data security, but differences in the performance of participating devices and the diversity of data distributions pose core challenges: 1) highly heterogeneous data reduce the generalization ability of the model; 2) “straggler” clients with limited capabilities or slow responses can significantly affect the system's training stability. However, existing research still cannot collaboratively address these dual issues within a unified framework, resulting in a trade-off between model generalization and system robustness. To tackle these issues, we propose SplitKD, which enhances the model's generalization to data heterogeneity and stability for straggler clients through parameter splitting and freezing, adaptive knowledge distillation, and differentially weighted aggregation. Specifically, SplitKD finely regulates the knowledge transfer from the global model to the local model through parameter splitting and an adaptive knowledge distillation mechanism, enhancing the generalization ability of the model. For straggler clients, we have designed a parameter-splitting-based differentially weighted aggregation strategy that distinguishes model differences by parameters and simultaneously aggregates their local knowledge, enhancing the robustness and compatibility of the global model. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the convergence of SplitKD, and experimental results show that, compared with 12 existing methods, SplitKD effectively mitigates the impact of stragglers on model performance and enhances model generalization.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

papers.title: Adaptive Federated Class-Incremental Learning for Privacy-Preserving Edge Intelligence
papers.abstract: Driven by the advancement of Agentic AI, the deployment of autonomous edge agents in safety-critical systems has introduced stringent requirements for privacy-preserving and adaptive intelligence over dynamic and heterogeneous data streams. While Federated Learning (FL) addresses the privacy constraint through collaborative training without sharing raw data, it struggles with the continuously evolving edge data perceived by autonomous agents. To bridge this gap, Federated Continual Learning (FCL) extends the FL paradigm to enable Agentic AI models to incrementally adapt to new tasks and non-stationary distributions, without compromising data privacy. Despite its potential, FCL faces significant challenges in balancing local personalization and global knowledge consolidation, particularly under heterogeneous and imbalanced class distributions across edge agents. Overcoming this dual challenge is critical to robust, adaptive and trustworthy Agentic AI applications at the network edge. In this work, we propose Meta Representation-based Adaptive Personalized Federated Class Incremental Learning (Meta-APFCIL) to tackle these limitations. Each edge agent first performs adaptive meta-training of a shared representation network using its respective exemplar memory within the FL framework. The resulting global representation is then personalized through fine-tuning on each FCL client's current task data and exemplar memory, guided by class-wise logit adjustment to effectively mitigate the bias introduced by class imbalance between current tasks and stored exemplars. As a result, this approach alleviates catastrophic forgetting, enhancing the model's adaptability and retention of previously learned knowledge. Experimental results demonstrate that Meta-APFCIL outperforms key baseline algorithms, achieving an average task accuracy improvement of 23.79% to 32.62% under varying levels of task similarity among clients' data streams. Additionally, it exhibits the lowest task forgetting ratio and the highest generalization capability among FCL clients, enabling trustworthy and adaptive Agentic AI deployment in edge networks.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Energy-Aware Air-Ground Covert Federated Learning for Terrestrial Devices
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) can preserve privacy, but it is limited by the coverage of static edge servers and vulnerable to security risks due to the frequent exchange of model parameters. To address these issues, we establish an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted covert FL framework to protect the transmission of local models from detection by an aerial warden. Acting as a flying server, the UAV aggregates local models from distributed ground devices to improve transmission efficiency. We aim to minimize the energy consumption of terrestrial devices in the presence of a severe security threat to the FL, where the warden adopts the minimum error detection probability. To meet the requirements of energy-sensitive applications, the UAV trajectory, transmission power, local accuracy, model upload time, and local computation capacity are jointly optimized. We decompose the optimization problem into three subproblems, and a low-complexity algorithm is developed. Specifically, for a given UAV trajectory, we derive the closed-form solutions for other variables to reduce the computational complexity. The UAV trajectory is then optimized using successive convex approximation. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed UAV-assisted covert FL scheme in minimizing the energy consumption while guaranteeing the secrecy.

papers.title: Semantic-Aware Digital Twin for the Internet-of-Maritime Things: A GAT-Enhanced Multi-Agent DRL Framework
papers.abstract: Search and rescue (SAR) operations faces many critical challenges due to high-bandwidth sensing, dynamic ocean environments, and strict energy and communication constraints that are encountered in maritime environments. Efficient coordination of Internet-of-Maritime Things (IoMT) devices, especially for guaranteeing the safety of maritime users, is therefore of extreme importance. Traditional approaches treat semantic communication, digital twins, and decentralized control separately, missing opportunities for integrated optimization. In this paper, we propose a semantic-aware digital twin (SemaDT-RL), a unified framework that incorporates variational semantic federated learning, a predictive digital twin, and multi-agent deep reinforcement learning with graph attention networks (MADRL-GAT) for resilient IoMT-driven SAR. The semantic layer compresses sensor data into lightweight anomaly-aware descriptors, drastically reducing bandwidth without sacrificing survivor detection. The predictive digital twin layer assimilates semantic updates using an extended Kalman filter to estimate survivor and node states and generate predictive guidance for survivor tracking and node energy-aware coordination. The MADRL-GAT control layer leverages these forecasts to optimize each node's trajectory, processing, and transmission decisions under mobility, energy, and communication constraints. Extensive simulations demonstrate that SemaDT-RL achieves faster survivor detection, lower communication overhead, and superior energy efficiency compared to baseline methods, demonstrating its effectiveness under the evaluated maritime SAR configuration.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Proxy-Guided Online Adaptation of OWA Aggregation in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning ensures data privacy but its effectiveness may be compromised under non-IID heterogeneity, which motivates adaptive server-side aggregation. However OWA, despite its rank-based coordinate-wise flexibility, is difficult to deploy because selecting effective weights is non-trivial and fixed profiles may not match round-to-round changes in client update distributions. This paper proposes an online and lightweight adaptation strategy for OWA weights, parameterized by a single temperature variable that generates a smooth, monotonically decreasing weight vector. At each communication round, the server evaluates a small set of candidate temperatures using a held-out proxy set and selects the one that minimizes proxy loss, with exponential smoothing to stabilize the temperature over time. Experiments conducted on 10 classification benchmark datasets under non-IID partitions show that the proposed adaptive variant achieves statistically significant improvements over all considered reference methods at the global level. Aggregated across datasets, FedOWA Adapt improves mean accuracy by approximately 3.3 percentage points over FedAvg and 1.9 percentage points over fixed-weight FedOWA. In terms of log-loss, the proposed method reduces the mean loss by about 0.12 compared with FedAvg and by about 0.15 compared with fixed-weight FedOWA, indicating improved predictive reliability in addition to higher accuracy. The largest dataset-level gains are particularly visible on selected benchmarks, reaching approximately 13.5 percentage points over FedAvg and up to about 7.8 percentage points over fixed-weight FedOWA. Furthermore, a detailed one-factor-at-a-time sensitivity analysis and an ablation study were performed, confirming the robustness of the proposed configuration and showing that the main source of improvement is the repeated round-wise adaptation of the OWA aggregation profile rather than a single fixed or one-shot selected weighting scheme.

papers.title: Trustworthy GPS Spoofing Detection in CAVs Using Logistic Regression Enhanced by Federated Learning and Digital Twins
papers.abstract: Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) are vulnerable to Global Positioning System (GPS) spoofing attacks that threaten navigation integrity. Existing detection approaches face challenges in privacy, computational efficiency, and class imbalance. We propose three progressive frameworks: 1) a lightweight standalone Logistic Regression (LR) model achieving 95.52% accuracy; 2) Federated Learning with LR (FL+LR), which enables collaborative training across CAVs while keeping raw data local and achieves 97.25% accuracy; 3) a Digital Twin-enhanced framework (DT+FL+LR), which integrates simulated spoofing scenarios and DT-based consistency checking and achieves 97.46% accuracy. Evaluation on AVG-Dataset-1 (62,042 samples) shows that DT+FL+LR achieves 90.00% spoofed-class recall and 100.00% precision. The computational analysis indicates potential edge deployment suitability for standalone LR under the evaluated configuration, while FL variants provide improved data locality with competitive performance. Across the evaluated configurations, the AUC increases from 95.02% to 98.10%, indicating improved discrimination capability and potential deployment feasibility under the considered experimental configuration.
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering

papers.title: Multi-Objective Offloading Optimization in MEC and Vehicular-Fog Federated Systems With Vehicle Mobility Using PSO-TD3 Hybrid Algorithm
papers.abstract: Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) and Vehicular-Fogs (VFs) are placed nearer to user equipment (UE), reducing propagation latency compared to traditional cloud-based systems and ensuring a high standard of Quality of Service (QoS). Nevertheless, MEC sites can become congested and overloaded during peak traffic periods, such as concerts or sporting events. To address this, offloading techniques can shift intensive computational tasks from devices with limited resources to those with greater capacity, enhancing task performance and thereby increasing battery longevity. This study investigates the offloading within a two-tier framework of MEC and VF, focusing on the offloading of MEC to VF. Maintaining QoS is challenging due to the instability of fog networks caused by high-speed vehicle movement, which disrupts both vehicle-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-infrastructure communications. To mitigate this, we analyze vehicle mobility using a Gauss-Markov Mobility (GMM) model. Our main goal is to reduce the normalized system cost by optimizing both latency and energy consumption while accounting for vehicle mobility. We approach this challenge as a multi-objective optimization problem and develop a reinforcement learning environment. Additionally, we propose an algorithm based on imitation learning called Hybrid PSO-TD3, an enhancement of the TD3 algorithm, to effectively manage these complexities.

papers.title: AegisFed: A Reliable and Efficient Multi-Binding Key Secure Aggregation Scheme for Federated Learning Against a Malicious Cloud Server
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without sharing raw data, yet model updates may still leak sensitive information. Multi-key homomorphic encryption (MKHE) can protect updates of clients, but existing works still suffer from complex key management, costly dropout handling, and reliance on an honest-but-curious cloud server. Verifiable MPC-based schemes verify the aggregated client set but incur high communication overhead.
